We waited for about 30 minutes from the time in line until receiving our $30 rib tip bucket, (that serves 4) and our departure.

A small order of fries came with the tip bucket. No bread. No coleslaw. The rib tips at the top were pretty dry. But midway and to the bottom, tips were emersed in a liquidy, highly vinegary thin sauce. The sauce tasted more of vinegar than barbecue sauce. So much so, that the inside of my lips were wrinkly as if I had just eaten 3 large sour pickles.

The tips them selves were just ok. About 60% meat, 30% bone and 10% burnt gristle.

Fries were dry, average and limp.

Between the wait, cramped space, difficult parking which threatens a tow if you park in the alley, unsafe area, overly vinegar sauce, mediocre rib tip flavor and the lady cursing audibly on the phone, in front of customers, behind the counter, we probably won't be back. The food here simply isn't worth it.

Good, inexpensive Mexican spot in Hyde Park.  If you are looking something above Pepes but below a higher end Mexican restaurant, Maravillas is perfect for you.  I'd even venture to say food-wise the needle points more to the higher end than the lower end.

I think the large disparity of reviews on Yelp have more to do with the service than the actual food itself.  The food has always been great to me and again its inexpensive.  So if you aren't looking to spend a lot but get a nice size meal, you would probably enjoy it.  The burrito dinners I've had have been big and plentiful in size.  And the taco salad is great too.  My biggest pet peeve about Mexican restaurants is sometimes they don't provide you alot of meat in your meal and overload it with vegetables, but they don't do it here.

Now the service may leave much to be desired.  The place isn't high end and when you walk in you may see tables that haven't been clean yet and stuff like that.  But that usually is remedied pretty fast.  And on a weekend or Friday night, you may encounter some wait for your meal so if you can, call ahead of time.  But besides that, its basically just like a diner.

If you want to avoid all of that my recommendation is to order your food to go and I think you would well satisfied with the food.  But makes you call ahead of time to avoid the wait.

First of all during brunch time, the waiters/waiteresses will push the carts out and walk around, and then you can call them over if you like what's on the carts.   This is how it is traditionally done back in Asia. Of course, you also have the options to order dim sum on the menu in case you don't have the patience to wait for the carts to come that have the dim sum you want.
Secondly, this restaurant is decently priced, which means you can spend about $25 to get stuffed and also have some leftover dim sum to bring home with you.
Next, the taste of dim sum is pretty savory, it was never too salty, bland, or anything like that for me. It has always been consistent every time I go. One of my favorites is the shumai, it's big and tasteful! I would always get 2 orders of them.

A family-run Cantonese seafood restaurant that screams "don't mess with tradition". The food here is unpretentious and this is reflected in both the ingredients and price. The things to die for here: roast duck served with five-spice sauce, deep fried soft shell crab, salt & pepper squid, and stewed beef tripe with tofu skin. The taste of the dishes takes a step back from commercial kitchens and reminds you of home-style cooking. Moreover, while most Chinese restaurants tend to use a ton of oil and MSG to enhance the flavor, there is a level of lightness to each dish that leaves you satisfied the entire evening. Advanced reservation is encouraged as the space is small. The ladies who take the orders might not have the best command of English, but when they have a suggestion for a dish, maybe because you looked stuck, do not think twice. This is a hidden-gem of Chicago's Chinese restaurant scene that I would absolutely recommend to any foodie who has a passion for adventures in authentic cuisines.

My wife and I were taking a walk in the city on a friday night looking for a place to unwind after work and we came across the famous Hard Rock Cafe. We've seen multiple locations arround the country so we thought let's give it a go, it must be a great place since there are so many of them all over. We walked in and we immediately were seated by a pleasant gentleman, but that is where the nice experience ended. Our waiter Joshua arrived and we asked him bring us two Lagonitas IPA beers for starters while we look at the menu and pick something up. We waited and waited and waited and no beer. We looked towards the bar to see if it was busy but there were only two older gentlemen sitting by it and they were already taken care of. Finally Joshua arrived and asked us if we picked anything to eat and we very politely said yes, we will have a shrimp appetizer but if possible to get the beers we requested first. He said no problem and disapeared. Still no beer. He returned after awhile empty handed and he told us that the shrimp appetizer is not available at this time but not to worry since it is not worth it any ways. Shocker! We remained calm. The place was not even busy in the slightest for them not to be able to make it. The menu has only few items anyways so for them not to have 1 of the 3 apetizers was just laughable. We asked Joshua if they had the nachos and he said yes so we went with nachos this time arround. My wife reminded him of the beer again. Few minutes later a tall gentlemen finally brought two beers. He balanced both beer glasses in the palm of his hand as if his palm was a  serving tray . He thought this is very cool but he did not pass us the beers, instead he froze his arm high up in the air and we were expected to reach out and grab them off his palm. This was an impossible task since if I took my glass first the other would simply fall out since both glasses were leaning against each other on the tiny surface of this person's palm. Also his palm was so high up in the air that we had to get out of the booth on order to stand up and pick our beers at the same exact time. Well, the beers spilled all over. The gentleman thought that his way of serving is cool as he made a ridiculous clown expression but in reality this was the most absurd service I've ever encountered in my adult life. The nachos took forever. My wife and I were really trying to maintain a positive attitude where there was no positivity to be found. At last Joshua arrived with the Nachos and we  asked if he can bring 2 more beers since so much time had past that our glasses were empty. He responded that the bar is busy but he will do everything possible two bring them when opportunity allows for it. Our instinctive first reaction was to look towards the bar and there was literally no one sitting there now. On top of that the night was very slow. I don't know if Joshua is a bad waiter or this place is just bad overall. The answer is both - the waiter and the place are just horrible. The nachos were a complete disaster. They don't even come with meat. It is just chips, a wee bit of sweet bean from a can and a pinch of liquidy cheese and jalapenos. You pay a premium price for that by the way. For reference 7/11 has way better nachos that come with beef by the way. We did get our second round of beers we chugged them, paid and left incredible disappointed. We still tipped Joshua $7(the bill was $58). To sum up-  The wait for initial  beer was close to 30min and the bar was empty; The beer was served in the most absurd way possible; the wait for food was 40min and the place was not busy; The food we picked was not available but we were not made aware till way way later; Food was horrible, fake and plasticky! How is this joint still in business!?

The menu is surprisingly large and well varied, which will probably please anyone in a group. The food itself was above my low expectations and came out hot. Service was friendly and the seating was clean.

Appetizers of choice are the shrimp & crab bisque when it's cold out or the baked goat cheese, crab cakes, or lobster-crusted rack of shrimp when it's not! (Scallops are pretty awesome as well!)

For those looking for a meal I've always been a fan of the Medallion Trio allowing you to snag three of their signature crusts (All 6 are good though I usually go with Blue Cheese, Mushroom, and either Horseradish or Parmesan depending what mood I'm in.)

They have a slew of great cocktails and wines to pair with each meal and if you somehow have room for desert the cheesecake and key lime pie's are amazing. I've heard the triple layer chocolate cake is too for chocolate lovers.
Delicious dinner tonight! The lobster and steaks were superb and the service excellent! Can't tell you if the price was worth it because work paid for it.

If you are looking for that classic old fashioned steak house this is your place.  A large menu with several meat and fish options, great sides and drinks.  I cant forget to mention the deserts either.  This place is great for any occation.
Went to a private dinner and EVERYTHING was delicious!!!!!!.  the service was great too.  Can't wait to go back.  Get the glazed salmon!
Nice place to eat. We enjoyed the steaks and will return soon.
Great location, close to shopping, so perfect for refueling. The menu is fun and hearty and the ambiance feels like a throwback to hunting / ski lodge. Very cushy and comfortable.

Let me start by sharing my fears before my real experience. We were doing family style, which I have never had a good experience with at any other restaurant. I thought it would be mass production of poorly made food. I also have never been and just thought it might be chain like. I WAS WRONG!!! Woohoo :) Sometimes I like being wrong (don't tell).

My beginning experience was with their social media person because I tweeted about going to dinner there. As a social media strategist I absolutely LOVE when restaurants interact with people who are actively talking to them. Kudos...your social media person rocks!!

Ok on to what matters...food and booze. I seriously wanted to eat a second round of EVERYTHING. We had a group of 11 people.
-Started with 2 Appetizers - Pizza + Spinach Artichoke Dip. Both were delicious. The pizza was so crispy and flavorful. Yum. Could have made that an entire meal.
- 2 Salads - Chopped Salad + Cesar Salad. Both were good but the Chopped Salad took the cake. It was like a Southwest Salad almost with corn and tortilla chips.
-2 Main Dishes w/ 2 sides - Steak + Salmon. 2 sides - spinach and twice baked potato. I could have eaten this for a week straight. The steak was cook perfectly and was so juicy and tender. Salmon so flavorful. The sides were yummy too.
-2 Desserts - Apple pie skillet + Cheesecake - YUM

I had a Wildfire Manhattan and it was absolutely delicious. Strong but had great flavor.

Had a wonderful experience. This is the "morning after" and I'm still full! Can't wait to go back. Now I just need a date to take me ;)

I've eaten here, and I've had the pleasure of being part of a company Christmas party here one year, and it's a solid steakhouse for Chicago. Never had a steak here I didn't like, and the drink selection is solid, too, with options like The Macallan 18.
The food was good and the menu had a ton of options. The atmosphere was great and wi would go there again. I recommend this to everyone. Great location with bars and shopping

Call me snobby but compared to other steakhouses Wildfire has a pedestrian, suburban feel to it. The dishes are your standard steak and seafood entrees which are fine but in a city like Chicago I expect a little more. Every time I've been here the restaurant has been busy and a little too loud. My advice: take a large work party here but don't bring a date.
Great taste comes with price
Very good PIZZA

Wildfire is consistently great food and a nice place to go with a small group of friends.  It's a little pricey (what downtown place isn't though?) and it can get a little over crowded for my taste but I'll be back.

Good atmosphere, food and service all for a great price. This is the place to go if you want a good steak dinner downtown for under $50 bucks. I've been here twice and had the Ribeye and New York Strip. The steaks were quality cuts and cooked as ordered (medium). I haven't yet developed the taste for aged steaks, but one meal here and you will be pining it again over any chains you might have tried in the past. I'm not one to add any fixings but I know some rave about the crusts you can add. Non beef-eaters have options as well. My wife enjoyed both chicken entrees she has tried.

Wildfire has a range of offerings for starters and sides but I just go for the house salad and gigantic, stuffed baked-potato. Desserts and bar service are great as well. I don't see any reason not to come back even if I could afford to eat at some of the other steak & chop houses in River North.

We went there last year on our annual trip to Chicago. The staff was very friendly, especially our waitress. The food was absolutely amazing and their drink specials were great. Usually a $5 long island isn't the best (bottom shelf items). But, the ones we ordered tasted almost like top shelf. My boyfriend has been talking about it all year. We were very impressed and are definitely planning on going back.

I Was There Last Night... The Food Was Awesome And The Wine Superb! The Waitress Was Divine! She Had Great Timing And Was Very Friendly! However The Only Problem Was The Manager On Duty Petros Diakatos! His Insensitive And Attitude Towards Customer Was Very Disrespectful And Uncalled For... When The Patrons Where Explaining Something He Would Cut Them Off And Answered Questions With Questions... Very Rude! I WILL NOT RETURN HERE AS LONG AS HE'S THERE! SOUNDS CRAZY BUT THAT DISTURBED ME KNOWING HOW LARGE MY BILL WAS! I Suggest That They Send Him To A Hospitality Classes!

Energetic vibe. Quality wines available in half bottles. Roasted beet and goat cheese salad was delightful. My petite filet with roasted vegetables was excellent.

Service was attentive and courteous

I look forward to going back.
Great mid west steakhouse
Great restaurant; Great SERVICE GREAT FOOD and return often! Love the halibut when in season!

Everything I had was delicious. However, my husband was less satisfied with his menu selections - the broccoli was seasoned with way too much lemon, and his steak was cooked to medium-well instead of medium-rare, but I give it 5 stars anyway because it is such a great place for someone who can not eat gluten.
Went here for our wedding anniversary, great dining experience.

It was serviceable as a steakhouse. Very nice waitress - was able to try the bacon-salted mixed drink before committing. The steak was ok. Tried a bite of the bison meatloaf and we both agreed it taste quite a bit like turkey, and the sauce lacked flavor. Co-worker said she wished she had ketchup with it.
My favorite restaurant. Always good food, drinks and service. The price is right on point for a great meal downtown. I go back constantly.
great steaks, nice atmosphere

Was just recently here for a birthday party. Such a great experience here. The wait staff was also constantly running around making sure everything was taken care of properly. There is nothing special about this restaurant. The service was very poor and our server was very slow and rude. The bisque was no better than an expensive can of soup. The outside of the restaurant is so unappealing that we almost did not go in, but we had tickets to a show nearby and the reviews of this restaurant looked good. I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone that has a sophisticated  palate and enjoys finer food, because you will be very disappointed.
Disappointing trip to wildfire. Mediocre food and super uncomfortable heat

Will be going back solely on the service.

Food was fantastic

Very good menu selection of steak and sea food. Wine selection is very good too. Really enjoyed their house wine with my steak. Dessert menu is okay... Not much variety.

Great place for dinner. Great atmosphere, snappy service, and the steak is out of this world. Highly recommend to anyone who enjoys a classy evening out.

Solid LEYE restaurant. Good food and service.

I paid the tab, needless to say- I won't be returning.

All I can say is WOW. This is a wonderful Steakhouse.

BEFORE DINNER:
Valet parking was quick and attendant was happy considering it was pouring rain when we arrived. There is a coat room to the right along with the restrooms and a private dining room to the left as you walk in. A large bar is farther up and the main dining room is across from it. We had an early dinner and was seated upon arrival. Dining room is large and very comfortable. Plenty of room between the tables.

APPETIZERS:
We started with the Jumbo Shrimp Cocktail, yummy. Then the Wood Oven-Baked Pretzels (2). I never seen a soft pretzel on any menu. It was so fluffy and light that it melts in your mouth. It was not dense like the ballpark pretzels or salty. It came with Sharp Beer Cheddar & Honey Mustard sauces.

ENTREE:
We had the Roasted Prime Rib of Beef rare, it was awesome. It was served with Horseradish Sauce, which was very tasty and not overpowering. Also the Au Jus was not salty at all like most are. NOTE: we requested a larger cut then the King Cut and they accommodated us with a 30 ounce cut for a very respectable price.

A consistent, mid-range, Chicago-based chain with solid, better-than-average cuts of the steaks they carry. Generally good service. Wildfire attempts to evoke old school steak houses while keeping prices out of the stratosphere. It's popular because it balances good meat, good service, and high but not exorbitant prices. Far better than, say, Sizzler or Outback, but not comparable to the Palm or Smith and Wolensky or the many local standards in Chicago. Notably as part of that balance, Wildfire avoids culinary trends like waygu or reverse sear, but by sticking to classics it does deliver a good, dependable value and tasty steaks. I don't go there when I want the very best red meat experience, but I do go there when I want a solid streak with good service and a pleasant, relaxed atmosphere.

Wildfire is one of those reliable, stand-by restaurants that you just know you're going to have a great meal at. My husband and I had out first date there in 2002 and have subsequently celebrated anniversaries and birthdays and hosted business dinners there. We moved abroad in 2015, but would always think of Wildfire when we returned to the States. Finally, last week, we happily made it back. Overall, our service was exemplary and the food good, but, unfortunately, not as mind-blowing as I remembered. It was a very busy Friday night, and though our appetizers and mains came in a timely manner, side dishes were forgotten or not fully cooked. My sister and I both ordered the au gratin potatoes (which, historically, we loved because they are amazing), and had the same experience with them being almost cold in the center, with very hard, uncooked potatoes. Our server graciously took them back and had them refired, but, they came back nearly the same. I finally came to the conclusion that, not only were they undercooked, but they were unseasoned and simply didn't taste very good. So, while my leftover steak, potatoes (seasoned and reheated) and lemon-herb broccoli made for a great lunch the next day, and the rest of my dinner experience was good, I can't help but feel like Wildfire's star has dimmed a bit in my eyes. Perhaps they just had a bad batch of potatoes - I won't hold it against them because we have had some many other wonderful meals and memories there. We look forward to giving them another shot!

Warning signs of a bad Greek restaurant:

1.   No lamb on the menu.
2.   No moussaka or other traditional Greek dishes.   (Souvlaki and gyros aren't enough.)
3.   No Greeks.
4.   Few diners.

I should have known better than to eat here, if not right when I walked in the door, at least when I looked at the sad, sad menu.    There are certainly a lot of Greek restaurants in Chicago's Greektown.    Perhaps 9 Muses is one too many.

My platter certainly *looked* appetizing.   The Greek salad had nice presentation, but was unfortunately quite flavorless.    My pork chops looked big and sumptuous, but were actually THE WORST PORK CHOPS OF MY ENTIRE LIFE.    They were so dry, it was like I was eating jerky.   These chops were so tough, I injured my elbow trying to saw through them with my steak knife.     (One of my dining companions ordered pork kabobs that were also overcooked.   Who runs the broiler in this place?   He should be taken out back and beaten with spatula.)

My friends raved about the french fires at 9 Muses.   I found them soggy, uninteresting, and no better than that of any hamburger joint.

One of my companions ordered the calamari (predictably deep fried almost beyond recognition) and they certainly smelled good.    But I was horrified to taste squid so old it smelled rotten.    I hope my friend didn't end up getting sick from eating this spoiled fare.

Other dishonorable mentions:   lousy beer list, poor ambience, and lukewarm service.

The only saving grace to this place was that it wasn't too expensive.    My share of the bill was only $24.    A better meal elsewhere would have cost more, but certainly have been worth it.

All I could do after eating here was drive home, feeling disgusted, yearning for a shot of good ouzo, and praying for better meals to come.

About 10 minutes later we ordered 3 appetizers to share while we thought about our entrees.  The waitress told us the kitchen will only take full orders and then course it out for us.  Look, we're not tourists and we are all well versed in Chicago dining.  My sister who was there is a food writer and even included Sepia in her book on Chicago dining.  I can understand why the kitchen may want to get the full order at once, but we just weren't ready to order.  Then it just became combative.  To the waitress' credit she wasn't rude, but she just adamantly refused to take our order unless we were going to order everything.  She kept saying she was just following management's rule, to which we replied, that if that's the case send the manager over.  She did not send over the manager, so we just paid the drinks we had and left.  At that point there was just too much tension that it was clearly going to make it an awkward dinner.  On the way out we told the hostess, who was genuinely concerned and asked us to wait to speak with a manager.  At that point we were just tired of dealing with it so we left and said they can call us if they want to follow up.  The bottom line is we didn't try the food that we've heard great things about because one very standard issue request was so hotly contested.  I definitely don't want to see anyone fired over this, but I'd be shocked to find out that a professional kitchen in Chicago would so adamantly refuse to take an order even at the expense of a customer.  Perhaps it's just inexperience.  I would consider going back to try the food if I knew that this was more of a one off event, but I'm certainly going to stay away for a while.

What happens when you turn an old 1890 print shop into a Michelin Star restaurant? You get Sepia - no I don't mean the effect you get in photography although the restaurant boasts several portraits highlighting this hue. Sepia is one of my favorite fine dining spots in Chicago thus far!

The interior is pretty mind blowing - the space incorporates pieces from the Chicago's past eras so it has a nostalgic feel to it while being incredibly modern and chic at the same time. Here's what's good:

VEAL AGNOLOTTI
This dish was absolutely delicious. The tender pasta was aldente and stuffed with a flavorful and meaty veal mixture served with raw diced vegetables. Additionally, there was a hot veal consumme broth that was poured over the pasta table side which was a nice touch.

PAN SEARED TROUT
The fish was perfect seared with crispy skin and served with smoked potatoes and chiogga beets. What made the dish though was the horseradish sauce that added a kick to the subtle flavors of the fish.

PORK BELLY SANDWICH
The portion was generous with the unctuous fatty pork belly and crunchy veggies that cut the richness of the meat. The dish was also served with crispy duck fat frites - how can you go wrong with anything fried in duck fat??

COCONUT PECAN CAKE
This dessert was knock-your-socks-off good! It came garnished with coconut tuile and the cake was incredibly moist and flavorful. Definitely recommend getting this. You won't be disappointed.

The service was outstanding. Dishes were always cleared and servers were professional yet friendly. The manager Ben was super accommodating always checking in on us making sure we were having a great experience. Although some say the portions are too small, I'd much rather have a small serving of great food than a huge plate of food that's bland. Quality over quantity! Make sure you check it out!

They also provided an amuse bouche of vegetable broth.  It had a beautiful light tomato and carrot base.  The sable fish I ordered was cooked to perfection.  The skin was so crisp while the fish was so tender.  In our party we also ordered the strip loin and pork tenderloin.  The sauce with the pork was really tasty. Thank you for a great birthday meal!
Not only is the food great and quite innovative for old school dishes. But also cheap (for chicago)

Great food. Wine list is incredibly interesting with off the beaten path wines. Best part - the sommelier doesnt hide somewhere and let you fumble through the list. Jenny came over and picked the perfect wine for us. She's great. Ask for her!
Nice service and well decorated chocolate moose. Desdert wine was excellent!!
Great table in back & superb duck!
Can not say enough great things about this place. Went here for lunch the service were very friendly and attentive. They were very accommodating to allergies, and the food tasted really great.
Delicious meal and attentive service. Nice ambiance. Solid restaurant, but not especially memorable.
Just had drinks at the bar. The bartender was incredible. Super friendly and makes great drinks
Delicious!! The Cavatelli was incredible!

Group of 6...we were in town for a conference  visiting from Calgary .Beautiful dining room. Outstanding service. Wine selections from sommelier were great  Everyone enjoyed their meals  For me  the highlight was the dessert. Pumpkin Cheesecake  with ice cream, salty toffee crunch on top  Wow. . Brilliant balance and flavour mix.
Fairly decent place for lunch

Wow, what a total disappointment. I think the other reviews here must have never been to a true Michelin Star restaurant. The service was not just not good, it was bad. The food, yeah okay, but seriously, at a $100 a head for a four course tasting menue it should have been much better. Don't waste your one night in Chicago like I did...I should have gone for a pizza and it would have been much, much better.
Very kind & delicious and creative foods but price $$$

I totally didn't mind this cafe, the food is amazing, plus the washrooms were clean. It was a little fridgity inside, so that was not the very best. The service is great. I will absolutely consider returning once more if I get the chance. Me as well as my close friend ordered the toast as well as we were not disappointed. My one tip is to keep the cool exterior. Laters!

Happy hour was the highlight. Drinks amd bites were fabulous. Dinner was underwhelming. Staff was excellent but I was surprised and disappointed that the dinner menu was uninspired and the food itself didn't have the finesse I expected with a Michelin star...

Your wine glass will never be lonely: great service (perhaps too good).

Food is incredible

Intimate experience.
Moderately even small servings, pleasant atmosphere, good service.
Delicious variety of options in every course!
Love the decor- great food and selection
Perfect meal. Every course was nuanced and balanced down to the amuse bouche. Will be back.
Incredible food, wine and service. Jason was amazing !
Food, drink, service and ambiance were just perfect. Loving this meal days later.
Absolutely the best service and the tasting menu was phenomenal!
Excellent food. Best service and amazing cocktails.

I went for lunch and enjoyed my meal. Starter soup was good. This place is definitely big plates, small portions type of restaurant. I loved the wood around the restaurant - the entryway,  the bar. Service staff was amazing and our waiter was knowledgeable.  I didn't give it 5 stars because I felt the meals took a long time to come out every time. The restaurant is small but they have 2 corner tables that are a little private and secluded that are a nice option. Other than that, great experience.

Very tasty food historically, we only popped in for drinks this time during their happy hour. Easily one of the best old fashions in the city! Ridiculously tasty and delicious, definitely a must have if you’re there!
Staff was very friendly and knowledgeable. Fantastic place for dinner and delicious seasonal cocktails. Definitely plan on returning for another meal.

Always delivers a beautiful meal. Flawless really. Cocktails excellent. Not an inexpensive place for these reasons. But not as pretentious or painfully trying to be precious and exquisite as some of the newer places in the neighborhood.
Worthy of it's Michelin star.  Pleasant,  unpretentious service.   Enjoyed an excellent tasting menu with accompanying wine selections.  Fairly priced for what you get.

Went on the restaurant week 2019. We didn’t like the duck liver mousse, a little too greasy and not delicate in the flavor. I like the agnolotti and the chocolate mousse! The ocean trout is a meh, bland and doesn’t have the level of surprise in sepia.

An elegant Michelin star restaurant. We went as part of Chicago restaurant week. The menu was tailoured for restaurant week, but I would definitely come back for the very homogenized and delicious squash soup as well as the wild rice crepes.

I can't believe Sepia is Michelin Restaurant. I spent about 120 $ for dinner but ended up eating extremely salty clams, and other ordinary foods. The size of the foods was small, but the foods only are okay, more like something you could purchase at 40-50$. I think Sepia didn't treat this event seriously. Sepia possibly reduced the quality of foods to deal with the reduced profit.

Also, the service was terrible. We ordered Sparking water, but during the meal, waiter added plain water to our Sparking water!!! The remaining sparking water was screw up, and that's not a mistake a Michelin Restaurant should make. Plus, the manager didn't come to ask us how was the meal. The dinner was not busy at all, so I guessed the manager didn't care a lot about the Chicago Restaurant Dinner
The food is good.  The people are nice, but the service is very slow.  Expect to spend a minimum of 1.5-2 hrs for lunch. I have never gotten out of there in less than 1.5 hrs.

A really stellar experience, our host and sommelier were fantastic, excellent services and great conversations. Went here for celebration dinner with my wife. Arrived a bit early and was able to get cocktails at the bar, truly on point. Great intimate spot, I was somewhat concerned that the smaller venue would have us right on top of our neighbors, but the spacing was great. Wonderful time!
Michelin starred and for a reason. Food is mouthwateringly good. Ambience is lovely. Would definitely go back to try their tasting menu and other items!

A concise menu of locally sourced foods, paired with a well curated wine list. What used to be a challenging acoustic environment has been much improved and the friendliness of the staff has been consistent over the ten+ years it's been here.
Very tasty modern food, nice service and delicious drinks. I will be back.
Always perfect.
It was a great example of how a human touch of your server makes a whole experience. Alex thank you for that
A real gem.  The tasting menu is a mind-bender.  Great for client outings or a quality evening out with a significant other.
Stunning restaurant. Sexy! Some of the most pleasant and accommodating staff!!!!!  GO HERE!
Amazing food, staff and decor. Love Sépia.
High standards getting higher, can satisfy even the most refined palates. Each meal brings you such a tasty flavor. Wonderful interior design and professional staff. Worth every penny. Recommended

Andrew Zimmerman has maintained a Michelin star since he started at Sepia; since 2011. Food was impressive; service was great. Tasting menu was one of the cheapest we’d had and every single thing was good. Can’t wait to come back. They did well to take care of my gf, whom can’t do cow dairy.
my favorite restaurant in Chicago
american food, mmm, so good. I was super full. This place has a great atmosphere.

Went for lunch last Thursday with my husband. I was overall disappointed.  We picked the fixed price menu.
I asked our waiter if they was any way I could switch the dessert for something else like cheese for example as I'm not sweets. He didn't even bother to try or anything and said no.
Appetizer was ok, I would suggest nice country bread with the mousse instead of the fried tiny toasts. It is nice to have that much of mousse, but you should give enough of bread to go with it.
I picked the short ribs. My bad I didn't read the details... When the plate arrived, I figured this was actually pasta with some short ribs sauce.
I switched plate with my husband who got fish. Our waiter stopped by, didn't noticed the switch... We didn't complained about anything but we should have.
Food was good but our waiter was totally careless.
The menu can be a little light, but a solid contribution to the foody scene.
Bright, paced, deliberate.

My wife and I came here for a quick lunch before our flight.  Not really impressed with the quality of the food.  We ordered the cheese board, burger and The cod.  I normally don’t write reviews but the fries were burnt,  the cheese choices on the board were blah and the cod had no taste.  We were expecting a wow meal but got a less than OK meal.
Fancy schmancy haute cuisine. Very nice.

Took my wife here as an early Mother's day gift. What a fancy outing this was. We did the 6 course entree experience. Definitely a pricey menu but well worth it.

Very nice decor, friendly staff, just bring a fat wallet. Lol.
Always a great meal and great service.
Fantastic food and cool ambience. Probs are good and a little smaller than other places, but absolutely delicious!

Delicious dinner! Great service! The falafel dish was a great vegetarian option. I also got roasted radish side dish which was absolutely delicious. The main dishes are not very large, so you will definitely want to have an appetizer or side of veggies as well.
Solid under the radar business lunch place, walking distance from the Loop
Tasty food and accommodating to my nut allergy! Great experience
Keith is a master mixologist, and the cocktails and experience reflect this.
Only the food amount is so little, I wonder I ordered the children lunch set.
Loved it!! Everything was incredible from the food to the service.
Servers are great, but the food is on 2 stars. For this amount of money, you expect more delicate taste, and you just get tons of salt and pepper instead.

We went here for the first time during the restaurant week. Out of the whole prefix dinner menu, what we liked the best was duck liver mousse. They were very generous with the portion of the duck liver mousse. The pork loin was a bit too dry. Ocean trout was good but nothing too special.
Decor is good, service and staff are good, food fell short of expectation. I’ll be trying proxi next to really get to know the chefs and figure their food out!

I'd give four stars if this were a comparison between 1-star Michelin restaurants only, but in the world of Google we are comparing Sepia on the same scale as we are comparing Burger King - and that's just not fair to a place of such high craftsmanship. I really enjoyed the reasonably priced tasting menu, I liked how the flavors played together - I would have expected 6 instead of 5 courses (excl. amouse bouches). But who am I to judge? The pappardelle were a highlight to me. The wagyu tri tip more of a marketing thing (it's a pity the chef has to measure against inspectors who expect fancy ingredients over flavor). Why not offer duck, quail, iberico or other powerful flavors instead? Cheaper for the restaurant and better for the tasters - but worse for the pretentious folks who need that Wagyu.

Excellent food with a generous tasting menu in this one michelin star.

Find the complete experience @rafamxcdmx on Instagram
Consistently excellent.
Delicious food! Good service!
Unremarkable food with high end prices. Three little nuggets of falafel does not make an entree.
Effortless dining at Sepia thanks to the impeccable team, both front and back of the house.

Visited in July 2019 while visiting Chicago. That was definately one of the highlights of our tour. Excellent service and menu. We decided to go with their tasting menu ($95) and wine paring ($60). Both were excellent. Wagyu beef is just to die for. Amazing! Scallops were wonderful too. The whole menu is unbelievable! Wines were amazingly paired with all dishes. The interior is classy, simple yet very beaitiful. It is a former print house, so it has that that vibe. It is pricey, (well, it has a Michelin star) but so worth the experience! Thanks for the holiday of taste!
Wonderful. Great service. Flavorful food. Amazing wine list.
Food was great but service was very slow. I've been to 12 course tasting menus that took less time. There was a ton of time between servings. All that aside the food was great.
Great food! Lots of surprises. Ok service...
Excellent service, simply amazing food preparation and presentation, good prices..a winner all around!
Great drinks and food, brilliant staff
Incredible food and very well priced for the portions you receive.

Before anything else, I asked for a cocktail, and settled on one made with tequila, though as a general thing, I have a marked preference for mezcal.  This cocktail was appropriately made with Reposado Tequila.  For those who don't know the difference, do a little research and learn something new. Sorry I don't have pics of every item, sometimes things are too appealing to permit the pause needed to take a photo!
Wonderful space, food, and wine list. I can actually hear my friends talk in the dining room. Lovely

Had a business dinner here in their private event space. The space itself is excellent and the service was solid. We had a fixed menu and I ordered the chicken and apricot tart. The salad was light and fresh but tasty. The chicken was well seasoned but a little over cooked. I did like the couscous and vegetable medley. Dessert was very tasty apricot tart but if you blinked it was gone it was so tiny. Overall, it was a tasty meal but nothing amazing.
One of the best restaurants in Chicago. Staff is very professional and catered to every need. Nice a la carte options if you don't want to do the tasting menu. Food was absolutely outstanding.
Really good and chef food
Best Old Fashioned I've ever had. Great dining experience if you want a nice night out.

I picked Sepia based on customer reviews as I wanted to find a great spot to celebrate my friends Birthday. I had high expectations being a Michelin star restaurant but needless to say it was a flop. Ambiance was average at best nothing out of ordinary the food it self was just okay. We opted for the tasting menu thinking that would be the best way to try everything however there was nothing that wowed me. For the price we've been better going to Boka or Maple & Ash where you can always expect delicious food. Service was slow and not attentive. It was a one and done for me.
Delicious food, warm and quiet atmosphere, beautiful presentation. Very classy place!
Best food ever! The service was perfect!

Really wanted to give this restaurant 5⭐
The food was good, but nothing blew my mind.
Service was 4 stars. I had some questions about the origin of the fish and did not find out if it was wild or farmed. Sturgeon was nicely flavored, but a little dry.
Wine pairing was 5⭐ very good selection
The details of the food could have been a little bit more professional, Michelin like.
It was a nice 2 hours experience in which I tasted numerous types of different food.

Have eaten here three times now. First two were for restaurant week and the third was regular menu. The first experience was the best. 1st review: Very good food. Visited for restaurant week, but will definitely return for the full menu. Service is great. Cocktails are great. Decor is classy.

The second two visits the service seemed cold and lacked the friendly touch I expect from not only Michelin rated, but from Midwest Chicago dining hospitality. The food from the second restaurant visit was lacking. The regular menu on the third visit was very good.
Stopped in for the lunch prix fixe. Seasonal flavors, well-executed and balanced savory/sweet. Great service.
Very good food for those seeking classic culinary experiences. The food is delicious, the selection of wines is great. Staff was super friendly and polite. Nice place for a special dinner.

I've been wanting to try this place for months, but that's because reservations is about a two month wait.

The bone marrow is a must.  I don't come here often so I never remember what I ordered until I look at my last photos.  For some reason I am always getting the agnolotti.  It always sounds so good.  And for some reason it doesn't taste the same when I first had it.  It doesn't taste bad just different.  Even the color of the meal looks different also.
Nice restaurant with warm welcome. Varieties of food options. Very few vegetarian options.
Exquisitely imagined and executed dishes; attentive service. Easy to see why they got a Michelin star!
Finest place to get something when in a rush. The service is prompt, pricing is reasonable, good vibes. I highly recommend this place

The food was good.   The service was terrible.   We were there for a business lunch.   It took us over 2 hours to finish the meal.   We has to ask the bus boy if we could order starters 12 min after we were seated s the waiter had not arrived. The restaurant was cleared out before we got our mains.   There was a good 5 min between the food arriving at the table for 5 of us and when the food arrived for the 6th person.   We literally had to go to the front desk to ask for dessert menus.   When they arrived, we were told we could not order a dessert of the price fix menu!    One person at our table had ordered the dessert as part of the price fix and another person wanted a slice too.  We were told they do not do that.  That about sent us off but we had another 20 min to discuss the service while we waited for the desserts to arrive.
Excellent food and service
Great food and service!
My favorite Chicago restaurant. Chef matches flavors perfectly and great wine selection

Fantastic experience dining with 6 coworkers. It’s almost easy to miss this place, as the signage outside doesn’t immediately catch your attention, but it was a welcoming atmosphere as we were greeted just inside. We tried a little of everything the menu had to offer and were impressed with all of it. The grilled sturgeon was fantastic, and sea scallops as one if the appetizers were perhaps the best we had ever tried. Would definitely recommend, and I’m sure I’ll be back during future visits to Chicago.

This was my first time ever dining at Sepia and I must say, I was impressed. Sepia is moderately priced, especially for the quality of food the are creating. The food and menu is of a different order entirely—wide variety, often locally sourced, and presented creatively. The cocktail menu was, creative and the cocktails were delicious. The wine list, had some big names, but also some hidden gems. This was very cool to see. The night that I visited the restaurant was busy, and the team looked to be understaffed. The service was good, but not what I was expecting considering what I have heard about there service. Overall, my experience was great, and I look forward to returning in the future.

I have been to Sepia several times. "In the beginning" it was great experience.  Fantastic food served by awesome folks.  The last few visits delivered excellent food but the service so lack luster a robot would have been preferred over our uninterested, uninvolved waiter who was able to offer no description of the dishes, how they are prepared or make recommendations when asked.  I think last week was my last visit regardless of their Michelin Star.
Delicious food and great service.
Friendly service in bustling location.  Outstanding apple and celery soup, a too salty but very good foie gras sausage and a great moist carrot cake headlined the lunch menu

We booked the table a few weeks in advance, and good that we did as the reservations fill up quickly on the weekends. I received confirmation via email and a personal call to verify any food allergies and sensitivities.

Our server was top notch and so was the dining experience. From the tender Japanese A7 Wagyu to the smokey caramel of a 30 year old Port each element complimented and built on the previous.

The atmosphere was full of sound as everyone in the room appeared to be happily conversing and enjoying themselves while the wait staff was buzzing with food and drinks.

Our table received a special taste plate from the chef that seemed unique, similar to miniature macaroons and cream. It was tart and sweet which made for the perfect palate cleanse after the appetizer of savory buttered scallops.

We didn't feel rushed, there was no pressure, and our server was patient as we asked questions and bantered about the menu. The server knew all of the menu items and was not shy about sharing opinions and making recommendations.

Dessert was worthwhile, and I won't regret the extra calories. Throughout, the house special drinks were easy to sip. My taste was for a "Gentlemen's Thief" (Rye and cider?) which was not too week, not too strong, was perfectly balanced and felt natural while waiting at the bar for our table as well as complementing the meal.

On a side note, the local Uber Black drivers knew to stay close as we were picked up within a minute or two of stepping outside.. very good for a cold evening with warm friends.
Atmosphere is very comfortable and accommodating. Wait staff knowledgeable and very friendly. Food was exquisite. Will go back when we are in town.
Caring atmosphere and wait staff. Interesting combination of foods.
One of my favorite restaurants, always a pleasurable time and amazing food

I believe it all starts with co-owner Donato Poto at Providence. It is clear he cares about every detail. He personally made my guests feel welcome and gave personal attention to the entire meal. He has an amazing staff who know just what to do to create a wonderful dining experience. Donato it would seem to me has hand picked the very best talent available anywhere. There is a gentleman his name was Adam who orchestrated everything to perfection, including having Donato help introduce various courses of the meal. Every detail was perfection. The outstanding reputation they have is earned every day.
This place gives wonderful service as well as tasty food. My favourite place in the area. The food served quick and the rates are fair. I recommend this place.
Food was decent enough. Duck was on the rare side. Service was very slow - took almost an hour to get orders in
Great food, very nice staff members, constantly excellent ambience. They charge convenient prices and the food quality is good. Fantastic work.

Had the privilege of dining here during restaurant week, and was quite pleased.  Small, piquant dishes with carefully paired flavors, gracefully presented and served by friendly, knowledgeable staff. Ambiance was sophisticated without being stuffy. Great date night out.
Classic style inside, with incredible food. Worth every penny.

Always something interesting, be it something entirely new to me, or something otherwise mundane done amazingly.  Was just there for restaurant week 2020.  If you are going, Milk-braised pork collar isnhighly recommended.  The polenta in that dish is simply amazing.
This spot gives extraordinary service as well as tasty menu. My favourite spot around here. The drinks and food served quick and the rates were economical. Recommended.

There is a reason for the other good reviews! Food and service were great and consistent. The wine ordered wasn’t available but it was well replaced by the sommelier. Definitely coming back and highly recommended.
Food art!  Dinner was fantastic! Alex was our server and his recommendations were spot on. Restaurant Week in Chicago!  Stop reading and make a reservation!
We visited the restaurant a few days ago and we were very satisfied. The service was very attentive and the food was flavorful with a lot of finesse. Highly recommended.
Truly delicious. Service was impeccable and the food was absolutely delicious. Everything you'd expect of a top tier restaurant.
Very good food, nice spot and the people are simply a joy!
Delicious and beautiful food. The taste is Rich and balanced, highly recommend.
Portions were really too small for the price. Interesting mix of textures and lovely plating, but flavors left some depth to be desired--appetizers and entrées overly salty, dessert rather sugary.
This place was great. Had a Quintessa wine tasting this night. Has a private room for parties. Had a drink in the restuarant and it was great.
Great atmosphere and food
Went there for Valentine’s Day, was in my expectation! Recommend.
Staff was phenomenal and the food was delicious

This was my first time ever dining at Sepia and I must say, I was impressed. Sepia is moderately priced, especially for the quality of food the are creating. The food and menu is of a different order entirely—wide variety, often locally sourced, and presented creatively. The cocktail menu was, creative and the cocktails were delicious. The wine list, had some big names, but also some hidden gems. This was very cool to see. The night that I visited the restaurant was busy, and the team looked to be understaffed. The service was good, but not what I was expecting considering what I have heard about there service. Overall, my experience was great, and I look forward to returning in the future.
Had a wonderful work lunch with my colleague.  The food was exquisite and the staff was extremely attentive. Thank you for  a great Michelin star experience
Amazing dining place with delicious food

I tried this jewel during Restaurant Week and I can’t wait to go back. The flavors and portions were just right. They had a great lunch crowd and very good service. The coursed lunch was perfectly and I would recommend this place.

I come to this excellent place from time to time  as I like the  special atmosphere that is unique to this restaurant. The team is exceptionally loving and skilfull. The service is absolutely fast. Most important, the food they serve is good. I ate there often and I was always satisfied. The expense is reasobable. I highly suggest this restaurant to to everybody.

I have been going to Sepia for many years and have always had a great experience- local food, unique combo’s, and a speakeasy vibe. We did their takeout tonight and I felt compelled to write a review. We ordered the eggplant entree for two which came with a gazpacho soup, salad, dinner rolls, broccoli, and dessert. It was flavorful and multi-dimensional. Will definitely be ordering again.

Take home menu during this pandemic gave us an exceptional Michelin experience on my own dining table. My wife missed dining here for a long long time so I decided to surprise my pregnant wife with their take-out menu.
Couldn’t believe the excellent value for the generous price. Thoughtfully prepared and generously portioned. They got everything from appetizer to dessert. Finely decorated and absolutely delicious. We said ‘unbelievable’ more than 100times while eating.

The presentation of the food is exceptional and the food was probably good. They kept bringing drinks but no food. We waited an over hour and a half for the first course. We asked the server to please bring out the first course. He brought out more bread. It was the poor guys second day and he was confused. He wasn’t trained and didn’t have any knowledge of the menu.  After 3 hours; we left without having the fourth course served. It might have been a great experience if the food would’ve been brought out within a reasonable time or if the server wasn’t so overwhelmed and undertrained.

Fantastic staff and extremely clean. We were really impressed with how Sepia handled the dining process with virtual menus and receipts., allowing for little to no items being passed back and forth.  The food was excellent and absolutely quality.

Visiting Chicago, me and my cousin felt it would be fun to go to a Michelin star restaurant. Sepia was definitely the right choice.

The experience began before we even sat foot in the store. They called ahead to ensure we has no food allergies, which is very nice of them. Walking in we were greeted by a hostesses who was super nice and took our jackets. Mind you we were dressed plainly and in our early 20's, and were treated very nicely.

The food? Was absolutely spectacular. I loved every portion of my meal. I got a lamb rack and it hit the spot in flavor. Large enough to get full and full of flavor, cooked exactly medium as I requested. They brought a Biryani, that was amazing, needless to say I was shocked they pulled that off. The potatoes gratin were great as well.

5/5 the experience, ambiance, and food were worth the modest price tag.

Fantastic dining experience. Not only did I enjoy the food but also the rustic decor. The extremely friendly and accommodating staff as well as the amazing food made my evening in Chicago a night to remember. I will definitely be back!

I came with my partner and of course the 4 course dinner is what we ordered, they had the menu online, so all you had to do was hover your phone camera over a QR code to find the menu. I ordered shaved mortadella and plums for my first course, and I can certainly say that even thought it was great I preferred my partners choice which was the fluke crudo. For my second course I ordered the mushroom chawanmushi, my third was halibut and for desert, strawberry and buttermilk Panna cotta. The interior was beautiful and the staff was extremely friendly. My partner did notice that we were the only couple that had not been visited by the manager, she had greeted every table except ours, and I don't really want to take too much offense to it, but it was just unprofessional to walk around and greet the table next to ours and make eye contact with my partner and walk to the table adjacent to ours.
Unexpected.. sometimes a stroll to a close by place and having a superb experience is quite the highlight of .. this year i think.. best restaurant i have been to this year definitely..
Ok spot for tasty american food. It was so tasty. I've had nothing but pleasant experiences here and plan to keep coming back. The bill was appropriate for the quality.
Great food! Friendly staff. This is one of my go to places. I will be back
Ok spot for quality American food. nice location to meet with family. the service was very sociable and kind.

One star prix fixe menu that costs less than my regular hotpot dinner so yay!
Non-special food that you forget about once you leave the door, but was pretty good while you were eating.
Ok cocktail.
Waitress didn’t know anything about wine but was really nice and enthusiastic!
If restaurant can update their menus more often this could be a good regular food spot!
Favorite 1 Michelin star restaurant. Superb food and service. At decently affordable rates. Will come again, and you should too
Superior dining experience! Everything was excellent!
"Fixed prix" menu is a bargain for all the different dishes you get. Food is great. Neutral decor. Friendly and unpretentious staff. Highly recommend.

The most careful dining experience we have had - clearly protecting their staff and their customers, and that made us feel very comfortable - best dining-out experience we have had.   The four course offering presents varied choices that include something for almost every taste.   I don't ordinarily take the wine accompaniment but I was glad it did.  The sommelier included wines I would not normally order but which went perfectly with each course, and sized to ensure I stayed sober.  The side of corn chanterelle salad is so rich that it is almost a meal in itself.  So nice to have a constant in our dining lives.

From the moment you walk into Sepia, you notice the laid back, wood tone and calming atmosphere of the restaurant. That calming and intelligent design aesthetic marries perfectly with the attentive, but unassuming servers who finesse the flow of service with professionalism and knowledge. The Tasting Menu was exquisite and the perfect amount of food, if not more so. Especially good were the two mains that my husband and I had of the duck and the halibut confit. My husband said it was the best duck he’s ever had. Sepia is perfect for a fine dining experience, without the fine dining pompousness. Date night approved.
Nice service and great food. Such a lovely experience
My top spot for tasty American food. Everyone at our table was quite pleased. Service is typically great. Prices are decent for the quality.

What a fantastic experience dining at Sepia! Beautiful, intricate and refined dishes, and an eclectic cocktail list made for a wonderful dinner experience, that ended with very tasty dessert.

Service was friendly and attentive. Would highly recommend!

Added: pictures from our recent takeout experience, which, while a bit involved, was also really spectacular food-wise!

To add to the review above, since the COVID-19 pandemic, we’ve tried Sepia at Home twice now and both times we’ve been stunned by how great it was.

This Thanksgiving week, we’ve tried the beautiful moist chicken breast with mustard jus, and the salmon, with multiple sides and everything was spectacular. A consistently great experience!

Edited to add: we also opted for the Sepia Christmas dinner and immensely enjoyed it. The rack of lamb was good, but the roasted root vegetables and the mashed potatoes were the real star! 😋

A West Loop resident long before Fulton Market became Chicago’s hottest hangout, Sepia’s reopening sees the Restaurant operating in a new era of social distancing and time limits while the current $65 prix fixe may just be the Windy City’s best Michelin-starred bargain. Housed in a 19th century print shop since 2007, restaurateur Emmanuel Nony smartly recruiting Executive Chef Andrew Zimmerman in 2009 and since earning accolades from the French tire guide, JBF and Jean Banchet Awards, diners visiting Sepia in the era of Covid-19 will begin their evening with checked temperatures followed by city-mandates necessitating masks be worn any time staff approach the table with fresh serviceware or even a refill of Water.

Started off with the complimentary bread and the butter - always a great start. To start, I went with the Tagliatelle, which came with pheasant sugo and black trumpet mushrooms. The tagliatelle was perfectly al dente and the mushrooms were so savory. Really enjoyed this pasta + cod combo!
"This place gives wonderful service as well as tasty food."
This mixologist knows what he is doing!
Amazing flavors!
An amazing dinner. They were very on point with the covid protocol and still made the night memorable.

Restaurant week and Sephia popped in my radar.
We were lucky to get a reservation. The atmosphere and ambiance is top notch. The service was awesome! Very attentive. The food was excellent!!!
Now, I started missing Blackbird. I wish they survived this pandemic.
Thank you Sepia. We really enjoyed ourselves. Will be back!

Couldn't have asked for a better experience during the 2021 Chicago Restaurant Week. The service was above and beyond, kind, and attentive. They sincerely cared about allergies, ensuring we were comfortable, and that we understood the foods we weren't sure about or questioning.

The food was simply amazing, decadent, the perfect and expected portion size. The selection for such a set menu was broad and amazing to choose from. Stars were the monk fish and the potato agnolotti. The roasted banana ice cream on the dessert was out of this world, and it was such an honor that they recognized and honored my birthday. There was no bad dish, the cocktails were also stellar. The staff made us feel comfortable, kept up laughing, and ensured we were well served.

In seeing some of the other reviews, I see no issue with the servers asking for us to put our masks on when they approached our table, this is fairly common and a way to help the staff feel more comfortable. They should not be faulted for that in any way.

Fantastic staff and extremely clean. We were really impressed with how Sepia handled the dining process with virtual menus and receipts., allowing for little to no items being passed back and forth.  The food was excellent and absolutely quality.

The best part of the experience was the hostess, bar tender, and then our server Kim.  The food was ok and whoever selected the wine parings was...  ok.  The service was a highlight and for those that love to feel special while dining, I cannot recommend it enough.  The food, wine, and desserts will take a back seat to your experience with the team.  I would still recommend.
A definite place to go in Chicago . Food is an experience of joy.  Wine pairing was excellently handled by the sommelier.  If you are thinking of going there,  do.
Amazing meals and service
Attended for Restaurant Week, loved the vibe, great food, fun wine pairing, excellent service. Would definitely go back.
It is a belated birthday outing that all enjoyed the food and service is always superb.

Sepia deserves the full one star Michelin rating based on it's food alone, but what makes my wife and I come back over and over again is it's amazing bar service from their head bartender, Keith.

Everyone should start their meal with a cocktail before wine, as this is simply the best cocktail bar in the city of Chicago. Forget Aviary, Violet Hour, etc...just find a seat at the bar and let the bartender know your ideas and preferences.

I've yet to be able to replicate this experience anywhere else in the world to date, and I've been lucky to travel quite a lot.

Thank you to Keith, his fantastic partner bartender who has since moved away, and the whole staff at Sepia for weathering the storm of COVID. You managed to come out even stronger/better/more competitive than when things shut down.

We'll not only be back again and again, but will continue to enjoy and recommend Sepia for business dinners, big nights for out-of-town family events, and most specially: the best before or after dinner cocktails we've yet to find in our 7 years here in Chicago.
Exquisite! Excellent service, as well.

La Scarola is the real deal - it would be at home in the North End or San Fran - classic dishes immaculately prepared.  We're still aglow from an enchanted evening of fun and fabulous flavors.  Now some specifics:

Scarola & Sausage special app - tender escarole and tasty Italian sausage, awesome.

Mussels in White Sauce app - fresh mussels with flawless flavor and texture, garlicky and decadent sauce worth dipping every piece of bread you can find into.

Pasta Vesuvio - perfectly al dente linguini with chicken breast browned perfectly and suspended in a rich wine/mushroom/garlic sauce.

Vitello di Franco - Jose pushed us toward this one and he was not wrong.  Crispy scallopini with garlicky fresh chopped tomatoes.  Uh, yeah!

Pasta Amore - special of the day, penne with seafood in a creamy sauce - basically seafood pasta alfredo and 100% fabulous comfort food.

Pollo Italiano - fuggedaboudit - so good.

Cannoli, vino, cocktails, cappuccino...

Other honorable mentions on their menu include the cheeseburger and hot dog. But make no mistake, this place is all about the polish sausage. You'd be crazy to go here and not buy at least one of those.

The prices are fair, about 5 bucks for a nice sized polish with fries. They have 24 ounce sodas, bottled water, and canned soda also. There is no place to sit, (typical Chicago hot dog stand) but they have a long counter against the building where you can stand and eat if you wish. If you are transporting these buns of goodness, I'd recommend either putting the paper bag in a plastic bag (if you have one) and closing it tight or put them in the truck if you don't want the smell in your car. One of the last vestiges of Chicago's historic Maxwell Street shopping district, Jim's Original Hot Dog Stand offers up a satisfying array of "greasy spoon" fare.

Originally located on the corner of Halsted and Maxwell streets, it relocated to its current spot on south Union Avenue; just south of Roosevelt Road on the western flank of the Dan Ryan Expy, some 20 years ago after the nearby University of Illinois in Chicago (UIC) bought up the surrounding real estate.

Since then, the entire area has been gentrified; with upscale Townhomes and Night Clubs having replaced the old shopping district. In that sense, you might say that Jim's Original is a "throwback" urban island of sorts ... a nostalgic reminder of the area's rough-n-tumble past.

Polish Sausages, Hot Dogs, Pork Chop and Chicken sandwiches; Hamburgers, Cheeseburgers and more - all come with free French Fries.

Mustard, grilled onions - the aroma of which wafts across the adjacent Dan Ryan Expy (I-90/94) - and sport peppers are the only toppings available off the grill for the sandwiches (sorry!, although ketchup packets are included).

They're a 24/7, 365 day operation (as is the Express Grill, located just 50 ft. south; oddly enough, the fare is identical to Jim's Original - Jim's is simply more well known, having been a neighborhood fixture since at least the 1940s, and probably longer).

In its own way, Jim's Original is just as iconic as Chicago's deep dish pizza and Italian Beef restaurants; many tourists as well as locals regularly frequent this establishment.

It's a bustling place; always busy - especially on weekends - no matter the season, day or night. It's a carry-out, open-air restaurant. Despite the frequent long lines, they have a surprisingly efficient system for ordering and paying for your eats.

If you want an authentic, big-city, non-corporate fast food experience; and if you like this type of food, Jim's Original is a must-go!

Picture this; it's 2AM, the night air is crisp and heavy with the smell of onions, diesel smoke, and cigarettes. You and your crew are drunk and maybe a little high. You spent most of your money on the IPA's at a near-north side bar that had barely any singles, so the night's looking like sort of an L. You need something hot and greasy to cut all the beer and shame in your system. There it stands, Jim's Original- the bastion of all Chicago Polish Sausage stands. You couldve just went to the "maxwell street grill" your uber drove by, but it looked super run-down and there were nothing but thugs in line so you decide to pass. Jim's is different- a welcoming yet small stand off the coast of an ocean of cars clipping along down I-90. You hand the man your last $5 bill, and out comes a sack of happiness not illegalized by the federal government. A nice, long, Polish sausage Sandwich topped with greasy onions grilled to jammy perfection. A side of perfectly crispy steak-cut fries to supplement. Bliss. The hot peppers are hotter than you'd expect, but thats okay because you need something to get the taste of bong rips and IPA out of your mouth. Blessed be this hot dog stand, as it has served drunk chicagoans for 80 years now. Clearly, they're doing something right.

Brian [one of the owners I believe] is a super-nice laid-back guy who's looking to make your meal as delicious as possible. Great staff and great food that takes about 10 minutes to prepare. Can't lose.

In Chicago you cannot give a single answer to "what's your favorite pizza?" without specifying the type of pizza.  For us, this place is our favorite for traditional Neapolitan. Great service, neighborhood crowd is cool. Place will not disappoint. Pizza is cooked, as the namesake indicates, in a great coal fired brick oven.  This makes all the difference along with the fresh ingredients.

Love their pizza - crispy, grilled & a bit smoky. One of my faves in the city as far as thin crust goes. You can choose between a white pizza or a red pizza & personally I love white pizzas, so Coalfire can do no wrong. Their special pizzas are always inventive & tasty, def worth a try. Super friendly staff & a great casual bar atmosphere on a quiet corner.

What to order: the White Pizza (how your resist so many cheeses, including ricotta?)
Great wood-fired pizza, and the service has always been excellent for me, both dine-in and carry out.

Had dinner there for the first time Saturday and the Pizza was great but the service was even better! Erin was our server and she didn't hesitate to take our salad back when we had forgotten to order without onions. She also warmed our pizza a second time when we mentioned that it had cooled while we were chatting. Kudos to Erin and all the staff at Coalfire!

Delicous pizza made in coal ovens, giving their pizzas a yummy crust with a slight smoky flavor. You can also get calzones, and customize your ow toppings, delish!

Love their Italian style Pizza. (I ordered Nduja with salami which they recommend and it is really great!)

One of our choices came to the table a little burnt but they apologized for it and replaced it before a 2nd piece of pie was to be had. I'll be back for sure.

Best thin crust pizza hands down, try it with the steak bits on it

Other than that there really isn't anything to choose between them. If you think you have had Pizza before eating at Coalfire, you really have not.

I love my deep dish but I love a good thin crust as well. There is something about that crispy crust that somehow manages to be chewy as well that leaves me wanting more. I think it has to do with the super hot oven. The ingredients were very fresh and the staff was great. In a city where pizza isn't taken lightly, coalfire definitely earned it's street cred.
Their 'Nduja pizza and Caesar salad is amazing.
Coalfire is quite average in my opinion. Perhaps my expectations were too high .. I compared them to East coast pizzerias (Salle's , Pepe's, Di Fara etc)  .

Consistently named to top pizza lists, Coalfire doesn't disappoint. I love that they use simple, fresh ingredients that let the wood-fired crust sing. They offer several reasonably priced wines by the bottle so bring a few friends, order a pizza or two (try the Pesto or Fiorentino pizzas) and enjoy an evening in West Town at this neighborhood joint.

Customer service so attentive to detail,  Promptly notified of wait time and given beverages and menus to salivate over the  next courses.  The house salad was delightful and abundant (enough for two) with a taste of sweet red onions.  The pepperoni and mushroom pizza was reminiscent of our time in Rome but with an earthy smoky flavor.  Tonya was attentive and informative regarding beverage selections for our palate.  Truly an epicurean delight.

There's a reason you see Coalfire mentioned positively everywhere. For starters the staff goes out of their way to make you happy. I often tip based off of refills and they were on top of it.

I think most of my drinks I was just putting down from finishing and a replacement was already there!

Onto the food. I've eaten here three times and each time was fantastic. The Caesar salads are amazing and the pizza is to die for. I love pizzas made in this kind of an oven and there really aren't enough places that do it these days. I've had both the Prosciutto pizza (amazing) and twice the Sausage and onion which, most likely, is what I'll have my next trip there! My friends that introduced me to the place insist I try their pepperoni as well so that'll probably eventually end up in the mix.

Great staff, great service, great food. This is a must visit for fans of oven pizzas in the city!
Love, love, LOVE this place! Hands down the BEST brick oven pizza I've ever tasted. The owner and employees are just as amazing as the pizza.

Chicago is known for its deep dish pizza.....but I'm a much bigger fan of the crisp-yet-chevy, superthin, coal-oven, Neapolitan style of pizza. Coalfire does this VERY well.

The inside decor is minimalist -- nothing fancy. They've got a variety of decent craft beer in bottles. A few types of cupcakes for dessert.

But the pizza. OMG... the pizza. This is one of my favorite pizza joints in Chicago. Last time I was here, my group had the 'Nduja (spicy Calabrese salami, fresh mozzarella, basil and tomato sauce) but we added goat cheese. The 'Nduja is one of the tastiest pizzas I have ever eaten. The flavors were a perfect combo. Sweet, creamy goat cheese with the fresh basil and that spicy sausage!

Pizzas are thinner and delicate, so I recommend no more than a few toppings on a pizza. Two people can share a pizza....3 if you're not that hungry. (Just get another one if you have 3 people. They're so good. You'll want more.)
Fantastic!

It's a great spot for a first or second date, packed with plenty of people watching and an energetic noise level reason enough to sit a bit closer than usual.

Pizza is Neapolitan style, very crispy and thin.  Went with a big group and they were accommodating.  Place never disappoints.
This is such a lovely little spot.  The place feels like a family business.  I don't know if it's not one. And I was mesmorized by the guy shuffling the pizzas around in the coal fire.

For takeout, they gave us a cup of basil to put on at home, and the combination of the sweet basil, spicy sausage, and tangy sauce was unreal. I cannot wait to take my family to this restaurant and to try more!

Best thin-crust pizza around, rightly deserving of the many accolades it's received over the 8 or so years Coalfire has been in business. Owners Bill and Dave bring East Coast-style Neapolitan pizza to Chicago, baking it in a coal-fired oven (850+ degrees) to give the chewy crust a slight, smoky char. (NB This is not cheesy, greasy NYC pizza, but more resembles New Haven apizza than anything else.) The menu allows you to build your own, but highlights a dozen or so tested and true combinations. Our current favorite is the Cremini, with coal-roasted mushrooms and garlic finished with an arugula topping. But the house specialty Margherita is a perfect example of its type, and the White pie is classic New Haven. Meats and cheeses are sourced from a variety of local vendors, and over time you'll see them mix it up a bit. (I'm still missing the bacon-and-onion pizza they had a few years ago: the bacon came from PQM and was deeply porky and chewy.) Good selection of bottled beer and wine. There are a few salads to start, and dessert is a selection of sinfully-rich cupcakes. Friendly, highly efficient waitstaff and a fast order turnaround time means that even when there's a line outside, you'll be seated quickly, usually with in 20-40 minutes. If it's real busy, Bill or Dave will take your phone number and direct you to a nearby bar, where you can relax and wait for your table to open. Coalfire is the real deal, so no more excuses - Go!

If you come on the weekends you risk extremely busy crowds, we went Sunday and waited over 20 minutes. Well worth it however, because the food is some of the best Filipino food in the city. Focusing mainly on breakfast, you get comfort foods like garlic fried rice, bangus, tocino, longganisa, and more. Each order comes with Lugaw, sawsawan, and champorado. Lugaw needs a little extra kick but honestly that's how it usually is unless you're at a place legitimately serving you lugaw as a dish and not like... a bonus... lol. Just add a little soy sauce and vinegar and you'll be good to go. Something I saw in other reviews I'll echo, the texture of the champorado is not something I was a fan of. I will also admit I haven't eaten it yet. It's in my fridge. I plan on  trying it, and usually I eat it right then and there but I got full really fast and I was thrown off that it was cold. My mom said that's normal, but I'm used to champorado being warm or room temperature and the texture did look pretty gelatinous. With all that being said, ima still eat it. I love champorado. Just hoping this one is good but again, it's a bonus dish lol. The place is super old school. Feels like one of my tita's basement from the late 90s. I personally would only come here on the weekdays to avoid those crowds. Or order pickup. But when family and friends come into town (like this Sunday) a 20minute wait is WELL worth it for Uncle Mike's. You arent going to find a Filipino breakfast better than this. And with new restaurants opening up and me being disappointed by them, Uncle Mike's stands the test of time again and again.

The food was magnificent! I ordered the mushrooms which were easily the best much rooms I've ever tasted. I don't know exactly what they did to them but it was magical.
