First, the food took long, which is something that usually happens there, but if the food is good and hot, I don't mind the wait. We finally were given our food, not by our waitress but by someone else, which I assume was the manager on duty (blonde lady), she was not so friendly and basically just thew the plates on our table and walked away, didn't ask anything else. I noticed a different smell coming from my plate and as I look down, I see American cheese, grilled onions, red peppers all piled up on our sandwiches, which in all the years and times I've ordered this item, it never had any of this. They also forgot to bring me the extra jerk sauce I requested upon placing my order. Our waitress was working alone so I understand she couldn't attend to us, so we waved the same person down that dropped off our plates and I asked what was all this stuff on my sandwich. She said that's how it came. I told her that I was a long time customer, since the location opened and never had all this been on the sandwich. I also showed her the description on the menu which read, "lettuce and tomato", nowhere did it say anything about all the extra things added. She then proceeded to tell me that the menu was changed, I then told her, well it's not in print. She then seem to have been bothered and finally offered if we would like our sandwiches fixed. My friend didn't want to deal with is, so he just took off all the extra stuff. I told her, yes please for mine. I want to taste the jerk sauce, not grilled onions, red peppers, or American cheese. I could've just gone to any other place for a chicken sandwich on a pita if that were the case. So she takes my plate and returns about 5 minutes later, which I found odd since it took more than a 30 minutes to get my sandwich when I first ordered it. They removed all that other extra stuff and just threw jerk sauce on it, and the same old piece of soggy lettuce and tomato from the original sandwich. Not sure what's going on here, but most places just make a fresh one when there is a mistake, not recycle the same sandwich. Still no extra jerk sauce on the side as I had originally asked, so I had to flag her down again and she brought it back like it was such a hard task. I really wanted to be happy that this place had opened back up, but not sure if I will return after this. No apologies were given, no complimentary anything for the inconvenience, just no type of customer service at all. I also miss the plaintain chips that they used to bring while you wait for your meal. Not sure who's running the place now, but these changes I'm seeing are not positive so far. I hate to have to give this place 1 star, but maybe you should look into who your staff is and update your menus. Our waitress was nice, but she needed help, no complaints on her, or the music. Sometime ago prior to shopping in the area at Aldi, I had some spare time to hop on Yelp and search what restaurants were near. Well, Feed popped up, so I scrolled through its reviews, tips and pictures. And needless to say that the rest was history because from there I bookmarked it.

Anyway! My initial visit came after feeling in an adventurous foodie mood, deciding to eat at Feed prior to hitting the boundary between Humboldt Park and East Garfield Park neighborhood. The restaurant itself has been one of my bookmarks for a while now, so I figured why not? Parking is the only reason that has held me back from eating here within my discovery of it.

As for parking your only option is street parking which can be limited at times and may put you further out from the restaurant, so choose wisely when or if you visit. I almost said the hell with eating here before doing a u-turn to snatch an open spot I found on West Chicago Ave.

After entering the restaurant, I could not help but to look around at its intriguing interior which consisted of chicken decorations & pictures all over it. Other than that, the restaurant has this old-fashioned feel to it. Kind of like a combination of a momma-and-poppa breakfast diner and a southern food restaurant with a serious obsession with chickens!

Being that I wanted breakfast, breakfast was the main thing I searched for on their displayed menu. And speaking of breakfast, it is served from 8:00 AM -3:00 PM.

As for my order, I ordered the biscuits and gravy w/ 2 eggs which arrived in a timely manner. The biscuits and gravy was flavorsome! And when I say flavorsome I am meaning that my taste buds will crave it regularly. There was just something about it that made my taste buds go wild! And prior to leaving I giggled at the employee and stated that "I need to leave before I order something else."

In closing, I left Feed happy and with a bloated tummy, realizing that I had to push my workout back towards the evening, go figure! FYI, take notice of their nightly specials which will have you considering it as an option for dinner as well. And be sure to bring cash, but if you forget, the restaurant does have an onsite ATM.

The Oakley Fest was going on over the weekend and rather than settling for a slice of pizza or an Italian beef sammich at the tents we decided we wanted something more intimate. Ignotz was right in the middle of the fest so we figured we try it out. I didn't realize their main door was on the  side of the building to the right... do make note... it's the door on the left as you walk "back."  We were greeted and seated immediately. There aren't many tables, I would say about a dozen tables, but there was a good amount of ppl dining in.  It got a little loud. I knew I loved this place already the minute they put down the roasted garlic right next to the bottle of olive oil. We were given 2 different breads, one "ball" shaped one and then 2 sliced rolls.  I liked the rolls better,  the bread was much softer. So we ordered the linguini & red clam sauce ($14.50) and the baked rigatoni ignotz, not on the menu, the server suggested it ($18.95). The rigatoni came with a choice of soup or salad.  The minestrone soup was pretty tasty. Both pasta dishes came out piping hot and were absolutely delicious.  Each pasta dish alone was enough for 2ppl so we had plenty of leftovers for lunch the next day.  We did not get to try any of their desserts since we were so full, but they do give you 2 complimentary chocolate covered cherries with whipped cream before you leave, which was nice.  I appreciated that the owner, Roger, walked around to say hello to everyone and shook our hands. You don't get that in many places anymore these days.  And Lisa, our server, was awesome! We will definitely be back.  Definitely recommend Ignotz if you're looking for some really good Italian food, cozy hole-in-the-wall experience, or if you need a good date night spot.... this place is it.  Cheers!

This place can give a new meaning to rush hour.  During peak times such as lunch  and dinner hours( approx 11a.m.-1:30p.m. & 5p.m.-6p.m., respectively) the two lane drive thru is often jam packed, sometimes spilling onto Kedzie and causing a bit of traffic inconvenience. Not to mention there are extensive wait times to even get to order inside and outside (at lunch rush more than dinner generally) but once the order is made it does not take as long as I'd think given then amount of customers.  During these times,  I have found it best to drive to another nearby McDonald's (if you must) such as near Cermak and Western,  that location can be a bit less busy even during peak hours.  Another perk is online ordering with Curbside pick up,  great for a timed work/ school lunch time or you just don't like long lines like me. ( Additionally,  there are other food options within a 1 block radius in nearly every direction if you don't have the time or inclination for ordering through the app).  Otherwise it is your average McDonald's nicely located near an intersection beaming with a variety of businesses. So if you find yourself shopping near 26th and Kedzie you may want to pop in here especially if you're on foot since there's nothing particularly special (good or bad,  other than prime location,  I surmise)  about this drive thru/ dine in .  On the other hand if you're driving, when it's not bumper - to - bumper busy you can see that it has a nice sized parking lot esp. for this area with stores packed like sardines.  And if you need to,  you can get gas directly across the street!

Overall,  if you're hungry they'll  take care of that without usually taking too much time or money. Always,  check your order though because I can't promise it will always be right the first time - nobody's perfect.

Great vegetarian food is hard to come by and so is healthy food. Moonlight vulture is a sandwich place that serves up vegetarian and vegan food with a couple of fish exceptions. As far as the food goes, it ranges from pretty good to ok among the dishes that I’ve tried. The seasoning is as muted as their unassuming sign making the place easy to miss.  Many of their spicy dishes are pretty tame spice wise despite the warnings to the contrary. Here’s a breakdown of the dishes I’ve had so far.
- The Tuna Face Melter has spice that is slightly detectable but the sin of the dish is the lettuce which gets soggy from the heat of the panini press.
- The Atomic is probably the best item on their menu but could also be spicier as you’d expect for a burger named the atomic.
- The Crabby Paddy tastes great and the real victory of the dish is the amazing sauce.  The cakes themselves are still delightful.

All things considered it could use a few tweaks to the menu and I’ll likely go back since it so close to my home, but I wouldn’t go out of my way to eat here.

Placed an order by phone and picked it up. Once home, we discovered two things we ordered (French onion soups) were not included.

Called the restaurant, they recognized the mistake and were apologetic. Offered to "hook us up" with soup with our next order. Guess the bottomline: never go to Bistro Campagne for your birthday.

Can't share the enthusiasm for Vincent. Went there on a Friday evening for dinner. No ambience on the outside area, compared with Replay or Marys on the opposite site. I had the burger which was OK. Fine dining prices for casual dining experience.

Pro: they do take care of social distancing, tables are far away from each other and you don't have contact with the staff.
The food and drinks are amazing and we’ve always had great service! We love bringing friends here whenever they come to visit!

Vincent is a once or twice a week destination for us. During the past 6 months they quickly and thoughtfully adapted to ever-changing public guidance to continue to safely serve their patrons and the community.

They never skipped a beat. Their street café is the place to be if you want to get out, enjoy a bite, and relax in the knowledge that your hosts understand the importance of safeguarding health and safety in the midst of a pandemic. Vincent's team goes above and beyond with 10 feet between tables, contactless ordering and service,  disinfecting and sanitizing, etc--all while serving delicious and imaginative dishes and drinks.

Creativity, adaptivity, and putting patrons and the community at the center of their business are among the many reasons Vincent is our favorite place to be.

Thanks to the amazing Vincent team. You've been our connection to life as we once knew it during this tough time.

I’ve been to Vincent more than a few times to have cocktails and a few smaller plates. Vincent has done an incredible job to make their customers feel safe during a pandemic. They’ve been creative, and asked the guests to participate in their desire to keep the environment safe and healthy. There’s not many places where I feel super comfortable dining out during a pandemic, but Vincent is one of them. Thanks all!

Thank you for keeping people as safe as possible during this time- if only other restaurants could adopt your method. I will support this restaurant, because of this. Remember guys, we are in a PANDEMIC! It is a PRIVILEGE to be able to dine out right now...

Contact-free dining experience with tables about 10 ft apart. I LOVED the ability to reserve a table and preorder online. Show up, find your table, order drinks and pick up/drop off your food without any issue. I hope restaurants continue to do this in the future! And the cherry on top was that good and service was INCREDIBLE. Will be returning specifically for the chicken liver mousse, pork chop and pot de creme  :) Well done, Vincent team!
Excellent food and great service!

Brillant meal with great cocktails
Outdoor seating and bar area to enjoy these delicious cocktails!
Great food (try the vincent burger), atmosphere (chill) and reasonable prices... I'll definitely be back.

Visited Vincent 2.0 last evening and was blown away by the new menu items.  Been going to Vincent for years and always enjoyed the food. We started with the Tartare followed by the Burger and Trout.  All three were amazing.  The tartare on top of the crostini was a palate pleaser. Not something I would normally order but the server gave it a thumbs up so why not try.  I'm still craving it the next day.  The crispy skin makes the dish and the side salad gives it a nice balance.  We can't wait to return.
Get the mussels!

Love, love, love this place and these people! Brian’s cocktails always impress me. There is always a cocktail on the menu that I’ll enjoy, diverse and well priced. Food is always on-point. Highly recommend for a date night, a night out with your pals or a solo evening for a bite and drink.

A friend and I ordered a bunch of appetizers and sides for carry out and everything was delicious! My favorite was the chicken liver mousse (with perfectly toasted, chewy toast points) and the roasted mushrooms.

Fantastic food.  Great service.

If you like authentic Korean bbq this is the place for you. They have affordable prices and the food is great. The service was great as well. good for big groups.

The ambience is very dark and classy--although maybe a bit too dark but it really sets the mood! The food is really good, try anything with fish! It's a souped up korean place so go here if you're taking someone new and want something more Americanized. The staff is REALLY helpful too!
One of my favorites in Chicago.  The dolsot bibimbap is delicious.  Don't miss the Korean chicken wings (DAK GAN JANG) or the Mandoo.  Friendly vibe, neighborhood restaurant and excellent cocktails!

This is what I get for relying too much on reviews when picking an Asian restaurant. I guess I should have realized that this wasn’t going to be what I was expecting since it’s located in the Andersonville area. I was trying to find a place with cocktail soju on Yelp, and this came up… but there is a HUGE difference between cocktail soju and soju cocktails. The cocktails we ordered were just mediocre, and didn't taste as well blended as cocktail soju--- there's a fine balance!

I had the octopus dolsot bibimbop, which was pretty good, but mainly cuz I love octopus! I love bibimbop. Service was pretty good. over priced. not as many free banchan as at a regular Korean restaurant. The food was good, and it wasn't far. so there's that.

Top shelf Korean.

I went here with my girlfriend last night and we had a great experience. The server, Mike, was very attentive and knowledgeable on drinks to order based on what we were looking for. He recommended a cocktail that had a spicy kick to it that was fantastic, as well as a ginger one (I believe called the Gin-Ju) that was also great. Nice place. The food was really good. The server answered all our questions (we had several haha). I had the Mandoo, Bi Bim Bap (both dishes were really good) other people on the table ordered the Mandoo (fried) and was good as well. Had two different Korean beers, they were "ok" nothing special.

FYI, there are no grills on the tables, this is not a Korean BBQ joint. It is however a lovely restaurant with delicious Korean fare and really great drinks.

This was a surprisingly good find, since we just walked in randomly, of the street. Every dish we had was great and the staff were very friendly and had good recommendations.
Really good and authentic Korean cuisine. They have small plates options so you can pick a variety.
Great service, delicious dishes...quality food for reasonable prices. Definitely come here next time you’re craving Korean, or want to try something new.

Delicious!!! It was busy when we got there, but we only had to wait 10 minutes. I usually get Bulgogi when I go to Korean restaurants but this time I got the Chap Chae because I wanted to try something new and it was totally worth it!
The food was delicious and the service was superb !
Really interesting menu, good service and a fun, energetic atmosphere. I haven't had much Korean food in the past, but I really enjoyed Jin Ju and will definitely be back to explore more on the menu.
Good food (get the sweet chili wings), tad pricey, good atmosphere, but would recommend!

All very familiar flavors. All the dishes we got were delish and I would recommend them all. I would totally come back to this place to try other things.
Great Food The Chicken Wings and Bulgogi are awesome.

Very good Korean food and cocktails although when we went last night, the service was slow and food was just ok. Don't know whether they changed hands but when we first dined there several years now, the food was simply amazing. Still a lovely place to have good Korean food maybe it was just last night.

I like to go with friends to this restaurant with my warmest recommendations. I visit this restaurant often. This recommendation is always successful. The dishes they serve are yummy and the crew is welcoming and cooperative. Whenever we visit this place we pass a cheerful evening.  warmly recommended.
Not all that knowledge about Korean food, but enjoyed the food here
It was an absolute joy dining here.  The food was absolutely amazing, and the bartender delighted us with his soju concoctions all evening long!

two days ago was the first time in this magnificent restaurant. But It is surely not the last time. We enjoyed the evening very much with the excellent service, with the exceptional cooking and wine and with the friendly cost. We will definitely go back there in a short time.

They have mediocre food for really high price. Do not recommend here at all. Go to more authentic places around H mart and Joongboo mart that taste like real Korean food and are cheaper. You are paying for the atmosphere.

This restaurant is absolutely one of the most pleasant restaurants in the region. Anytime I come to this place I am absolutely glad. They keep their very high  standard service and the topmost level of cooking  they offer. You definitely will enjoy this this place. Warmly  recommended.

So much yes! I haven't had Korean food in a long time. I ordered delivery tonight and the food was delicious! I had the kimchi pancakes, spicy rice cakes, and tofu soup. The portions were extra generous and banchan (small side dishes) were included. I don't remember the last time I had such amazing food delivered. My only regret is not discovering Jin Ju earlier!

Traveled 3 hours from Indianapolis to pick up some of this food! Worth the drive. Restaurant had a great social distancing set up inside for takeout. A bit pricey, but for someone who has limited Korean options, I was happy to let it slide and support this business.

Personal favorite was Japchae. Soft chewy noodles, wonderful umami flavor.

Kimbap was fresh and had a comforting taste, a familiar one.

Sides of rice were all perfectly cooked.

Kimchi is a bit spicy but effing delicious.

Kimchi pancakes were a bit oily and had a certain bitter taste at the end (I'm guessing from the oil). It reheated a lot better the next day when I threw ittit with the rest of my leftovers in a fried rice.

Can't wait to go back once the pandemic is over. Good luck!
Always look forward to eating at Jin Ju. They have delicious food and great customer service.
This place is good! Fair rates, considerable portions and the staff are always welcoming.

The ambiance is good, they are practicing social distancing and the food was good too. All the employees wore face masks. Although it didn’t seem that people were social distancing at the bar. All in all good experience.

I can say Jin Ju is a hidden gem (jin ju literally means pearl in Korean) of Korean food in Northern Chicago area. Grown up in Korea ~30yrs, the foods here are authentic Korean and the best Korean food I had experienced through entire my life in U.S.
My favorite spot for Korean food. Food was super flavorful.
My preferred location for delicious Korean food. this place is absolutely outstanding.

Jin Ju is most certainly the best find we’ve had in three years.  It’s so good, we’ve been there twice in the last two weeks.  The food is delicious, be sure to order numerous appetizers to experience the variety.  The wings, scallion pancake with and without kimchi, the gnocchi (they call them something else, the big plate ribeye steak is incredible.  The service was great, had the same server both times, he is a hoot, not to mention very attentive and helpful.  We had the opportunity to meet the owner last evening and she just makes the experience even better.  Five Stars isn’t enough to tell of our experience.

Visited during covid times and felt very comfortable with the large open windows and spread-out seating. Service and drinks were excellent. Pork spare ribs, duk boki, and chap chae were very good. Not knowing what to expect Jin Ju surely didn't disappoint. Service was professional, friendly and quick. The Sojutini was fresh and a nice touch to this contemporary Korean restaurant. Bibimbap remained hot the entire meal. The seafood was cooked perfect and was full of flavor. Recommend the bibimbap or bulgogi bowl. Overall a fantastic experience.

Unfortunately this place did not meet my expectations. I felt the pajun (scallion pancake) and mandoo (dumplings) were excellent, especially for the price. However, the brussel sprouts in the sam gyap sal were not nearly cooked enough - they needed a good char. Similarly, the texture of the bulgogi beef was not nearly chewy enough, and the meat was not well marinated. I did enjoy the accompaniments, but I've honestly made better bulgogi beef at home. Though there were certainly some winners on the menu, I likely will not return.

Their dishes are authentic and delicious (I grew up in Korea) - even their banchan (side dishes) were perfect. Jin Ju is a little more expensive than other local Korean restaurants with similarly traditional food, but the atmosphere is completely different. More modern and upscale with a bar, while still being casual.

This was the best experience I’ve had recently dining out! The staff is so professional and friendly, the atmosphere is warm and inviting, and every part of the meal was outstanding. We will definitely be back and highly recommend.
We ordered pick up and we really enjoyed everything we got.
ALWAYS an incredible experience here. From the ambience to the drinks to the food to the service, you just can't go wrong.
I’m Korean. This place is good. Eat here and thank me later.

Svea is Amazing!  Cheap and delicious food in an amazing swedish diner atmosphere.  My swedish cousins ate here and spoke of the authentic atmosphere and flavors.  I have been coming here since I was a little girl and it's always delish!
The best breakfast in Andersonville is also affordable and very friendly. Cash only, and only open to 2pm, but try it and you'll love it, too!

One of my favorite breakfast places in Chicago--gotta go at least a coupla times a year. Svea does great breakfast, great coffee--with a smile.  I have friends who've moved away that always daydream to me and reminisce about the wonderful Sveas....

Why in the world have I never stepped foot in this place when I've been living in the area for practically my whole life?!  I knew that Svea was a Swedish restaurant in Andersonville.  It was here for as long as I can remember.  I never knew that it was a cute little place that serves great breakfast items!

I liked the service, it was very quick and the food was great.  I ordered the Swedish Tease and it was perfect...one Swedish pancake with eggs and 3 strips of bacon...delicious!!  I wonder how busy it gets on a Sunday morning.  I will definitely be back!

This is hands down my most favorite restaurant in any cultural region of Chicago. Thanks to my dad who introduced me to this place before I read the menu, I have been going to Svea my entire life. I really liked it. The fried chicken was outstanding. Best crab cake I have ever had. The pork duet was disappointing. The beignet dessert with the molasses was way too sweet and I am a sweets lover. I would come back again. I wish it were easier to park in this area because we live in the suburbs but that's not their fault of course. Service was very good. They bring dishes out as they are made and it ensures that things are fresh and piping hot.
took my mom to lunch here for her birthday and we loved it!  I had the carolina shrimp burger with grits and we had fried greens and outstanding corn bread.  Service was hospitable and prompt!
Honestly one of the best places to eat in Chicago. I consistently love their food, and the bourbon list is amazing.

I feel like I know Southern food after living in Georgia and South Carolina, so four stars is more than fair. It's a bit more of the upscale Southern food with reasonable portions. The shrimp grits was a little heavy on the gravy, but the pork duet was well cooked and delightful.
Great southern food; good deal for restaurant week
Service and food were on point
Amazing experience here. Everything we ordered had tons of flavor and the cocktails were very good. Would recommend the corn bread and you can't go wrong with their desserts.
Great southern
Awesome southern comfort style food. Brunch is great. Def try the popovers. The name does not lie when it comes to portions.

I was not very pleased with this place. We visited with the hopes of aiming a true southern meal since we transplanted from MS approximately 7 months ago. I ordered the chicken and dumplings which turned out to be a kind of cabbage soup with egg dumplings and chicken and my husband got shrimp and grits which treated plain, watery, and very under seasoned. This was not the southern meal were were looking for but the wait staff was wonderful and the atmosphere was well done so I will give them credit for those aspects.

The roux in the gumbo is so dark, complex, and rich. Best fried chicken I've had so far in Chicago. I could also just eat spoonfuls of their pepper jelly. I just left having brunch their and I already can't wait to go back.
The chicken and biscuits are the best here

I've been here a few times for brunch and both times were completely different experiences. The second time was pretty terrible compared to the first. So this is almost two reviews. The first time, the head chef was here and everything was beyond perfect. I would have given this place 20 stars that day. I have been looking for a really well done southern restaurant. Regardless of anything, they have the best bloody mary in town.

The first time we had Bayou Teche, salt and pepper biscuits, and a simple cajun breakfast. We also received a set of beignets, no honey though. The Teche was just amazing. Smooth and deep flavor with the softest eggs ever. The sauce was mouth watering and the grits it came with were so good. The biscuits were these big awesome heavy lumps of delicious with some amazing butter to go with it. The cajun breakfast, while simple, was one of the best simple breakfasts my partner has had.

The second time, had some issues. I would say 2 or 3 stars. First of all, both our drinks were wrong the first time they brought them and my partner never got the correct drink she ordered after three corrections. By the time she got the third drink we gave up... and they were all pretty bad. At least my bloody mary was good, it usually is. We never received beignets even though everyone else around us did and we asked for them. The biscuits this time were tiny and extremely dry. Eugene's breakfast was decent but lacking in flavor. The roasted tomato and goat cheese omelet was pretty good but not great like last time. Part of this might be the fact they were packed and there was one waiter for the whole place.

So I want to love this place but it's pretty bad when you have two entirely different experiences. I'm disappointed really. I want to go back but I'm worried it's just going to be another sad experience.
The food description sounded interesting, but the flavor and taste was mediocre. I felt like the food was overpriced for the amount and flavor of food that I received.
Pretty good food.

I'm not sure how good this place is for brunch but for dinner? Uh nah. Came in for some chicken and dumplings and you'd think it'd be easy enough but what we got was a thin soupy, tasteless mess that could've been better doctored up in my kitchen with a boullion cube or two. Really disappointing for a place that's supposed to have some of that Southern flavor bombs coming at you. Bummer. For Southern food and the price point, was hoping for a bigger portion as well.  :T
Good food. Love where their food was sourced from, as they use some of the city farms like Growing Power.

The food is ok, I'm not a super fan of southern food but that's on me. The review is about the service. I've had both a good and bad experience with the service here. First time the waiter didn't acknowledge our party and made us wait a while to order. Second time the place was empty and we got service right away.
Pretty good cajun food for being in Chicago. A touch pricy but the brunch is amazing.
Unique and delicious southern fare! I love getting brunch here.
Great, extensive brunch.  Southern specialties I would not make at home.
Amazing southern cuisine, with a great whiskey selection. Ask them about their whiskey passport and you could get a free bourbon.
Great food and awesome brunch!
Good drinks, mediocre food that's barely southern.
Nice soul food joint! Had the fried chicken sandwich, hopping john, hush puppies, Sazerac. Delicious. Waiter was friendly and helpful.
The greatest fried chicken sandwich in the world.
EXCELLENT brunch menu.  High quality Louisiana-style fare.  Full bar with craft cocktails.

Scratch kitchen that bakes it's own bread, and breaks down whole hogs. Brunch is amazing, the heavy cream poached ham is heavenly.

Dinner: listen to the specials, they are always great. potatoe leek soup is dreamy

Breakfast: house made boudin, eggs faulkner

Cocktails: some of the best cocktails in andersonville, come for the food, stay for the craft cocktails. Also, they have the hands-down best American whiskey selection in Andersonville
Very good overall, cool little patio out back, the fried chicken was good but not as great as I had heard "some people say it's the best in the city"
Wonderful food. It's always busy and a fun environment.
Expertly cooked food
Unique and fabulous flavor combinations.
Best food in andersonville.
Absolutely amazing food.  The boucherie board is the best I've ever had.   Brunch was also among my favorite in the city with well planned, balanced and creative offerings.
Get anything pickled.  ANYTHING.   It's one of those moan at the table kind of places.
Food is excellent
Food was unique and very good. Waiter a little anxious to turn the table and did not ask if we wanted a brunch cocktail.
The place is small but the food is very good....

The food here is phenomenal. Stopped by for lunch but if you're planning to come for dinner definitely make reservations. They are popular for their fried chicken, it's very crispy and tasty. The side that come with it are okay. Order the tete de cochon it's really nice with the bread and pickled shallots.
One of my top three restaurants in Chicago. =)
Great brunch menu! Reservations can be helpful.

Big Jones is an excellent restaurant for dinner as well as brunch. The shrimp and grits is a classic dish. The omelette and corn griddle cakes were rich in flavor, and reasonably priced. Complementary beignets were a nice touch. The classy but relaxed atmosphere of the interior adds to the Southern charm.

We decided to try this place for restaurant week.  The room was packed but because we'd made a reservation we waited less than 5 min... The staff was very friendly.  Food was fantastic and our server Kim was very helpful with helping us choose our dishes. Every recommendation and description was spot on!  Can't wait to come back
The have some of the best fried chicken.  It's made to order, but worth the wait
Great New Orleans food!

Top notch customer care. Sometimes you can assess the true caliber of a business not by their degree of success, but by how they manage complaints/problem customers. There was a fairly minor issue with one of our party's dishes. Our server and the management went above and beyond to make sure that the mistake was corrected and that we would leave happy. Beyond the one hiccup, the food was excellent and the service very courteous and attentive. They definitely earned our future business and recommendations.
It's not your typical soul food restaurant,  in fact I didn't find it to be soulful at all.
Food is 5 stars. Service is usually 3 so be prepared ahead of time
The cherry custard French toast was amazing!  Breakfast for three (with cocktails) was over $100 though.
Fancy Southern food in the middle of Chicago, also has a great cocktail list.
Nice flavors and perfect portion sizes.
Great food, nice service.
Lovely creole food.  Be sure to make a reservation because this place is well sought after.

My wife and I had a wonderful lunch. We tried the fry chicken and we tried the catfish and grits along with collard greens. Simply marvelous. The cornbread was good but not great due to it being overly soggy.
Best fried chicken ever

The food is always top notch. The service is excellent. This last experience compelled me to write a review though I hardly ever do.
We went there last Thursday night for a friend's birthday and were seated about 40 min late because of some stragglers. No big deal, just had a cocktail at the bar. Once we were the executive chef came out and took care of us himself! Love this place, will always go back.
Very friendly and helpful staff! Lovely decor!
Best Southern - style food in Chicago's Northside.

One of my favorite places in the city. Authentic New Orleans food and fantastic cocktails. A couple of must haves include the andoulie sausage, their hurricane cocktail, and you can't go wrong with the fried chicken.

Adequate - service was good, but food was merely ok - despite the imagination of some of the dishes, for the price and the portions of both food and drink, and the quality of cooking (at least how our dinners came out), you could do better elsewhere.
A hidden gem! Try it for brunch AND again for dinner. Both are winners.
Always good!!!!
Really good dishes. Great service.
Thoughtful southern cuisine in a cozy cafe setting.  Brunch is always popular with lines out the door.  Back patio in the summer.

Loved this place! My coworker suggested Big Jones for Saturday brunch and they didn't disappoint. Food was delicious and the waiter was attentive. The only downside is that they do NOT offer a pitcher of mimosas so you have to pay $8 per glass. I'd have rather paid $20 for a pitcher. Otherwise, great experience.
The food was just so so..it was a busy evening...thank goodness the weather was awesome the ambience was great the server was attentive and the Cubbies WON!
Probably the best southern restaurant in Chicago and its surroundings
I was not really into this but my girl love every bite of it. The service was most excellent though
Great food and great service!
Really cozy space and amazing food. Home made ice cream was delicious!
Really great southern food.  Totally authentic and excellent.
Great service and one of the best breakfasts I've had in a while.
If you don't develop an instant love affair with this place, there is something seriously wrong with you.
Not impressed

Service was OK.  Decor was OK.  Food was pretty bland.  Mediocre and not memorable.  We had gone there before and wanted to give them a second chance, since the bread had been good.  We wondered why this place had a lot of open seating and other places in Andersonville were pretty busy.  Didn't try the drinks.  Maybe they are good.

July 2017 - Just left the restaurant. I don't generally go on to review a place this quickly.  I took two co-workers out for lunch, spent $100.00 and was totally  disappointed. The gumbo and Kohlrabi Soup, delicious! We were not totally full and I wanted my co-worker,  who''s new to the states to get a decent experience. Southern cuisine ???? Who ever heard of Hushpuppies with cheese? Plus they were loaded with chopped onions.  The Hushpuppies were so heavy that butter would not help them.  I should have cancelled my Shrimp & Grits entree.  The Fried Chicken & Catfish entree was decent.  I would ask that you either lower the price for the Shrimp & Grits or just stop serving them. There was so much gravy, I had to spoon off a small plate full just to get to the grits.  I left a small tip for the waitress as she just seemed nonchalant and definitely not affected by  our experience. This is the type of restaurant if you're new, "Ask other patrons their suggestions."
Good food, good service. A little expensive for breakfast.

Cockroaches and fruit flies. My gf found a roach in the bathroom and the walls in the restaurant are literally crawling with fruit flies. The food was a huge let down. Biscuits were burnt and tiny, corncakes were also burnt. And for such small portions, its expensive. Our server was great though. DO NOT GO.
Incredible service and sumptuous food
Outstanding cocktails. Fantastic food. Super service.

The first word which comes to mind is "overrated". Friends invited me out for brunch here one Sunday morning after raving about it for months. We started with the beignet and if it hadn't been for the water I might've needed a Heimlich maneuver. Dense and dry. I ordered an eggs Benedict dish with Tasso ham over popovers. The ham was chewy and stringy and the only thing on the plate that had any flavor. Even the popover was flavorless and a bit soggy. My Bloody Mary tasted watered down. My friends ordered the Sally Lunn bread which may have started in the 13th century but it should have stayed there, too. Again, it was flavorless and the kind of bread your 9yo might have made that you'd be obliged to choke down. A theme was developing here. Next came the spoon bread but "bread" is a bit of an overstatement. It did have an interesting taste and a consistency similar to a soufflé but without the richness. A friend had a roast mushroom dish that was decent. They didn't screw up roasting mushrooms. The dessert was ok but not memorable. In fact, I can't even remember what I had. At that meal the coffee was the best part. Big Jones is the kind of "local" centric restaurant more concerned with the sourcing of the ingredients they use than with the taste of the food they produce. It's with no exaggeration I say eggs, hash browns and pancakes from Denny's would have been more flavorful and satisfying. With such concern over ingredients it's almost impressive to assemble a collection with so little flavor. My first suggestion to the chef would be... salt. Use it. I tend to trust the opinion of at least one of my friends who agreed it was an "off" day. She also privately admitted she likes it far less than her husband. I'd probably give it another chance but not if I had other options. Reading through the reviews posted here it's the critical ones which ring true to me. I'm not one to be influenced by fads and hype.

Best cornbread I've ever had.  The crab cakes were also very tasty.  For entrees we got the fried chicken which was very moist. GF got the pork duet which was very tender and full of flavor. Been here twice and would definitely come back. I have dreams about that cornbread!

Also note: we came in on a Saturday around 7pm.  No wait and we were seated immediately.

Just visited this weekend for the first time with another couple.  There on their gift card and none of us knew what to expect.  It did not look impressive as we entered - plain design, wood tables, old store front.  We were seated in the rear (patio was full) where it was quiet, and I was having doubts.  Then it turned out the very friendly and attentive waitress could describe all the tap beers with attention to detail usually seen with wine, and provided helpful descriptions of the menu that were right on.  Never had venison hash canapés before and thought it was a little pretentious, but turned out wonderfully delicious.  I would have been happy to make five of them a meal.  Two orders of shrimp and grits which she correctly assured us we would love, and two orders of clearly genuine shrimp etouffee, followed by sorbet with the blueberries mashed into it.  They clearly have their own ideas about the best way to make these dishes so some traditionalists might balk but we four older folk loved it.  And no one rushed us.  Nothing buy clean plates.
Nice new renovation, great drinks. Food was a bit salty so minus a star. Great place for Friend and Family gatherings
Bland!!!  Had a gift certificate and went with my Louisiana bf and have never eaten at a place so determined to stamp out flavor in their drinks and food.  Service was fine.
Waited 30mins and never received our drinks. Had to get up and leave.
Food was good; staff was very polite and helpful.  Unfortunately it was quite noisy and could stand to be freshened up.
delicious food and friendly people!
Loved the fried chicken!  Shrimp and grits were really good also. Keith was a terrific server!  Will take friends next time!

I am from Georgia and this is the one place in the city that I feel gets southern for right. They have a ton of gluten free options and their sweet tea is on point. Any meal you have here will be amazing, but I highly recommend their breakfast/brunch.
Ok food. Beer selection not that great
Great fried chicken
It is very important to me to give my business to a place that respects others and their employees. Management here has little respect for both. Never going here again.
Almost 4 stars except service was so lacking genuine enthusiasm. Food nicely prepared and flavorful, but repetitive.
Their crab-wrapped-in-trout special was amazing!
Great food
There aren't a lot of options, and I personally don't enjoy the food. My parents do, though, so it makes it worth coming here with them.

Weekend brunch and Monday night dinner ("industry night") at Big Jones are two of the most enjoyable meals you can experience in Chicago. The menu rotates seasonally and showcases some beautiful examples of Carolinas and Cajun cooking. It's also surprisingly friendly to people with gluten sensitivity, including some of the pancake dishes.
Trendy, delicious Southern/New Orleans fare.
Damn delicious
Great food
Amazing food and drinks, with a relaxed but elegant atmosphere. Perfect for a special occasion or date night. Believe the hype about the fried chicken; it's some of the best I've ever tasted.
Good good, nice ambiance, but not sure it was worth the wait

My biscuits were burned and my gumbo ya ya tasted like burnt gravy. The cheese grits were good but lacked flavor.  As a Louisiana girl,  I think I expected more flavor,  however,  after reading the description that this restaurant is "the chef's take on southern cooking", I realized that I got what was promised. My server was nice and responsive.  Management did not charge me for the items I didn't like,  however,  mgmt never came out to greet me or apologize. Most of the tables were open during my visit.  I will not return unless I am visiting friends in the area who insist we go 🙄
Good southern food, and cocktails too
New Orleans NORTH!!
Great food and service, with a well-stocked bar.
Great place and food, really nice waitress, southern type cooking, I really liked the fried chicken.  Prices are $15 to $25 about for entree
Fantastic brunch. Sat at the bar, chatted with the friendly bartender, ordered hot booze, and then the food arrived. Slightly comatose. Worth it. If you're in Chicago, come here.

Normally when I go to Chicago one of the things I look forward to is going out to eat.  Most restaurants don't disapoint, Big Jones did.  The shrimp and grits was not what the waiter said. He talked me out of the pulled pork and he told me, after i was very specific about the sauce not being over grits.  In fact it did.  There was I think 3 or 4 shrimp and the grits were lumpy. It tasted blah. My wife ordered a Manhattan Long island tea and at first they brought her unsweetened tea.  Then after we told them again, I was facing the bar, and watched the bar tender as she was making it, taste it and make a weird face.  The drink tasted awful and my wife just mixed it with the actual tea to make it palatable.  The food took over one hour to come.  I would of gave it one star but my wife's fried Chicken was actually good.  Appetizers were also so so.
Good food, great birthday dinner.

I usually try to eat here at least once per month and I'm starting to realize that maybe that's a bit too often...  over the last couple of years their food has gotten disappointing.  Appetizer portions are tiny and very expensive considering how much food you get for the price.  Same goes for the main dish as well - no fried chicken should cost $17+, and I don't know where the chef came from but maybe he should look-up chicken and dumplings  (it should not be a soup - or if it is, describe it on the menu as such).  I think I'm not the only one that feels that way since during my last few visits there was almost nobody else at the restaurant during lunch.  Also, there's no parking there so next time you think about going there, maybe you should try Calo right next door instead.
Boucherie board

It's good food, but kind of hipster for what should just be southern comfort food.  I don't need fancy expensive biscuits and gravy, I just want some hearty, delicious white gravy on fluffy tender biscuits.  That's not what you get here.

Beignets come with the food, though, which is pretty rad.
Well-prepared and well-served.
Tasty southern style food. Came for brunch and sat at the bar with no reservation. Service was prompt and food was delicious. The Benedict was fabulous !
The biscuits and gravy brunch was excellent

Big Jones is our go to for a special dinner, brunch and quiet weekday lunch. I’m so thankful to have such a wonderful dining option in my neighborhood. I’ve been coming here since they opened and quality has always been consistent. If you are looking for some incredible fried chicken, a burger that is out of this world, or an inventive dish like homemade oatmeal with potted duck and local peaches and berries- you’ve found a great option.

We never venture up to Andersonville because it's such a hike to get up there from the west side, but this weekend was Andersonville Midsommar Fest and we figured what better excuse to try out Big Jones!

And I'm glad we did, because the brunch was delicious. It competes with some of the best brunches I've had in New Orleans!

First things first, the Eggs New Orleans! Don't think, just order! Jordan and I split the Eggs New Orleans, which is a MASSIVE dish! It's like eggs Benedict, but exponentially better, because instead of serving the poached eggs on top of boring English muffins, these poached eggs are served atop popovers and crab cakes, SERIOUSLY!!! It was hugely delicious! It's even come with a side of crispy hash browns!

I was also impressed with the Bloody Mary, which had excellent flavors! It has a horseradish kick, but nothing too spicy and is served with asparagus, pickle and pickled okra. And also surprised by the complimentary order of beignets (in place of bread). They were so sweet, so light and so airy... Comparable to Cafe du Monde!

This brunch is great! Big Jones is closer than New Orleans, so next time I have a craving, I guess I'll head up to Andersonville instead!
If you want to wait twice as long as the anticipated wait for some overrated food and overpriced drinks come here.

I've only had brunch there and will try and go back for dinner, but brunch was awful. My shrimp and grits (or something and grits maybe sausage) was insanely salty. I couldn't finish my food it was so salty. My boyfriend's food was mediocre. My coffee ran out before my food arrived and I never got my refill.

The food was hit or miss - mostly good, although I thought the French toast was overly sour, my partner loved it. The country white bread and spoonbread were both delicious, as were the spreads and preserves that came with it. Unfortunately the service was so unpleasant I would not return. I want to emphasise that I am very easy-going as far as restaurant service goes, but these people were truly awful. They took the plates away as we were still taking the last bites of food, and reached over us while we were eating to take a plate that was still being eaten off of - AFTER I said "Dude!" and *tried to block the bus boy from touching the table * We felt very unwelcome, and I for one would not return. And we were seated in the back of the restaurant, which was more than half-empty when we arrived, so I don't think they had that much need to turn tables. And even if they did, there was no excuse for how rudely we were treated. Again, the food was good, I think the French toast was a matter of taste, and if the service was better I would have wanted to return and try something else. But I was unhappy enough with the way we were treated that I will not be going back.
Good soul food and craft cocktails.
Very good!
Brilliant food and awesome cocktail program

Really disappointed with our experience on NYE. I had been checking out the menu earlier in the day and was really looking forward to the chicken and some of the other starters. We arrived to find out there was a prefix menu with not so appetizing options.

The risotto starter and biscuits were amazing but then things fell apart with the salad.  The butter lettuce salad was really lame. No dressing at all and the lettuce was really wet.  The sea bass was really undercooked and not so great.

I hope to be back and try the chicken but so far not such a great first impression.
Great food

On the pricey side but worth every penny. Both the shrimp and grits, and the catfish and grits were amazing. The skillet cornbread should not be missed. The persimmon pudding for dessert was everything I want in a winter dessert - warm, sweet, and full of baking spices. I can't wait to go back.
Excellent service, outstanding food, cozy environment. Easily the best meal I've had in the last year. Highly recommended. Our bartender Jennifer was a joy to talk to and had great suggestions.

Big Jones makes some amazing fried chicken! Their cocktails are delicious as well. Service is good & the atmosphere is pleasant. It is a smaller restaurant, so you will want to let them know if you have big party!
Great place for brunch

First off, excellent staff. I cannot say enough about the bartender who was mixing wonderful drinks, was very friendly with a sense of humor, very knowledgeable about the menu as she walked us through it. Now the food. Absolutely excellent. Had the fried green tomatoes, crab cakes and the smothered pork chop with candied yams and collard greens are all highly recommended. But the highlight was their fried chicken, possibly the best I have ever had. Most certainly will be back to try other things on the menu as this was my first time there.

I can't say enough great things about this gem. Great food. Great people. Great experience. The fried chicken is award winning for a reason! The libations are a must try. This place is not to be missed. Andersonville is full of hidden treasures but Big Jones stands above the rest.
Great food fun place good service
Love this place
Great service, food was just ok.
Always good food!!! We love Big Jones!
Always love the food here. It never disappoints.
Great Restaurant Week menu
Awesome menu of truly authentic Southern recipes, rivaling those of my ex, a Cajun  from SW LA
Great selection of different flavors. This place is always crowded.  I love the fact that it's open late so I can head right on over when I have late night craving.
Line goes quickly and they except credit card.  First time to Mitchell's and it was a nice treat.  Flavors are unique and will return in the future.

The waitress that found our seat was extremely rude, making us wait for her to finish a phone call about a food allergy instead of seat us, and in my experience face to face customer interaction supersedes all else. The food was also not an accurate representation of flavor from New Orleans. It fell flat, drinks were much too sweet and they only serve beignets on the weekend at brunch, again no representative of the NOLA way.  In branching out to put their own spin on New Orleans classics, they lost their way.
We wnt for Mardi Gras so they were super busy, but we still had excellent service, and everything was delicious!  We will definately be back, maybe for brunch for the free beignets!
The drinks and food were good. The bartender (Jennifer) was extremely knowledgeable and helpful.
Intimate, a rustic country charm in a big city. I came for brunch and it was divine. I highly recommend it as there is enough for those who prefer sweet or savory fare.
The chicken and biscuits is to die for!

I came to Big Jones for restaurant week and had a great time. The restaurant had a great atmosphere, it was intimate and a good spot for conversation. My friend ordered a cocktail and he really enjoyed it while I ordered a great gose beer that I had never tried before. The food was great my friend and I ordered different entrees so that we could try each other's food and everything was great.
Great white meat fried chicken. Pimento burger was outstanding. Whiner Miaou on draft.

Recently I saw an article naming them one of Chicago's best fried chicken sandwiches. I had to try, so I stopped in on a Saturday afternoon and they have a couple fried chicken items on the brunch menu. The Sweet & Spicy Fried Chicken on a biscuit with grits is the ticket! Wonderful service, in a very cozy place.
presentation was nice but don't order the specials
Such good comfort food. Loved the brunch.
Atmosphere was good server's great and friendly food was ok enjoyed the pickle tasting appetizer

Tasty food, cute place, but really lackluster service. Told 60 minute wait, waited 2.25 hours. Then they ran out of the chicken which is what we came for. Waiter forgot things, busboys never cleared plates from our appetizers, just overall disappointing experience as service spoiled an otherwise good meal.

Their fried chicken is the best in the city.  It’s a bit of a drive from my house, but worth it.  They also support local farms. Everything is quality and made from scratch.  The effort comes through on the plate.

Not southern but a bad Chicago version of something else. Grits were not good, pieces of corn husk in them and they lacked flavor,  the portion sizes are also suspect, the chicken and dumplings gravy was okay but lacked any depth and the dumplings were flavorless. They called it coconut cream cake, what it was, a brunt doughnut with some flavorless cream cheese in the middle. I was raised in the north but have lived and traveled the south for 20 years, this place is an embarrassment and should not call it self southern in any way. On a positive note the staff was nice.
Had great carry-out, looking forward to dining in
I was very underwhelmed.
Great food & very attentive service. Everyone left satisfied!

I've been here a couple of times I am a big fan but it does Target a specific crowd they do have a preset menu on some occasions as well as their natural menu is not that big. But they do have a great alcohol menu you can always find something new and unique their food is definitely Top Notch I would say one of the better places in the area
Excellent for brunch. Fried chicken lives up to its reputation. Best grits I've had in a while. Good cocktails that are legitimately worth the price.
Some of the best southern food I've had outside of the South.
I got the pimento cheese burger, highly recommended it! It is a lot of food!
Great southern brunch.

Been wanting to go to Big Jones for brunch a long time, and it absolutely lived up to the hype. Nice and spicy Bloody Mary, Eggs New Orleans (blue crab cake Benedict), and fried chicken biscuit were all excellent. The fried chicken lives up to the billing. Highly recommend.
Great service and above average food.  The calamari was slightly below average for me.
Great food and really friendly staff. However, no changing table in the bathroom! The bathrooms were really cold as it is, and then I had to change my son on the even colder floor.
Yum!! You can't go wrong...from brunch to dinner...this place is a winner!

The food was freakin amazing! The highlight of our meals were the bacon on a salad. They butcher and process a hog once a month and make their own bacon and as well as other stuff too. It was the best bacon I've had!! The rest of the meal was great also (fried chicken, collards and black eyes peas). The free whiskey pour was Knob Creek, it was good too. Ask for a whiskey society card. There are many perks with it.

I write this with a heavy heart. My partner and I love Big Jones, but last night was disappointing. Ordered the burger and made sure to ask about the serving temperature. “Medium,” the waiter replied, as I hoped. He said he would tell the chef. But that was just lip-service. No gesture was made to reconcile the issue. As a former chef and restaurant manager, this is failure at the 101 level. I will mention that we did not say it was anyone's birthday but I still found it unacceptable for someone who made an early reservation days in advance.

Food: I was hoping the food would make up for our experience but it didn't. To make it easier I will break it up by individual dish.

Cocktails: this was the best part of the meal. The NOLA 75 was a perfect burst of citrus and the cava balanced the drink well so it wasn't too sweet.

Cornbread: We had this as an appetizer and  it was decent. I wish it was cooked longer because it was a touch under baked. There is real corn in it which I enjoy.

Chicken and Dumplings: This had a great flavor and the dumplings were done well. The problem was that it was just in a broth which is not real chicken and dumplings. It also had clearly been sitting under the heat lamp for too long.

Light Fried Chicken: The texture of this dish was amazing. Crispiest crust I have ever had and the checked was tender. With that being said, it lacked flavor. I have had much better tasting chicken around Chicago for a much cheaper cost and also in a greater quantity. The hype this dish up to much. The best fried chicken I've ever eaten. Ditto for the cornbread baked in a tiny cast iron skillet: light and flavorful with just the right amount of crustiness. (I'm saying that as someone who grew up with a Kentucky hillbilly stepmother who was a terrible cook in general but somehow pulled off dang good fried chicken and cornbread.)The sweet potato hash was savory with the salty smokiness of high-quality bacon permeating every bite, the cubes of veg a perfect not-too-mushy texture. The greens were mm-mm good. But back to the chicken: brined to add flavor and retain/add moistness (sorry to those of you who cringe at the word moist), then dredged before being pressure-fried in "leaf lard, ham drippings, and clarified butter," all four pieces in our shared half chicken were crispy on the outside, tender and uniquely flavorful on the inside. We had a very horrible experience at Big Jones on February 26, 2019.  The staff seemed overwhelmed with the full restaurant they had that evening. We were sat in a table only to be moved 10 minutes after sitting down because they needed the table for a bigger party coming in. Not a big deal but our waiter failed to see that we were moved and no one came to our table to even get a drink order. Turns out we didn’t have a wait person so the bartender came over to get our drink order. Even then it took about twenty minutes to get our drinks. He then told us about the special menu and soups they were offering that evening and we placed our order. We decided to split a few things and he went and placed our order. Our food started to show up in the wrong order from how we placed it and the woman who was running the food was very annoyed that we wanted our salads and soup before our entrees. She even brought the wrong soup and told us they didn’t have the soup that we ordered on the menu. As it turns out they did have that soup but our waiter put it into the order system wrong.

The soup was their gumbo and it was so burnt it was inedible. The salads we got had so much dressing on them that the lettuce was floating in dressing. That wasn’t even the worst part about the meal. When our fried chicken finally arrived,  the same food runner/manager who brought the soup stood at the table and very sarcastically asked if this was the right time to bring the chicken. At this point we had enough of Big Jones and asked for a check and to give us a container to take the chicken home.  The manager did come back to the table after realizing her rude behavior and comped the meal. We didn’t ask to have it comped but none the less she did.

Chances are it won’t be opened for very much longer if the staff continues to treat their customers like we were treated last week.

Not exactly the busiest time of the day or week, so we expected a better experience. It was one of the coldest days of the year, and we were the first and only diners in the place. They put the four of us at the very worst table, given the weather...right behind the hostess stand at the front door. We asked to move and the hostess did at least promptly accommodate us.

We then waited ten minutes for drink orders and another 20 minutes to get the drinks. By that time, there were ten people in the restaurant. We all finished our drinks before our server came back to take our food orders.

At this point, we could have each eaten an arm, so we ordered the skillet cornbread and biscuits as starters. We got them less than five minutes before our entrees arrived.

Most of our party thought their entrees were adequate. I got the shrimp and grits which I thought was watery and flavorless.

As we were finishing up, our server asked if we wanted dessert. We said, sure, let's take a look at the menu. We waited another 15 minutes before our server returned and asked if we wanted dessert. We said, well we haven't seen the menus, so no. Check please.

We need more southern-themed restaurants like this place. The skillet cornbread was great, the chicken and dumplings better than that, and the dessert - chocolate creme brulee, IIRC - was even better than that. Just outstanding.

I came here with family when we visited the Chicago area. The reviews were great and we were all excited to try the food. I was disappointed by the lack of attention, how much time it took to make the food, and the taste/quality of the food.

We arrived at Tahoora at 0955 and were told that they are opening in five minutes and to come back at 10am. This was not a problem, my family was expecting them to let us be seated at least, but I didn't make it a big deal. We walked over to a Dunkin Donuts, had some coffee and walked back.

We got back to Tahoora at about 1040. There were three men that I could see behind the counter. One was sitting in a chair by the register, another was cleaning the dessert display, and the third was not facing us and on his phone talking to someone. I don't believe there is any way that they did not notice a large group if 18 people (14 adults, two kids, two babies).

After about two minutes of deciding what we want, we walked over to the counter as a group. The man sitting in the chair walked to the back of the restaurant where the kitchen was when he saw us approaching. The man cleaning the dessert display looked at us, then walked to the kitchen area as well. The only person left was the man on the phone. He acknowledged us and indicated that he will get to us in a minute. There were no other customers.

Another 10 minutes went by (not an exaggeration), someone suggests we go somewhere else but the parents insist we stay because they heard this place is good. Finally after almost 15 minutes we order our food.

I ordered a large gyro platter. My family ordered an assortment of food and drinks. My food came out about 40 minutes later and was not what I expected. It was all just chunks of gyro meat, no bread or veggies or sauce. We asked the man behind the counter and he said that I should have gotten the gyro sandwich. The menu didn't specify that the gyro platter does not come with anything. It cost $18 and was just gyro meat. I wasn't happy with that, but I was hungry so I just ate it. He told me that bread would be extra and asked if I wanted some, I said that ok as I didn't want to wait another 40 minutes for bread.

Everyone else's food and took between 50 minutes to one hour to be called. They forgot everyone's drinks so some of us waited again to make sure that the drinks are made (lassi, falooda, a few canned sodas).  They forgot my wife's sprite, so I waited in line 12 minutes to get my sprite. I even asked one of the guys behind the counter if I can just get a sprite and he rolled his eyes at me and didn't say a word. I was behind another customer, but still, it's a sprite I paid for that was not given with my order. Some of my family didn't get their lassi and falooda until 1150, over an hour after we got there.

Now the food. Mine was not great. The gyro meat was dry. I've always had greasy gyro meat in the past and never knew it could be dry. I would have asked for something else but the service and attitude of the staff here was just going to disappoint me again and I did not want to wait another hour for my food. The parents said their food was ok, most of the younger adults agreed that we would not be back.

I rarely leave a bad review, this could be my first bad review on over a year. My experience may have just been a bad experience among all the good reviews I read. I gave ot two stars instead of one star because the drinks were good. Unfortunately, I would not recommend Tahoora to anyone. There are much better places to eat in the Devon Street area with amazing service and a comfortable atmosphere.  Don't waste your time or money here.

The food is definitely on economical side, average item price was $8 and the total was $55. The chat, samosas and chai were flavorful and we enjoyed them the most. The zinger was of mighty size but lacking flavor. The hunter beef was lacking any vinegar/acid taste, so it was more like shredded pulled beef sandwich. The mayo garlic roll was below average, it had a ton of greasy mayo and big chunks of onions. The chinese rolls were very doughy and below average. Cheese kabab was average with barely any cheese inside. And Beef Khause is still in our fridge, haven't given it a shot yet. Overall, not my favorite place, and definitely not worthy a drive from all the way from Wisconsin. There are definitely other flavorful better options especially if you are coming from a distance (Hint: Chi Tea in Lombard).

Udipi restaurants in India are one of the supreme representatives of South Indian delicacies and we entered this place with a lot of expectations. I’m from Minneapolis and was in Chicago for the New Year weekend. Since my wife was feeling little under the weather and we had our lunch already in a different place, we wanted to just order a tomato soup to get her feel better and my cousins ordered filter coffees for themselves. I don’t have to stress enough on how much a filter coffee from a South Indian style restaurant is prominent and how much our expectations on this restaurant would have been. One soup and two coffees took their own sweet time to be served.

To our utter surprise the soup wasn’t hot and had chunks of bread floating on it. Adding to it, the breads weren’t even fried fully to look like croutons and quickly turned soggy. Like a sponge on water, the soup was soon absorbed and the bread croutons had become all bigger, hardly giving us any glimpse of the soup beneath it. Like rubbing salt on the wound, the coffee didn’t meet our expectations either and was another sour spot that we hit.

We called out our host and informed him that we were pretty disappointed with both the orders. While he was apologetic and offered a replacement with a different soup, he defended that the coffee should have been good. Since we were running shot of time, we were not in a position to wait for another 15 or 20 minutes for a soup and decided to pay for what we had(rather not had) and left the place.

I certainly hope that the place must have some enticing menu to offer, which we didn’t try our hands on, but to us get back to this place for a dining will definitely take some time.

I was there for lunch with my family on a Sunday. We ordered the following:

1. Pav Bhaji
2. Sev puri
3. Idli Vada Combo
4. Mysore Sada Dosa
5. Bhel (Jain)

All of these were like the equivalent of the paintings of exotic animals made by people who heard descriptions from travellers travelling to these lands.

I'll start of with the Pav Bhaji. Pav Bhaji literally means Dinner Roll with Vegetable curry. Technically, the Pav Bhaji at Uru Swati was exactly that: we were served dinner rolls with a vegetable curry. However, the vegetable curry was all wrong! I like spicy food, so I have no qualms about hotness of food, but all I could taste in the curry was the taste of powdered chilli. It's not bothersome, but its not what Pav Bhaji is supposed to taste like. Period.

Sev Puri is an Indian snack and to get an idea of what it's supposed to look like check the wikipedia pic (google wont let me post the url).
It also usually has gracious helpings of Onion, Potato, sweet and sour sauces, cilantro, mint chutney etc. Consequently, it has some heft to it (see wikipedia picture for reference). What we got was a sorry mess devoid of half the ingredients with tiny, TINY portions. which they charge you $5.95 for.

The Idli Vada Combo is served with Sambar and Coconut chutney. The Idlis are steamed rice cakes made from a fermented batter. The idlis were probably not allowed to ferment for long enough or had less rice and more peas in the batter, but they tasted off and lacked salt. The Vada on the other hand had slightly more salt than needed. The most offensive element was the Sambar. The Sambar needs to be at least mildly tangy, in addition to having other vegetables (shallots, okra, drumstick, eggplant, pumpkin, tomatoes etc.) and cooked split-pigeon peas as well as black gram lentils. Uru swati's sambar was neither tangy, nor did it have any veggies at all! This was basically a regular dal that was served in place of Sambar. Shameful!

The Mysore Sada Dosa is a dosa which is cooked with a red, dry chutney applied on one side while it's being cooked. Uru Swati's version was made with some random chutney which was essentially flavorless. This too was served with that travesty Uru swati passes off for Sambar.

I did not taste the Bhel myself but my mom-in-law that had it wasn't particularly impressed either.

Everything here tastes amazing, especially their fried pork belly and seafood dishes. The rice and beans are flavorful and, as far as I can tell, authentic and well-seasoned. The atmosphere is super fun and festive, and they do a good job of cleaning. Being here feels like I’m in a cozy, lively neighborhood in the heart of Colombia, with its plentiful and colorful decorations and upbeat music. The staff are friendly and attentive; always making sure you have everything you need. It’s a small family-owned business and you can tell they really care about quality. Pay no attention to the negative reviews left by people who don’t understand restaurant etiquette; almost all restaurants have last call for the kitchen about 30 minutes before closing. It’s unreasonable to show up with a big party right as the kitchen closes and demand full service. Maybe ask nicely if they can make an exception, but if the restaurant says they can’t accommodate you, it’s for a good reason! Equipment breakdown and deep-fryer cleanup take forever. Don’t be rude to the people doing their best in these difficult times. Not okay. Anyway, highly recommend this place. Give them a visit and make sure to try their sweet, crispy, perfectly-golden tostones or their flaky yucca fries!

Writing this review after trying to resolve issue amicably with general manager. GM has not responded to my e-mails, so:

My friend and I went to Rockwell's for some drinks and dinner. We've always been a big fan of your homemade tortilla chips (as the receipt attached shows). The establishment was not busy (in my opinion). We took a seat at the bar. It was a little less than normal until we were greeted (but no big deal).

I worked in the food service industry for 10yrs - in almost all facets (server, bartender, trainer, manager, etc ).

After placing our drink and appetizer order - we noticed a few patrons to the left of us had been waiting quite some time for some things and were growing upset. They eventually handled their business and left (clearly unhappy).

At the time, we didn't let it phase us. Why would we? Our app did take a bit of time but we had drinks and were okay. The app was great. Drinks were good. We placed our food order (had to request the bartender to do so, who I would later learn was the manager on duty...)

I ordered chicken strips (as receipt shows) and my buddy had a burger. It is no understatement when I tell you that our food took over 45 minutes. Being knowledgeable about the industry - I know these items take nowhere near that time BUT I did chalk some of it up to "maybe short staffed". We were excited to eat.

What happens now? I go to eat and my food is ICE cold. My buddies food was cold too - but he was starving and sucked it up. I, unfortunately, could not. It's evident our food got left in the window and somebody forgot to run it.

After contemplating if I would bring it up to anyone - I did. I brought it up to the bartender. I kid you not - this was his response: "I am sorry about that. Would you like me to remake it or I could microwave it for you". MICROWAVE IT?! ARE YOU KIDDING ME?! This is what you tell a customer?

I politely said "No, I am sorry. I do not want it to be remade as I have already waited 45 minutes and fear it will take just as long. My buddy can eat his meal and I will grab some fast food on the way home. I can't risk a long wait time again". He said "Okay Cool" and walked away.

I tried to let it pass, but was still shocked at the level of customer service I had just received.

As if it wasn't enough - he disappeared for 20 minutes. The couple next to us had no water and were growing antsy (as were we for our bill).

We got our bill and low and behold my items were still on the receipt. I leaned across the bar and spoke with the manager and stated "I do not feel as if I should have to pay for this meal when it was not acceptable" he stated "I can give you a box to take it home so you can eat it there"

Now why would I want to eat food at home... if I wanted to eat this cold mess I would have ate it within your restaurant. Take it home? It makes no sense.

After back and forth he agreed to take it off the bill - but could not comprehend how I had been inconvenienced (and still had not eaten dinner at 8pm by the time we left).

I am truly - one that does not complain. I understand the nature of the business and it's taxing. However, this manager is clearly incapable of basic customer sympathy and genuine customer service. He lacks any and all initiative and during our interactions, it was almost as if he was "slow". I am not sure if his "20-minute disappearance" was to go out back for a break.... but something was very off.

•	Service: Poor
•	Price: Average (reasonable)
•	Atmosphere: Below average (Crowded and a bit noisy when the restaurant has a full of customers, Cleanness of restroom)

I am still currently seeking the bastion of Korean food in Chicago. From many of my acquaintances, I have been told that this is the place in Chicago for Korean food, and  sadly, I felt my experience was very underwhelming.

Overall, this place is a small, very cramped, smoke filled Korean establishment and initially has the impression of being a great place. I would like to rate 2.5 but that will never happen. I went here with a few people and we ordered Mandoogook (dumpling soup), Pork Saam (marinated pork), bulgogi, and brisket. Do yourself a favor, go to your nearest Korean market and just buy the meat there, grill it at home, and have some soju with friends.

The place is a BYOB with no corkage fee and I must say, that is a smart move for a bbq joint. The mandoogook wasn't too bad, it had a robust beef taste in the soup, the dumplings had a distinct pork/tofu taste, and the rice cakes were cooked thoroughly but it still tastes like cafeteria food in LA for double the price. To be clear, LA Korean cafeteria food is generally pretty good to me.

For those of you wondering why there are about 10 little plates of food around you, those are side dishes (baanchan). It's about contrasting flavors, refreshing the taste buds, and diversity. The phrase "diversity is the spice of life" can be taken literally here.

Would I recommend coming here?  That depends. The lines are long, the crowd is boisterous and inebriated, and the place is a bit pricey. If you don't have access to Korean ingredients in your home or choose not to, I suppose you have no choice. If you know how to cook Korean food at home, stick to that. It's a fraction of the cost. Overall, it's better than other places I have had in Chicago but that really doesn't mean a whole lot. Korean food isn't a strong moving force here unless you count terribly made "kimchi" that has has bean sprouts in it.
