I felt like our experience was probably better because a member of our party was Korean and could speak to the waitress efficiently and ask questions. She ordered all of the food for us and I trusted we'd be getting good stuff. First up was all of the different kimchi, and they were really good. I think my favorite was a potato dish. Then came the seafood pancake. I should note, I'm not much of a seafood person. I was also especially hesitant when I heard there was octopus in the pancake. But hey, I'll try anything once. If I hated it, I could coat my mouth with more delicious kimchi. But surprisingly, I loved the pancake. Whatever they're doing is really great and I could eat the whole gigantic thing myself.
Next up were the meats. We got the unseasoned beef and the bulgogi. Two options for the meats were to either add green onions and a spicy concoction, or you could dip them in this sesame oil that had salt and pepper in it. I prefered the sesame oil. The meat was lightly seasoned and the sesame oil made it taste crazy delicious. I definitely need to try this new technique at home.
Then, when we were all about to burst from being too full, the waitress came by and put all of the leftover kimchi and other items into the BBQ and added rice to make a kimchi fried rice. It was amazing. I especially loved the burnt parts on the edges. I even had some fried rice to take home with me.
All in all, the food was over the top fantastic. We will definitely be back at some point when we know we aren't in any hurry and I'll probably end up ordering the same exact thing we got last time because it was so good.

For all people reading this review and saw the one stars or the 3 stars because they didn't get stellar service, do not expect to be wowed with service like western restaurants. The thing is, most authentic asian places are not service oriented, it is about the quality of the food and the price point. You can go to a downtown korean bbq spot where service is superb but expect to be paying more than $100 for the quality that you would get here for half that price! Food is really good and authentic. Place is so packed but do not let that deter you from coming. If you order bbq they will make a Kim chi fried rice on the table at the end. So a good tip would be to cook all the meat you have, dont immediately eat it and then ask for them to make the fried rice so you can enjoy with the meat. Pajeon is also really good!

Second time there the food was incredible but there was absolutely no service. Theres a difference between no service and terrible service, the latter being expected of any Asian immigrant owned restaurant because it's generally common in our culture, but when I say this place has no service I mean they have no service. 2 servers that also bus, host and cook for the entire restaurant. I saw a server once at the beginning of my meal to take my order and once at the end of my meal to bring me my check. Didnt get water, didnt get a drink order, didnt get rice, salt, lettuce leaves or any refills on our panchan even though I asked for them multiple times. I wasnt at all upset about the neglect of common courtesy but I was upset that I didnt get water or a salt shaker my entire fricking meal. It's a shame because the food here is the best I've found in the city and is ridiculously cheap compared to any other Korean restaurant in Chicagoland so I guess that's the tradeoff you get for no service.

Our annual trip to Chicago involves an annual trip to a different Chicago style pizza place…this year my wife’s sensibility wanting gluten free options won out which brought us to Chicago’s Pizza (The Lakeview location.) There are lots of gluten-free options including bread, calzones, pizza (of all depths) all made from their house-made gluten free-dough.

For gluten-full me I had two kinds of deep dish pizza to choose from…One is their stuffed crust (“what we’re famous for” our waiter said) which has an extra layer on the bottom with cheese in it. They also have a more traditional Chicago deep dish pizza and the crusts and sauces for both are different.

It was Memorial day Monday and we were the only people in the restaurant. They took good care of us.

I got their house extra crust/cheese pizza which very much looked like a traditional Chicago Deep Dish. The taste of the crust though wasn’t the classic buttery crust you’d get on the traditional deep dish…more like thick bread which isn’t usually what I’m going for on pizza of any kind. The sauce was super good though!

My wife thought the gluten-free was satisfying for what it was, though it had been so long since she had had a deep dish pizza that she couldn’t quite compare to the real thing. She did think the bottom of the crust in the middle was a little mushy but kudos to them for home making gluten-free dough and providing a legitimate experience to those with that diet, as opposed to so many restaurants that use frozen gluten-free dough.

The small pizzas, by the way, are actually quite large. It was way more than us little people could eat. (Especially getting 2, one gluten free and one regular.)

In the end I would have preferred the standard Deep Dish with the butter crust as that’s really what Chicago is all about whereas the stuffed crust is a little gimmicky and doesn’t offer anything special.

On their website it states that they have been perfecting their gluten free crust for many years and that it tastes almost identical to their regular pies. We decided to put that to the test.

I ordered a large 14" pie for myself and a 14" pie for him and we went to go pick it up. This was during the height of the 2020 pandemic so we were not able to enjoy the restaurant itself, but it was very nicely decorated and the cashier was very polite.

When we got the pizzas home, I noticed that my boyfriends pizza was placed inside of a special green pizza box with "GLUTEN FREE" on the top. This turned out to be very necessary because the two pies looked and smelled absolutely identical. Heaps of cheese, crust and marinara.

After slicing into my own pie, my boyfriend offered me part of the crust from his and I can honestly say that there was absolutely no difference between the two. The gluten free crust was just as flaky and buttery as the regular.

Keep in mind that there is a slight up-charge for the gluten free crust, but it is well worth it for the downtrodden, anti-gluten person in your group to enjoy a classic Chicago deep dish with you and not feel marginalized.

We will definitely be returning many times to Chicago's Pizza whenever we need to scratch that typical Chicagoan itch for our city's unique pie.

The color was grey and the cheese was definitely poor quality bagged shredded cheese. Side of fruit looked and tasted like it was cut days ago. You know how strawberries just get mushy when you cut them and leave them in the fridge for a day or 2? All the fruit was like that. We were one of 2 tables that were seated in the front of the restaurant and the waitress didn’t stop by one time the entire meal to check in or fill our coffee or water. I know it sounds like I’m ragging on these people but the service was really bad, and the dish I ordered was terrible. She did however ask why I didn’t eat the food and I was honest and said it wasn’t very good and she promptly took it off my bill. I would never ask them to do that I would have just accepted it, so they get points for at least realizing I wasn’t happy. The place is oddly decorated but that’s kinda their thing I guess. I don’t think I’ll be going back.

I tried the coleslaw, creamy and delicious and the potato salad was even unbelievable. I can't wait to order again this weekend. There goes my diet😂

Great Service and they fix your order as it should be. Will be back again.

THE BEST BARBECUE IN CHICAGO.  STAFF IS VERY NICE.
The food is Always Delicious

Cashier was friendly. Food was ready.
Enjoyed my tips n link combo!

The place is good, probably one of the better place on the south side of chicago. I ordered a small rib and tip combo. The rib tips are well seasoned and the sauce does not overpower the meat. They came clean off the bones and we're very tender. The hot links had good flavor but they were cut into pieces like bite size chunks. I would prefer a whole hot link.  The fries were there and they were just okay. The portion size was not bad for a single person but for almost $15 I would expect more for my money. I will go back to try the brisket and the ribs.

Tasty Tender food. The rib tips are seasoned and not over powered with sauce, its the perfect amount of sauce. The Links are juicy. Found this place searching the internet for a local  BBQ spot and I am glad we did. Friendly service and great food. We will be back soon
This place is amazing. These people leaving anything negative in the reviews are crazy

Best ribs on the Southside of Chicago.

Friendly atmosphere! Great tasting BBQ, matched with great customer service. The rib tips were cooked to perfection. The cajun sausage was well seasoned. Overall had a great experience and will be back to eat there again.
I need to remember that they take a while to pack things up, even when I've ordered a day before. So I need to call ahead before I start driving there. Love their hot links, great smoked chicken.
What BBQ restaurant run out of Ribs and Tips Blk ppl give the  worse service...
Authentic Barbeque, price is reasonable for portion size. Good customer service. Bring cash, card not accepted.

They where so nice 😅
And the rib tips and rib tips where off the chain. I the area was so nice. I will definitely be going back there again. Yes.

To me, going to the Bristol is like walking into the office of a job you're dying to quit.  You walk into the nicely decorated place full of people that you don't want to spend time with, you have a few awkward interactions, you wonder why your there, then you remember you're getting paid.  Normally, my first two experiences at the Bristol would have eliminated them from consideration for a repeat visit, but the food is just so good, I couldn't just up and quit it.
I LOVED this place. The food is amazing and the cocktails are gorgeous! Monkey bread, flat breads and all the cocktails are to die for. Will be back again and again. Hoping to hit up the brunch!
I don't know why they are still in business.
Great Mixologist. Small portions, but really good food. Great atmosphere. Cool little spot in Bucktown.
Great foodie option in Bucktown.  Very unique menu but quite tasty, although often very rich as well.  Get the homemade Nutter Butters for dessert - they are heavenly!

Unbelievable food. I'll never forget the pig's tail I had for my 29th birthday. Wow. And I'm not an avid pork eater. It was crispy, moist & delicious. Not what I expected.
They have great, knowledgeable servers at this foodie destination with craft drinks, fresh from the farm dishes with rich flavors. The menu is ever-changing except for a few things that remain like the Monkey Bread (amaze), Duck Fat Fries, Scotch Olives & homemade Nutter Butters (UNREAL).

What to order: Crispy Pig's Tail, Monkey Bread, Nutter Butters for dessert

Tip: The brunch menu is very small & all of the eggs are prepared sunny-side/runny.

I consider this to be and "industry" restaurant, a place where you will find a lot of cooks and servers on their days off. The food is simple but very good. This is the type of place where I would go for a Sunday night dinner and just order everything off the menu.  The dinning room itself is a little small but it still feels comfortable. The hand made pasta is really good, they usually have about five on the menu and you can't go wrong with any of them. When it comes down to it this is a good place for some really good food and a nice night out.
The chicken hearts are to die for! And the Basque cake is heavenly.

Great cocktails, great food, great service. Most of the dishes are meant for sharing, and the staff and kitchen always make sure to keep things paced at a comfortable rate. The menu changes daily, so if you see something that you really want, it's best to order it since it may not be back the next time you visit.

The food. OMG the food. I would eat the ravioli (singular–it's one large ravioli) for every meal every day if that was an option. The staff was also very accommodating when I planned my fiancé's birthday here, preparing a dessert to be ready when the meal was over without needing to order. Cannot recommend enough.

The Bristol is a great place for a cocktail at the bar.  The bartenders usually can make anything you want, experimental drinks and there's already an extensive drink menu.  The food is written on a chalkboard in the back (very cute) and is pretty decent.  I want to check out the upstairs, but I think it's mainly used for private events.

Great ambiance.  Amazing menu.  Monkey Bread is a must for an appetizer.  For dessert, the basque cake is mandatory to order.  Their drink menu has a very nice array of cocktails, with each one never disappointing.

very disappointed in the food. my expectation of this place was up the roof since it was only by reservation. however the service was phenomenal....but they really need to work on the food, one dish was too sour and the other one was too salty.
did not meet food expectation, food was too sour or too salty! i thought it would be better especially this was a reservation only.

I've been to the Bristol several times and each experience has been amazing. It's a go-to  venue for any special occasions. Usually we make a night of it and order many of their small plates and a bottle of wine. Some of our favorites are the duck fat fries and the order of their chicken. Definitely a must.
Went because of the pastry chef, Amanda Rockman. Worth it! But the entire menu was heavenly as well. A great, intimate place for a date night.

One of my favorite restaurants in Chicago. Creative menu that is always changing. The staples are amazing too though.  Don't miss duck fat fries, monkey bread or raviolo. After that, try something seasonal. Brunch is great too.
Really enjoyed the food. Seating was bit tight for a man of my carriage. Still, I recommend it.

As many restaurants as there are in Chicago I keep going back to The Bristol.  I love this place!  You really can't go wrong with anything you order and the cocktails are so great.  If you haven't been you must go.

Swanky spot to get stuffed, imbibe craft cocktails and have a good time. The menu is built to encourage sharing and you'll want to order as much as possible. The raviolo and monkey bread are a sweet combo, and the roasted chicken is simple yet amazing. Sure you'll spend a grip of cash but it's totally worth it.

One of my fav restos in Chicago. The atmosphere is so great and warm. Its inviting and always good food - no matter what. I prefer sitting at the bar and sipping on one of their many vinos. Make a reservation and go back often. It's just that good.

It's the little things. Everything here is lovely. The wine list is a perfect balance of geeky and accessible, and every dish on the menu sounds tantalizing. The savory monkey bread and roast chicken with dill spaetzle are both a MUST, and if basque cake is on the menu…oh, God.
I had a great time. the food was great. The cocktails too. One thing to be aware of is the price is more than the google user rating implies I'd put it at three or four dollar signs.

I came here for an early dinner, and hung out at the small bar for a couple drinks. The cocktails were perfect for the food they were serving, and the bartender is willing to put something together if you can't find a drink on the menu.

The food was really good, and I particularly enjoyed the bone marrow. It has to be one of the most generous portions in the city, and is right up there with Longman's. This is a nice spot to bring a date and relax.

I went here with a friend and we really enjoyed it. We started with a couple of cocktails which were great. We split the monkey bread, apple salad, and half a chicken; all were really good. It was definitely enough food for us; I even took a little of the chicken home. I will definitely be back.
Great food and ambience . small plates but rich in taste

I've been here 3 or 4 times over the years. It is a bit fancy, which means a bit pricey, but the food is really good. It is a smallish restaurant that feels super comfortable and the wait staff knows there stuff.

Took me a while to finally go to The Bristol and am now angry it took me so long to pull the trigger on a trip there.

I love sharing and they nail the shared plate concept.  The menu changes quite a bit but their constants are there for a reason.  That chicken and ravioli is so good.  Also, their monkey bread is a great way to start the meal.

As for cocktails, definitely try the Black Diamond...really good.

*Sigh*...I think you really have to be an ultra foodie or be trying to impress someone to enjoy it here.  I enjoy fine tastes on occasion, but the dishes were small and overpriced even for Chicago nouvelle cuisine standards.  Add to that the music that is a little too loud to hear your conversations and lights that are a little too dim to see the menu in front of your face, and you are left with an uncomfortable experience.  I gave redemption points for the cocktail menu, which was creative and well poured.
Amazing food, great service, beautiful space.

The menu looked good, but the food was a disappointment. To say disappointment is an understatement. I can only think that the chef from the previous reviews must have walked. My chilaquiles were really just tortilla chips with a chili that tasted reheated and too thick. The egg was cooked poorly with a runny white and a slab of bacon was oddly placed on the side of the dish. The peach coffee cake was sad and too dry on the outside while too wet on the inside. Overall I expected so much better.

Had brunch her Sunday morning. We made reservations which I highly recommend. A little disappointed in the menu selections. I'd say heavier on the lunch type savory meals less on the breakfast side. The cinnamon roll was amazing to share and I got the hangover breakfast which was amazing roman with everything you could think of in.  I'm not sure I will be back though because I prefer more breakfast food choices for brunch.
Such good cocktails! And really good meats!

Zagat nailed the review when they said "everything is delicious".  Thanks guys for a happy birthday & Sunday brunch, we really enjoyed ourselves. Staying open past closing time was an additional level far and above the 5 star service we received.

The pasta was hard. Not sure if that was the chefs choice but we ordered the fafalle  and raviolo  and both pastas were very firm/hard. The other flavors on the pasta was very good but the pasta itself was was hard.
Less "every part of the animal" under the current regime, but food is equally good.  An added bonus, it now accepts reservation!
Food was fine, service was terrible.

Best item there - Amish Chicken 6/5. Like the Kobe Beef of Chickens. Some of the most tender and moist chicken that I've ever had. I had always figured well-raised meat would taste excellent, but have never had the opportunity. My parents raise spoiled little chickens in the backyard (they feed them sashimi-grade fish) and their eggs are always some of the most amazing, creamy things ever - which has always made me wonder how the chickens themselves taste. So thank you Bristol for fulfilling my curiosity without having my parents disown me for eating one of their precious little ones.

Waygu tartare - 5/5. Melt in your mouth. With toasted bread that was firm but not too hard.

Raviolo - 4/5. The pasta is very thick and there's a lot of brown sugar butter on the outside. Inside had a slightly overdone egg yolk (looks like it hit the stage of gelatinizing and the egg yolk didn't really run). Very good dish but it was a bit too rich - and I wish the pasta was a little less chewy and firm, and that the egg yolk ran :(.

Duck fat fries - 3/5. Really good fries but just tasted like... really good fries.

Cocktails: If you like boozy negronis and manhattans, I highly recommend the Vieux Cruex. Extremely well-balanced and not as "put hair on your chest" as the the silician manhattan, which is more smokey. Can't remember what my husband had - a beer and some other cocktail, but I also can't remember how they tasted.

Oh and service was awesome. The waitress was spot on with her recommendations (I like to ask people what they prefer, since they usually have tried everything on the menu). She checked in often.
Great service, good food.  Would return.
solid meal.
Amazing brunch for mother's day.
I've been here a number of times and it is still going strong after many years. Excellent food with a dynamic menu. Get the duck fat fries.
Neighborhood feel, chef prepared food, great beer and wine selection and awesome cocktails.  it is a favorite of ours!
Great dishes that are fun to share. Not to mention great cocktails and an awesome wine selection!
My family has been going here for years and it gets better every time!  Try the raviolo and duck fat fries.  They also make mean cocktails.  I love the Moscow Mule!
Monkey bread is back!  Chef Pandel is in the kitchen!  Love it!
Went to Bristol for their Valentine's Day prix fixe, and it wasn't too bad! Definitely hard to get a table, but that's a good thing.

Hands down the best Burger in Chicago. This place flys under the radar but it's so good. The suggested family style eating if we went that route we would have over ordered 3 more dishes. If you are here try the burger!
Great cocktails.  Solid date night location.

Good food and good hours but I experienced a pretty long wait time for food. This place also has very low lighting, which I didn't mind, but I went with my parents who had a hard time reading the menu. The noise level here is also high, and it was hard for me to hold a conversation.
Cacio e Pepe and hangar steak were both delicious. Good wine menu too
A very knowledgeable winestress led us down a path of delicious reds. Fantastic chicken liver mousse, great beets.

A Bucktown staple. The roast chicken is a true Chicago classic
Love this place. It;s a neighborhood higher end restaurant where I'd grab a bite and drink every weeknight. Drinks are especially solid.
Great brunch. Food is always solid. Reservations recommended
The food is excellent and the atmosphere is cozy.
One of the best in Chicago.  Food is consistently amazing, service is great.  Awesome to see it so packed after this many years.
One of our favorites. Consistently great food time after time. The raviolo is delicious.
Amazing food, one of our favorite restaurants in Bucktown.

Aside from the excellent food, the wait staff and bussing crews were second to none. I left to use the restroom and they folded my napkin. My water was never below half a glass.

Only downside is tight dining quarters but that seems to be direction most modern places are headed. Cocktails are worth the money.

Also tried the smoked ham and eggs benefict, better then the chicken but eggs were overcooked and not runny. Very dissapointing.
Simple but flavors full. Almost perfect every time I visited if food more consistent on seasoned.

Nice atmosphere, but amazing food. On the host's recommendation, I order two things I could not possibly like: Brussels sprouts and pigs ears. I was not prepared to discover how delicious they were.

Terrific cocktails, too!
Great food and drinks, needs light in stairway to second floor

Been here twice now once for brunch and another time for dinner. We had a large group for dinner on a birthday party and they were very accommodating since it's a pretty intimate place. I have yet to try anything on the menu that isn't tasty.
Great atmosphere. Great tasting food. Interesting drinks. Only complaint, it's expensive for the size of meal. This was what $14 bought me. Tasted great, left hungry.

I'm not a fan of runny eggs so the waitress told us to let the raviolo sit for a few mins to finish cooking after they served it. Was very good with the ricotta filling. Burrata dish was great with the pesto and candied grapefruit peels. recommend the elderflower vodka drink. The painkiller drink is good and tastes like a lighter and less sweeter version  of a piña colada. Dessert-cake was delicious- it's an almond cake.
Good and friendly service, nice atmosphere, good food.

The food is delicious! We went for brunch. Unfortunately we had to wait to be seated, even with a reservation, and had to wait quite a long time for our food. They may have been short-staffed in the kitchen that day. Our server was very nice, brought us another round of drinks on the house, and the manager apologized and gave us some gift certificates because of the wait. Both nice gestures and appreciated.
Incredible food, wonderful dining experience and atmosphere. One of my favorites I've ever visited. Absolutely incredible!
Food is fresh and delicious.  Homemade pasta is amazing.  Service is always delightful
Delicious!
If your okay over paying for potatoes, eggs, and bacon- then this is the place for you. Yes, it's hipster and has a swanky touch but don't be fooled, it's breakfast.
The 🦆 fat fries with aioli is very good
Had the fried egg BLT with duck fat fries, which was pretty awesome. A little pricey, but you get a good amount of quality food.
This place was alright. It was very pricey and neither the food quality or portions lived up to the price tag.
Not bad

Used to frequent The Bristol regularly for the strong menu items and signature duck fat fries. Solid brunch. Most recently utilized their upstairs space for a private party where it was perfect for our group.

Absolutely love how they continuously upgrade and improve apartments. Since I’ve been in my apartment for past year they’ve replaced the roof , put in new windows, various safety upgrades they didn’t have too, and are completely upgrading and repainting everything.
They are not absent landlords but truly do care about their residences.
the service too slow and tasteless food

Tucked away in a small corner of Bucktown is this cute little restaurant-with-a-bar. I went here after a yelp event to check out the place. We sat at the bar, since even on a Monday they had no space- make a reservation!

The place is cosy, lots of wood, with dark walls and dark wood at the bar. I thought it was cool that there was a chalk menu on the walls, like in a number of German restaurants. We just had snacks, the duck fat fries and the monkey bread. Both are really good, I would recommend the fries for sure.

The place seems to have a number of European dishes, and doesn't mollycoddle people who dont know ingredients/processes by mentioning La Mancha and pain perdu. I would come here for date night.
Excellent food in a relaxed environment. Very attentive and well informed staff. Not cheap, but a good value. And easy street parking as well.
Delicious monkey bread with adventurous cocktail curated by Pablo.
Average in all regards. This is another exposed brick, Edison bulb, small plate copy + paste restaurant. I'm in no rush to return.

Went for early dinner, straight after opening. We didnt make a booking and that was no problem. By the time we left the place filled up, glad we went early enough. Food was pretty good! Here are my highlights: endives salad was pretty good, fresh, crunchy with manchego cheese and toasted pistachio. My fav was a combination we ordered by chance: crispy pig ears with the foie gras creamed spinach mixed with yolk on some yummy toast. It was perfection! At this point I was almost full. They recommend you share everything, portions are large. Pasta was in fact not, but it was the deal: tagliatelle bolognese with grana padano and parsley. It could have been made in Abruzzo up in the mountains. Def recommended. OK, at this stage I was full and we went there starving. We also had the apparently signature dish chicken, but we ended up taking it home.  For 2 hungry persons dont order more than 2 starters, 1 pasta and if you get a mains, you will probably take it home. Enjoy! Oh, nice restroom, bear in mind it is unisex though. They have L'Occitane products which is a lovely surprise.
Loved it! The Amish Half Chicken is to die for. Great cocktails as well
This is one of my favorite places to eat at. The atmosphere is relaxing and homey. My go to is the half Amish chicken. The servers have always been pleasant and I have never felt rushed.

Food poisoning.  Ate here and three hours later was throwing up until the next morning.  Pasta w/ seafood - probably shouldn't get this.  Also, the seating is too close and you can hear your neighbors conversation.  Got to listen to some lady cry about why she hasn't found a man yet...for the entire meal.  Not the most pleasant experience overall.  Service was good though, as was the beer. A little pricey. Won't be going back.
After almost 10 years still the best restaurant in Bucktown and one of the best in the city

The wine menu hosts a very good selection. The atmosphere is comfortable and cozy. It's great for a date. The menu was okay. I sent back a few appetizers. The service was great. If I could remember the waiters name I would call the manager and give him a compliment.
Went in for restaurant week. Absolutely loved the food. Service was good. Only complaint is the tables very close together. Gets loud quickly.
The food and service both deserve an excellent. Even with a very busy Restaurant week crowd we received personalized attention.

Absolutely Love Love Bristol.  I'd love it once more if the pasta portions were bigger. Smallest pasta portions I've ever seen but it is really really tasty and made daily! The burger and fries are the some of the best in the city. Crunchy duck fat fries and a farm fresh burger that doesn't require your desire of cooked level because they make it Perfect and juicy everytime! The drinks are strong also!! Great date place.  Or on the fly for great food! Very close to the 90 expressway.  Clean and upscale vibes right in the neighborhood!
The food is amazing! Plus Pablo the lead bartender has great customer service and his drinks are the best!
Really enjoyed the cocktails, in particular the Black Diamond. Small plates style, great atmosphere for a date, friendly staff.
Very good
The Basque cake was incredible! I would go back just for that.
Fantastic food. Never had duck like that before. Great mocktails (had a cold and wasn't drinking), loved the decor, great service.

In short: Get the Basque cake and duck fat fries - great for brunch!

Food: I’m usually a savory brunch type of gal, but the Basque cake won me over. We got it as part of the pastry board. It was perfectly buttery and just a hint of salty which paired perfectly with the vanilla bean pastry cream. The duck fat fries were addicting and I’m a sucker for a good aioli. We also had the mushroom toast, chicken n’ a biscuit and smoked pork hash. They were all good but the cake and fries stood out from the rest.

Service: I was really impressed with service here! All the staff worked incredibly well together to make sure our drinks stayed filled and our silverware was fresh. They were friendly and attentive even though it was Sunday brunch rush.
Loved the Basque cake. That is a must have if you go there!
Food and service is excellent.
Delicious and delightful
Fantastic food and atmosphere. Had the monkey bread, asparagus, and burger. All three were phenomenal.
Wow! Excellent cocktails, wine and food!
$15.00 for one ravoli and the waitresss didn't mention it was only one. Food wait time was long. Not worth the money
An always reliable and gracious Bucktown classic.
Brown butter Raviolo!!!
Above average fare (especially the starters!) Perfectly sized portions for sampling and sharing, as suggested by the friendly and helpful but not obsequious staff. A tad over-priced, however.
Had an interesting time here...

Love the food and the service. I've been here at least 5 times in the last couple of years and enjoyed it every time. They are always changing the menu and keeping things fresh. I want to specifically thank Jesus one of the managers for the way he handled a mistake they made. They accidentally assumed my significant other and I were sharing our entrees. So I had to watch her eat and then vice versa. Honestly I think it happened because of the way we ordered it. Anyways, Jesus came over and apologized very sincerely and offered my gf something to eat while I ate to make less akward. Then they gave us a desert to go for free. Lastly they gave us a gift certificate. These actions showed their dedication to make up for their mistake.  I would rate this as one of my best service experiences of my life. I've never been at a restaurant that really made an effort to make up for a wrong doing. You can't go wrong with this place, definitely give it a try.

The food is really tasty! We went for breakfast. Unfortunately, we had to wait to sit down, even with reservations, he had to wait a long time, our food. The next day they can be in the kitchen they are not strong enough. Our waiter was very good, brought us another vintage at home, the manager apologized and gave us some coupons to wait. Two handsome gesture and an appreciative. I love pie. If you go there, they are mandatory! The food is amazing and the wonderful lunch and atmosphere. My favorite. Simply unbelievable!
They have an amazing private space upstairs for events.
The Basque cake is the reason to go here. The service is great and so is the menu.
Fantastic

I absolutely love this place! The service is top notch. The food is always fresh, in season and so delicious. The staff is friendly and super accommodating. And they're located right off the highway, so it's a great place to stop for HH after a long day at work.

We started with the charred cauliflower, WOW!!!!! Amazing!!!! The yellow curry blended well with the cauliflower. Taste buds were extrly happy. Then the monkey bread with th dill butter was incredible (will definitely go back for more). We shared a couple of the homemade pastas. Incredibly flavorful sauces. Ended the night with their take on nutterbutter cookies with chocolate creme for dipping, OMG!!!! I used my spoon to dish out the chocolate. I highly Recommend the French press coffee! We will be going back & bringing friends!
Great food and great service!
Food was good as usual. Ambiance is loud but cozy. Wait staff can be hit or miss. Definitely a good spot for sharable plates.
Great place! Awesome experience!
Love this neighborhood gem
Foods are great.the dad's steak is real good plus great service.
A quiet comfortable place with interesting and delicious comfort foods.   Try the seared cauliflower appetizer.  The staff is terrific.

The staff is outstanding. When I couldn't eat the fries due to an allergy they brought me a monkey bread to snack on instead. AND when I could not pick a drink on the menu I described what I wanted to the waitress and the bar staff whipped it right up.
Wonderful atmosphere and food. Highly recommend.

This place had been a thing fora while, but I just dropped in for the first time recently. Food was phenomenal.  We split the cheeseburger and the white fish.  Noth were great, and the duck fat fries were a special treat.  But the standout breakaway favorite was the beat salad--don't miss it if it's available.  Will definitely be coming back!

The Bristol is one of my favorite restaurants in Chicago. The food is consistently wonderful and the cocktail, wine, and beer lists are always on point. Above all else, the service is unbeatable. The staff are attentive and charasmatic, and it's easy to feel at home. Alex (GM) and Pablo (Head Bartender), specifically, are awesome.

Finally, get the Basque Cake. Possibly my favorite dessert on the planet.

We went there on a Friday evening for Dinner.   We ordered family style.  It was nice to have a bite of everything, way to expensive for the quality of the food.  The steak tartare was spot on.  Everything else was average.   The cocktails were awesome!  Service was good.  With drinks and dinner it came to about $75 a person.   I’d rather had a meal that I wanted to lick the plate.  It was just ok food.  Gave it 4stars for the service and cocktails.   Feel it was too expensive for what we got.   Order individual plates and share if you want to.
Delicious cocktails and dinner. The black diamond was the winner for drinks and the duck liver mousse was the favorite appetizer.

We had a whirlwind, 9 week engagement and held our wedding ceremony and reception at The Bristol in late July.  It was a magical, amazing day.  We worked with Ashlei and Monica, Events Managers, and with the restaurant managers Jesus and Alex.  Everyone was prompt in their reply, attentive to detail, and extremely courteous to us and our vendors.  We ended up visiting about 4 times before the wedding to work out all of the details.  Our florist also visited several times.  They were more than accommodating to her, clearing their items off of shelves and taking artwork off of the walls.  They also met with our photographer about a week before the wedding.
The team problem solved with us when we talked about changing over the private space from the ceremony to the reception, with our music hookup, with a craft table for the kids, and with a few other concerns.  Ashei created a detailed BEO for me (she laughed because it was 10 times more detailed than most other events) and was patient enough to go back and forth with me several times before the wedding so that everything was perfect.
The day of the wedding is a blur, but it was flipping amazing.  The room was set up just as we had asked.  Ashlei sat with me before the ceremony and made sure that everything ran on time (we actually started everything AHEAD of schedule!) and then the event staff transformed the room for us.  The service was impeccable.  I had asked that the children be fed first, I had special requests in for vegetarians, we had special meals for the babysitter and the photographer, we had a request for no seeds for one table. The food.  The food was beyond amazing.  I can't even describe.  We had truffled deviled eggs, flatbread, and salmon carpaccio as passed apps.  During the dinner, we had monkey bread, an endive salad as starters.  We had a carrot sugo pasta, Amish chicken, and steak as main courses, and then the basque cake for dessert.  We served late night bites (duck fat fries and beef sliders).  All of our guests were full and happy.  We had mac and cheese and grilled cheese for the kids, and special vendor meals for our vendors.  We had tasted everything ahead of time, and were pleased that the food was as good for 46 people as it was for the 2 of us.
The drinks were spectacular. There was never a wait for food.  The staff was kind and gracious and fun- they were rocking out behind the bar as they cleaned up at the end of the night.
It was NOT a cheap wedding, it ended up costing about $220/person.  However, the good food and amazing cocktails were our top priorities, along with a really fun party atmosphere. The Place
The Bristol is an American restaurant located in Chicago’s Bucktown Neighborhood.  Reservations are a good idea as it fills up quickly.  Table seating available as well as bar.  Private events are held upstairs but I haven't been up there so I can't comment.  Very nice ambiance a little on the loud side.

The Menu/Food/Drinks - Dinner Menu
We choose monkey bread with dill butter and brussel sprouts made with duck confit, mustard-chipotle vinaigrette, cornbread crumbs for our starters.  Both were very good!  For our main courses we ordered half chicken with mustard & dill spätzle, crunchy salad, chicken jus.  This chicken was prepared excellently 5 star entree.  Our second main was a butcher steak prepared with broccoli rabe, smoked onion, mushroom powder, red wine sauce.  I found it to be flavorful but chewy.  Overall this main was a little disappointing a 3 star offering. The third main was a basic double quarter pounder burger with cheese, garlic aioli, and duck fat fries.  This main was a shocker wow what a great burger.  If there were 6 stars I it would have scored them.   Another Yelp review commented "The most underrated burger in Chicago hands down" totally agree mine burger was the best ever and the duck fat fries were delicious as well.  Dessert was snickerdoodle sundae chocolate & vanilla gelato, hazelnuts bananas, zabaglione.  It was different, fun and very good.

Drinks order were a couple smoked sicilian manhattan's which were excellent!!  We also had 2015 Smith & Perry Oregon Pinot Noir which was just ok for a Oregon Pinot Noir.

The Service/Experience/Value
Our service was very good.  Our orders were taken and delivered in a timely manner.  Our water glasses never emptied and the plates were cleaned promptly.  Overall we had a very nice experience and the prices while high were not out of line for the value presented.  I recommend you give the Bristol a try.

Overall I would reccomend this place for a quiet and luxurious night out.

Toast serves to fill a certain niche.  They only serve breakfast and lunch and while their menu is actually quite limited, they are able to squeeze a lot of quality variations out of what they serve. All of the variations of eggs benedict which I have tried are quite good, with real Hollandaise, properly poached eggs, and a good dose of protein. While the benedict dishes are good, their other eggy offerings are more creative and are packed with bold flavors. On one recent visit, I enjoyed the chorizo and eggs. While this dish was a bit a greasy, it was pure chorizo grease. Sloppy, orange tinted oil-tinged eggs. Not for the weak of stomach, but so good. The accompanying home fries can be hit or miss.

Making a home in Logan Square since late-Summer 2018 Pretty Cool Ice Cream is the brain-child of Bang Bang Pie and Biscuits founder Michael Ciapciak in conjunction with Dana Cree, the pair’s focus on frozen treats forgoing the traditional “Scoop Shop” and instead tackling Ice Cream on a stick.

Now socially distanced during COVID-19 precautions, bleacher-style seating and photogenic interior closed to the public while two young men serve guests from a small window, it is via online ordering or a menu taped to glass that selections are made, dipped versus undipped and Vegan or otherwise comprising some thirty flavors.

Certainly not the Ice Cream Truck of yesteryear, prices between $3.50 and $5.50 justified by entirely Gluten-free onsite production of each and every Bar or Pop, additional piece of mind comes from designer packaging such that the edible component of each is unexposed to both employees as well as other customers.

Not a good spot for the indecisive, but freezing each pop in such a manner that one guest can manage at least two Bars without worry of melting, this visit began with a collaborative “Piecicle” – the idea of Bang Bang’s Key Lime retooled into something of Popsicle rather than Ice Cream with recognizable tartness but generally underwhelming texture.

Improving henceforth, two Pretty Cool signatures selected in lieu of seasonal options, it might be expected that the author of “Hello My Name Is Ice Cream” would have a way with flavors, the intensity of both Horchata as well as Peanut Butter dialed way up while coatings fractured to the tooth before slowly dissipating and leaving behind the crunchy components.

I never leave reviews but have to echo what others have said on the puzzling bad service. The employees are nice enough - but somehow not a single one seems to have a clue how to efficiently make a simple bagel sandwich. Here’s how my visit went:

1. Place simple order at register - 1 bacon egg cheese sandwich on everything with pepper jack cheese, 1 bacon egg cheese sandwich on plain with cheddar cheese

2. Go to pay at register - $27. Hmm, $4.50 sandwiches and 2 bottled drinks from the cooler? Look at ticket - it has 2x brobagel club sandwiches at $8/ea. Ok - just a little mistake no big deal. They voided my initial transaction and charged me the right price.

3. After 20 mins of waiting (and not many other orders or people coming in), checked to make sure they didn’t cancel the order on the line by accident due to the initial mix up. Nope - they’re working on it, just incredibly slowly.

4. Order is ready - thankfully decided to eat there. Both sandwiches have the wrong cheese, and mine somehow has lettuce and some sort of mayo-based sauce? How? It’s a bacon egg cheese sandwich. Every employee knew of the voided transaction / initial mixup. Seemed like they started making me the wrong sandwich, realized it, and then didn’t feel like taking the time to fix it / make it the right way. Just an incredible lack of care.

5. Ask them to make me a new one - which they did without issue. Now they’ve run out of plain bagels. Ok - pumpernickel, I can see there’s 2 left. “Sorry those are reserved for another order...” at this point I’ve been in the store at least 30 mins for a simple bagel sandwich and those bagels were there the entire time. Another order? When were they planning on making that other order? Now I feel bad for me and the other pour soul who’s missing their breakfast bagels too.

It was really incredible to see 6+ employees looking like they’re trying to work but getting absolutely nothing accomplished. Honestly seemed like the whole lot of them ate a bunch of edibles before work - which who cares, as long as you can still function, but if you can’t make a bagel sandwich in a bagel shop without messing up multiple times in under 30 minutes - that’s an issue.

The reason I’m giving 2 stars instead of 5 is because they surprised us with a 24% covid surcharge! What the heck?! It’s not my fault that there’s a pandemic. It is not fair to pass on the loss of business to customers like me who are trying to support businesses like Taxim! I am a business owner too. I didn’t pass the buck to customers who are trying to support me. This practice is unconscionable! Very shady. It left a bad taste in my mouth! Won’t be coming back!

25% mandatory COVID service fee not mentioned prior to arrival. Not a good experience. Visiting from NYC. Read some great reviews about Taxim online and did some reading of their website. Came by train to Wicker Park from the city. Lackluster welcome by staff. When our menus were placed we found a note saying a ‘mandatory’ tip surcharge of 25% applies (not on their website or told to me when they confirmed my reservation by phone earlier that day). Also a ‘minimum spend’ mentioned on the menu of $45 pp.

We left before ordering and I said to the waitress on the way out I was upset because I didn’t want to be blind-sighted by an imposed charge. I was met with extreme indignation and ‘why didn’t I want people to be paid during the pandemic?’ I am a consumer who is just trying to help businesses by venturing out! We swiftly found a table at ChopShop down the street and gave them our 25% (I’ve been giving extra tip anyway during the pandemic) but the service was much better.
My top spot for Greek food. Food with real quality ingredients.  Feeling here is similar to a cafe in San Jose I liked.

Waited an hour and a half for our entree and cancelled after being told kitchen was backed up. Food that did arrive on time was descent. Will not return. Service was kind and did a good job wasn’t their fault.

Went here after a recommendation from a fellow vacationer while in Greece. Was told
This place has probably the best Greek food in Chicago. The food was good but I was not impressed. I was not blown away. The service was good and the atmosphere was better. We sat on the rooftop and enjoyed a beautiful Chicago summer evening.
Wonderful service and amazing kebab. Beautiful rooftop dining. Definitely recommended.
It was delicious. Definitely not what I expected but it was a really nice place great atmosphere. Felt very modern.

My fav spot for delicious greek food. came here on a saturday. looking forward to coming back with my relatives. the prices are fair for the quality of food. i see why this place has a lot of great reviews.

Excellent spot for quality greek food. Nice place to think about business. Fast, efficient, and courteous service. Bring your appetite because portions are generous. Feels like a place in Charlotte that I enjoyed visiting.
Amazing
greek food at this place - yummy. Very savory. Prices are reasonable.
A fav location for tasty Greek food. I wish there were more places like this around town. I will be back with my relatives.
Highly recommend the sea bass made in the traditional Greek style.
Great spot for quality greek food. Good place to hang and eat some good food. Definitely worth going back to. The bill was reasonable.

Really great take out experience. The ground lamb shoulder didn't travel the best but the smoked pork belly was beyond delicious! Price is a littler higher than some of the options around, but quality justifies the cost.
Great rooftop

We reserved a table for three and when we arrived, the hostess told us we had only an hour. The food was okay, but not the typical Greek cuisine that I was expecting. I ordered a salad and ended up with a dip and pitas. Where were the Greek olives, the feta cheese, the greens?

I ordered a martini and the glasses do not have stems. Big bummer for me! This would never happen at Greek Islands. Just saying. Plus they didn't have Absolut vodka or Bombay Sapphire gin, my favorite choices for a martini.

The lamb chops were excellent, otherwise, I wouldn't have given it a single star. A 25% gratuity was added to the check, and although this is printed on the check, this is something that should be verbalized to avoid a double tip being added. Luckily, one of the individuals in my party alerted me to remove the 20% tip that I had added, after we were told that our time was up. Four words: I won't go back.
Love this place. Amazing food and ambiance
One of my preferred locations for Greek food. the staff was friendly and observant. this place has a cool atmosphere.
Gnocchis were absolutely delicious but the wait was horrible  definitely not a good place for big groups. Perfect for a date.
Great food, drink, and atmosphere. Even though it was cold out the rooftop with space heaters was very comfortable.
greek food at this location - very good. I've had nothing but pleasant experiences here and plan to keep coming back. This place has a good atmosphere. Food is like a place in Baltimore I loved.
damn good food

Authentic, regional Greek cuisine in an upscale but comfortable setting. Best Greek food in Chicago! Order as many dishes as you can to share and take advantage of the all-Greek wine list. Taxim offers the ultimate Greek dining experience in Chicago, not like the Greektown tourist traps.

I have to say if the great Greek philosophers were to dine here they would have included the mention of Taxim in their works! Amazing food and vibe. I would recommend you to check it out and reread this review once! David and crew run the show like magnificent eleven!!
Food was super tasty along paired with great service.

Taxim is THE place for authentic Greek food. From the owner who flies to Greece on a regular basis to the taste of every dish (we’ve been there enough times to taste pretty much the whole menu), to the indoors and amazing patio, everything is to love about this place. We are now committed to go once a month because it is the only place in the city that truly makes us feel like we are back in Greece. Highly recommend!
Great food and ambiance. Everyone was kind there.

The food here was PHENOMENAL and I really wanted to order each and every item on the menu. The rooftop patio is covered so it makes for a great outdoor spot during covid yet also very comfortable temperature with the heat lamps! My favorite was the octopus, perfect flavor cooked over an oak wood flame I believe.

Giving 4 stars simply because the service was quite slow (over 2 hours to have a few small plates and a bottle of wine with a friend) and because we came quite early (6 pm reservation) on a Friday and they were already out of a lot of items. Probably all covid related so would definitely come back!!!
Go to Greek Islands instead. Lacking quality for the price. Dry meat, bland pita and food made me feel sick. Seriously regret wasting my time & money at this place.
Great atmosphere on the rooftop, but my husband and I got sick later that night.

With the small plate format you can try a lot. Main dishes seemed pricey for the size, but everything we tried was delicious. Favorites included the okra, octopus and pork belly. The wild boar reminded me of pot roast but I've never had boar before, maybe that's what it's like. A member of our group loved it, though. Cocktails were unusual and very tasty.
Great ambiance, shared plates, and an extensive wine list. Highly recommend the Lamb chops. Three small plates and one Entree was the perfect amount of food for 2 people.

Decided to give Taxim another shot after visiting just a few times over the past few years.

The good

The upstairs patio rooftop / outdoor area is nice

The Greek wine list is extensive and fairly priced and our server made a good recommendation based on our preferences.

The menu has a good collection of more well known items and some regional specialities

The brassopita was good and traditional but had more lemon or something in it than what you'd get in Greece. Fried cauliflower was tasty as well.

Otherwise

The appetizer / mezze portions can be small even for mezze and should either be larger or priced a bit better for what they are. Basic vegetable based staples and breads are cheap to produce.

The pita did not seem freshly baked which I'd expect for the price for some pita and mezze like fava or chickpeas

They were out of at least two menu items that'd I'd expect to be available

The lamb shank was tender and pretty tasty, but it was underseasoned/bland and the shank itself was small. The orzo and yogurt were also underseasoned and were a bit bland. Considering that you probably have to braise or roast a bunch of lamb shanks in advance and then reheat them, I'd expect a more flavorful sauce and for the shank and orzo to be served at a warmer temperature, as well as the plate itself.

Great server and bus staff, but the place itself was understaffed. Took 20min from when we finished our bottle of wine and food for the table to be bussed and for us to interact with the server, so we decided to not order dessert or after dinner drinks.

Overall good experience but nothing too special except for maybe the wine.
Frankly, the food is above average. I would like to give Taxim 4 stars, but the host/hostess duo downstairs is the reason for my current rating.

Awful service, terrible policies. Good food.

-25% tip automatically included - we had TERRIBLE service
-no split checks
-they demand that you spend at least $45 per person
-server insisted we buy at least 5 small plates per person (you only need two)
-they asked for a credit card to book a reservation- they will charge you $20 per head for no shows
-90 min table limit
-our food took 70 minutes to arrive
-drinks took 25 min to arrive (so we were over time)
-we had to go find our waitress for the check

Too pushy, too many terrible policies. Impossible to enjoy your meal and relax.
Nice experience

Hostess wasn’t very welcoming. Rooftop was very nice. Atmosphere was great, nice music playing and a friendly vibe with the staff. Our server Ashley was extremely nice. Food was amazing! A little overpriced menu. First time here, would definitely go back.
This place is a hidden gem. Menu is always amazing and great options for vegetarians!
a good place for a quick breakfast or lunch, but the lines can be long.  the staff are impressively efficient.
Not as good as it should be.

Really yummy yogurt and granola.  The casual atmosphere is nice and it's great when you're not in a rush.  It can get noisy and crowded that's for sure.  Service is quick and efficient.  It's a bit pricy for what you get but it's a good option if you're in the area.

Yum! Counter service brunch location can get busy, but they work through the line quickly. The simple menu makes it easy to do repeat orders for your favorites - by far the Huevos Rancheros! House-made oatmeal and the teas are outstanding. The also feature specials that change everyday. So, grab your morning paper and get a quick bite!
Huevos Rancheros are wonderful! Fantastic brunch/lunch spot, expect a wait (especially when the weather is great)!
Tasty pastry, muffings, coffee. No internet.

Counter-service Wicker Park standard brunch.  I was told to go here by multiple people and as much as I liked it i was expecting more.  There was a long wait and the meal wasn't memorable.  I would enjoy this place more if i lived closed by and could visit during non peak hours.

What a wonderful, cute place to get breakfast or lunch on the weekend :) While many reviewers on Yelp complained about the portion sizes, I did not find a problem at all with my normal size wrap. The flavor combos are amazingly well-thought out and delicious! I ordered the wrap with parmesan hummus, eggplant, feta, and pickled red onions and it was perfect! My bf got the avocado, tomato, romaine, and mustard sandwich and it was also great. I also recommend their granola bars as a tasty afternoon treat later on ;)
A good cup of coffee. Friendly staff. Nice people watching.

Besides have the best granola on the planet (guava cashew, sweetened with agave nectar), they also have great egg dishes and BLTs. Even on weekdays, this place is packed, so make sure to come early on the weekends to have a shorter wait.

Hearty breakfast granolas with fresh fruit is a great way to start the day, and we usually get it to share so we can taste more dishes! Also had some good huevos ranchero here.  Nice selection of pastries and coffee beverages makes milk and honey a nice place for afternoon business meetings.
good food, very fast service... a nice place to grab a quick bite
Best iced tea in the city, but weak coffee

This is one of my favorite brunch locations. They change up their pancake and waffle flavors weekly and sometimes have very unusual, but delicious, combinations .This also goes for their daily soups and salads, which often feature yummy things like goat cheese! You'll want to come early or on a weekday, because it fills up fast. If you are unfortunate enough to arrive when there is a long line, they have a separate cash register for take away orders, which speeds things along. This location is good for vegetarian folks, but could have more low carb or gluten free options.

Staff was rude. Food was ok but the service really bad. It was winter and cold and they wouldnt close the door. Our food got cold and the manager was rude with us. It's a shame. Food was good but they way I was treated I would never return.
best brunch place eva

Food is fantastic - a lot of healthy and fresh selections. The wait staff is very accomodating. You place your order and food is delivered to the table, but because this place is always busy, the wait staff works efficiently to reserve tables for you before placing your order.
Delicious food! Great prices. Delicious drinks.

This is my favorite weekend brunch spot. It's a cute little cafe with a great vibe and even better food. Stand bys include the orange brioche French toast, the dynamite huevos rancheros (only on weekends!), and their changing varieties of pancakes and waffles. Baked goods and pastries are also fantastic.

My absolute favorite brunch spot! The wait times at peak hours usually aren't that bad and the food is really cheap in price, and I would gladly pay double what they are charging for this food! Their signature dish, the huevos rancheros, is only available on the weekends, but it's the BEST THING EVER! You'd be a fool not to order it!

GREAT food! The huevos rancheros on the weekends are unbeatable. The thing that keeps me away is the set up of the resturant. It's always busy (I know it's in a crazy neighborhood) but you end up waiting in line right next to all of the people eating. It's kind of a hybrid between fast food and sit down, and as far as breakfast goes im not the biggest fan. I know they have their reasons for this, and they could probably defend them, but it's just not my preference.

Have stopped in a handful of times. Never had anything amazing, but it has been consistently good and it doesn't seem that there are any bad choices. Organic and fresh veggie options and a small but good beer selection helps. Typical brunch hours are very busy.

Sandwiches are awesome but the breakfast is what had me at Milk & Honey 7 out of 8 weekends this summer...the one weekend I didn't make it was because I was out of town.  Their breakfast panini is unbelievable - eggs are nice and fluffy, the tomato is juicy, and unlike other paninis that are pressed in a pool of butter, the Milk & Honey breakfast panini is perfectly pressed.  The granola is unreal and if they have the Thai Iced Tea Latte, it's definitely worth the $3.50.

This is a graet place and the food is awesome but the staff can snobby and rude. This place is such a neighborhood staple that it doesn't seem like they really care about providing good customer service to their customers. If you go and have to experience this, look out!

Milk and Honey is my favorite breakfast place. It has a relaxed vibe with delicious food and coffee. You can order inside and grab a spot either inside or outside on the shaded patio and your food is quickly brought out to you once it's freshly prepared. My personal fav is the oatmeal with milk, almonds and blueberrries!
Excellent selection and really fast service. Iced coffee comes with free refills and the special is always spot on perfect to my taste. Very affordable breakfast and lunch place for Wicker Park.
best brunch spot in wicker park!
Great Breakfast and kid friendly!!!
I wish their menu has more to offer, but what the do have is great. Their bloody mary garnish is the best! It's almost like another meal in itself. Go early as they don't have a lot of space.
Love it

Really solid food, but kind of an odd ordering process.  If you are there on the weekend you HAVE to try their Huevos Rancheros Breakfast Casserole, definitely one of the best breakfast meals I've ever had.  If you are looking for lunch, I'd recommend the crabcake sandwich (also very solid).  All things considered, this is a great spot and I'm happy to have it in my neighborhood.

Ordered the orange brioche French toast and granola pancakes, with sides of bacon and chicken sausage. Had the pumpkin coconut latte and hot chocolate to drink. Bacon tasted like bacon and hot chocolate was good. Everything else was not very special. Gave at least the 3 stars because I saw the young cook busting his behind alone squeezing out orders. Should've stayed home and just boiled an egg and had toast and jelly. First and last time at this place. Unsatisfactory breakfast.
Coffee and breakfast options.  Great mix granola available.  Orange Brioche French Toast with Toasted Almonds and Maple Syrup.  Plenty of #vegetarian sandwiches to choose.

Filled with baby strollers and booster seats, Milk & Honey's granola and pastries are worth the line. They also make tasty lunch options and have a solid black bean burger. In the summer the outdoor patio is the perfect place to people watch over a cup of joe.

Love it but note to all - MOM and KID friendly.  You will get a nice healthy - home like meal, but you will have many pregnant moms and kids ruining your zen approach to "working from home".  Especially love the egg dishes and their granola is to dye for.
A bit pricey considering you serve yourself, but then again, it's in hipsterville.
the place is just perfect.  They are a Ukrainian village must dine at.
Stopped in while in the neighborhood. Mom n Pop locally owned fast and friendly. Enjoyed my breakfast and latte

Neighborhood gem. Always a different special of the day and the dishes have a farm to table feel. Great for breakfast, brunch and lunch. As for weekends, don't even bother going after 11, it's always so packed.
Very nice, great Bloody Mary.
A super cute cafe for breakfast or brunch. The staff were super friendly, the atmosphere was relaxed and the granola was delicious.

Ordering food here can take a while - it's not full service, so you have to go up to the counter to order, which leads to a line on busy weekends. Definitely not Ideal. However, I would say it's worth the wait.

There are just a few brunch places along Division, most of them are bars, so Milk & Honey stands out as a cute, delicious option.

Prices are average for a brunch place, $10 for a meal, etc. I want to try out some of their lunch options as well as I expect they have pretty decent sandwiches & possibly some good fall soups.

This is the perfect affordable breakfast/brunch spot. The portions are hearty and they always have an interesting waffle or pancake flavor with some great coffee. While most of my visits have been for brunch don't overlook their lunch options, their sandwiches are just as good. I recommend getting their early to be seated right away if not be prepared for a wait, nothing too crazy but 30 min isn't out of the question.
The Salmon with cream cheese & bagel is delicious

Good food
.Nice Lady
Excellent breakfast burrito...very friendly staff!
Great brunch place. If only it was less popular so you wouldn't have to wait on the weekend.
Good sandwiches. Wait times can be annoying
While the sourcing of the ingredients may be honorable, the dishes could be made by a novice cook for a fraction of the price.
Amazing place !! The breakfast was so delicious, great menu ! Cozy place with a lot of daylight and very cute ambience!! And the prices for the quality is awesome ! Will definitely Come back !
counter service with an attitude
Love stopping in here for coffee and parfaits. Service could be a bit more friendly, though.
Orange brioche French toast.
Great local fresh food. Always consistent and delicious.
Love ginger peach iced tea!
Amazing coffee and food with a casual atmosphere.

I love this place so much, I go between 1-3 times per week and wish I could just about live here. Relatively limited menu but everything is excellent, can get a little crazy on weekends but they always get you seated surprisingly fast. Go on a weekday, grab a Chicago Reader and a scone/breakfast panini/coffee and enjoy.
Great service. Coffee is great. Food is made fresh to order
Amazingly good homemade pickles.
Get the granola to go; hanging around for the wait isn't really worth it otherwise, but if you don't mind, then it's a nice brunch option.
This mushroom soup is to die for! I forget how yummy this place is.

I visited on a Saturday morning the place was very crowded and a bit unorganized. It's a small place and the tables are very close together. A person in a wheelchair could get into the business, but it seems they would have a hard time getting around. Also the bathrooms small as well. The menu offers a variety of sandwiches, salads, and wraps. Specialty coffee and tea are served here as well and the fresh lemonade is refreshing.
Great coffee and hot chocolate. They have really good sandwiches a d their cocktails are around d $7! Cute place, they have a fireplace that makes your dining experience cozy.
Great menu and caring service.

Good food but confusing concept. Order at the door then sit down? I would rather just sit and get comfortable than have to stand right by the door with it hitting me in the back by other customers walking in. They might want tho reconsider the setup. The servers were nice but there certainly wasn't much time to get acquainted. I also would have tipped better but i only had a second to throw some change in a jar by the order line not even where you pay. It wasn't clear if I was supposed to leave a tip on the table either.
Customer service is great - non-dairy lattes are only okay
Always busy, staff isn't really the friendliest and food is just ok. Definitely over priced.
Good food and nice place a bit overpriced for the service that is not all there. Good location. A bit crowded at times.

It's not a large establishment and can feel real cozy on weekends.

Menu is not extensive which I appreciate. There is a fair assortment of options to keep me interested and just few enough to facilitate quick decisions.

Of course the French toast and the pancakes are fantastic.

The huevos rancheros is my favorite item. It's served in a large bowl and is piping hot. Absolutely delicious and the portion size is generous--particularly for a large man. And at $8 it's practically a steal for this area.

Coffee is standard, nothing to write home about.

Pros--I'm eating a spinach salad right now and it is fresh and flavorful. Counter transaction was very pleasant.

Cons--wish there was some silverware brought with my food. Very annoying to get your food and then go..."oh, well let me get up" (esp. considering the price of my beautiful salad).

Still give it 5 stars :-)
Everything down to the pickle spear made in house
Delicious food and low prices. We go there all the way from the downtown.
Outside seating is great if you can get a table
Delicious. Fresh.  Locally owned.  Go-to spot for breakfast, lunch and brunch.

(Translated by Google) Relaxed place to have breakfast or lunch. No Wi-Fi.

Relaxte plek om te ontbijten of te lunchen. Geen Wi-Fi.
Smoked Salmon for $7.00 and a latte were great. There was no waiting for seating. Place was clean and service was prompt. order at the counter and sit.
Great food, great service.

The food at brunch is generally really tasty. They have a great outdoor seating area that is dog-friendly and they go out of their way to get your pet some treats or water or whatever; a really nice and classy touch. My one dig on the place is that the portions are pretty small for the price. I am by no means a cheap man but I am a HUNGRY one!
Great food and service. Plenty of variety but it's crowded so make sure to get there early or be prepared for a slight wait

Love that weekend huevos rancheros!!!
Amazing food in a nice location
One of my favorite places for Sunday brunch! They have delicious food for everyone, sweet and savory ! I suggest getting there early for a seat and especially for a seat on the patio
Delicious food and good vibes!

Nice place with healthy food. I got the avocado toast and also a waffle topped with ricotta.  Very tasty.  You can buy whole boiled eggs individually which is a nice healthy snack
Only disappointing part is the cappuccino.  Mediocre to poor.
Have good vegetarian options
Quality and selection and a very relaxed atmosphere. Veg friendly, dog friendly, and they never disappoint!
Great place for breakfast. The huevos rancheros are delicious. They should have them every day but unfortunately it is served only on Saturdays and Sundays.
Great food.
Fun little cafe, quick service and delicious food. Only have visited during Renegade but always has a line (for better or worse!). Prices are a bit higher than expected but a good menu selection.
For some reason, I only end up here when I'm at a Renegade. You may know them by their own granola. Good brunch place and excellent service. Price is for the area
I love milk and honey, I'm never disappointed and I go there every other day lol
My wife and I absolutely love this place. Fast service and never a long wait. The brunch and breakfast options are extremely tasty. It was almost a weekly ritual for us to go here on weekends.

This local coffee shop and quick breakfast/lunch hybrid is always a treat. Saunter up to the bar to order your food and drinks. Curve around to the right to pay and get handed a table number. You're drinks will be called up at the bar and your food will be brought out by the staff to your table.

To try:
- Huevos Rancheros - melty goodness backed in an oversized ramekin
-  Cappuccino - just the right amount of foam
- Any seasonal baked good
-  Salad they are all fresh and delicious

One thing to note - they do get crowded and their may be a wait. For that reason it's not a sit and work kind of a place so please be sensitive to the lines.
Great little cozy cafe. Grab a seat by the fireplace and get some work done while you eat a tasty smoked salmon bagel and drink their yummy coffee.
Quirky and a bit eclectic with decidedly average food. Decent spot for brunch with besties. Would not take someone you’re trying to impress.
Great food but I found it to be chaotic at it’s peak hour
Simple food made well. Sometimes the wait is a bit much when there are many other options in the area.
Great breakfast place...a gem
Cute cafe with great healthy eats.
Owner looks like she is sucking on a lemon . Not friendly at all
Good food, somewhat unpleasant staff

One of my favorite breakfast/lunch spots in Chicago. Charming, tasty, friendly, what's not to love? Great outdoor seating for warmer weather, great fireplace for cooler weather. Just about everything on the menu is worth a taste, I'd recommend the Huervos Rancheros.
Great for breakfast or lunch

The wait here is always so long, and the girl taking the order makes the drinks before putting in the food order so the chefs can stay making it! I go back because it is convenient and the for is good. But the wait drives me crazy ever time!!!!
Great selection on the menu. Had the homemade waffles and they were delicious. Everything we ordered was good. Friendly service. Nice atmosphere.
Love their blt
Odd way to do dine in, service was not great. Food and drinks made up for it!
There sandwiches  are some of the  best i ever ate. love there shrimp &Grits are delicious

One of my favorites! The daily specials are great, but my favorite is the crab cake sandwich with a house salad on the side. Very cozy and not a long wait at all. Parking is street parking or wherever you find, but still very cute and awesome!
Perfect for a casual breakfast or quick lunch. Great food and coffee

The first breakfast/Brunch place that I went in Chicago and it still is one of my favorite. Fr9m the coffee to the plates, this is an awesome place with great service and awesome food. My favorite plate there is the Orange Brioche French Toast. They are AMAZING! If you are in Wicker Park, make sure to stop by and grab some delicious food...And yes, you are welcome!

Absolutely awesome food here! Ate here twice on a three day trip to Chicago.The Orange Brioche French Toast is amazing, and the Chorizo Chilaquiles dish is delicious. Also, they have the fluffiest eggs I've ever had in my life.
Nice place for breakfast
From their granola, to bakery items to special items like french toast, they rock it out of the park.  Love the atmosphere here.
This place has outlived so many Wicker Park sandwich shops. It's the best. Their soup rocks too.
Hands down best French toast I’ve ever had! Chicken sausages were delicious. The blood orange mimosa was okay ... but the food was delicious!

I discovered this place last week while I was walking my dog with my husband. We loved it because it was one of the only restaurants that actually had the patio opened at 10 am on a Friday. The service was amazing and everyone was helpful. The server suggested the crab cake sandwich (it was the best sandwich ever) and even suggested a chicken breast for my dog. I loved it so much that I would give it a 5 star.

The fallowing day I decided to go back for that amazing sandwich and I brought a long one of our new clients to talk about her new line of dog products. Since everything was so perfect the day before I figured why not. This time we arrived at 12pm and the patio was not all the way set up. We went inside and asked if they can set a table for us. I figured it’s 12pm on a Saturday, they should have the patio up already all the way. The lady who attended us was a older blonde lady with a pony tail and she seemed very nice at first. Once we told her that we wanted the corner table set up she automatically became very rude. She acted as if it was very hard to do. I felt insulted and  embarrassed especially infront of my client. The patio had 2 other tables being used with dogs. We wanted the table far in the corner because one of the dogs was barking very loud and we did notice  want our dogs to be a distraction. The lady really wanted us to be seated next to the loud barking dog. As a customer I expect to be treated with the up most respect. It’s really a shame because I truly love this place and it’s food. We ended up going to a patio next door and I was very unhappy because I really wanted that crab cake sandwich.

I don’t understand what her problem was, but it really changed my view on that place. I’ve never felt more disrespected in my life. I know it’s not a big deal but coming from a family that owns servers restaurants in Chicago I understand the importance of customer service.
Cute little cafe with delicious sandwiches and open patio seating.

This place was really good! I got the smoked turkey Reuben and it was amazing. It was incredibly flavorful and came with some tasty chips. The prices are very reasonable and our food came out very fast. They have plenty of seats and a nice outdoor seating area. This place was cheap, quick, and delicious and I would definitely come here again.

Chorizo Chilaquiles were delicious, just a bit of spice to them and perfect portion. Partner had the smoked salmon bagel and described it as delicious. Outside seating areas with ample spots was very nice on a warm spring morning.
Good food yes a little pricey. But overall good atmosphere.
Brunch spot that I actually enjoy- super casual and laid back, great prices and great food.
The Tex-Mex options were all very mediocre. Definitely don't come here for burritos.
This is our favorite breakfast spot in Chicago. We were in town 3 days and ate there every morning. The avacado toast was especially delicious!
The people are so nice, the food is so good, HIGHLY recommend for a quick bite that doesn't sacrifice quality.
Very tasty food but just a little bit overpriced. They have a very good selection of breakfast options
Shrimp and Grits could be hotter when they come out
Breakfast was good, service was quick.
A Wicker Park staple. You need coffee, a bagel or breakfast/brunch? They've got you covered.

My wife and I love coming here when we want a quick, light breakfast/brunch. I love their BLT. They have a good mix of breakfast items, and a lot of unique sandwiches. Patio space is great, good mix of shade areas and sunny. Seating can sometimes be tight, but most people don't spend too much time here, as the food comes out quickly.
I love this place! Great food, friendly staff, and they have outdoor seating for the summer. Wish they stayed open after 5 p.m. so I can grab a sandwich after work.
