Недільний бранч! що це таке і як це відбувається?

Вважається, що поняття «бранч» придумав сам Льюїс Керролл (англ. Lewis Carroll, справжнє ім'я Чарльз Доджсон Доджсон, або Чарльз Латуідж Доджсон, Charles Lutwidge Dodgson).
Письменник об'єднав слова breakfast і lunch і відправив лист ректору Оксфордського університету з проханням ввести в розпорядок дня brunch.
Незабаром бранч став новою традицією Оксфорда, а потім і всієї Англії.
Найчастішим місцем недільних сімейних зустрічей стають фешенебельні заклади.

У закладі погдготовка меню для бранчів займає не так багато часу три, чотири дні.
Асортимент змінюється в залежності від сезону і сезонних продуктів, а також від доступності постачальників.
На кожен бранч готується «specials» - кілька особливих страв, частіше однієї тематики.
Для таких позицій у закладу є можливість замовити продукти за пару тижнів, завчасно.
Основними стравами можуть бути цесарки з Франції, які запікалися цілком з апельсинами, розмарином і чебрецем, ростбіф, приготований при температурі 85 градусів з часником і чебрецем, а також йоркширський пудинг.

Важлива умова для бранча - це різноманітність блюд, оскільки найчастіше це сімейне проведення часу або ж в компанії друзів, і позиції повинні задовольнити вибір кожного гостя.
Строгих обмежень в асортименті немає, але обов'язкові позиції все ж регламентовані: салати, закуски, м'ясні і рибні страви і, звичайно ж, десерти, оскільки гості проводять в закладі кілька годин.
Бранч, за своєю суттю - це досить пізній сніданок, що переходить в обід.

Шеф-кухарю важливо показати свою творчу сторону, здивувати гостей, щоб у них виникло бажання спробувати всі представлені страви.
Подача і оформлення - важлива сторона презентації.

Активна підготовка до Бранчу починається за два дні.
У п'ятницю маринади, підготовка продуктів і заготовки до десертів (бісквіти, наприклад).
Основні приготування закінчуються в суботу ввечері або ж у неділю вранці.
Вранці, наприклад, випікається хліб, якого повинно бути не менше трьох видів - світлий і темний багет, багет з чорним шоколадом або сиром дор блю, чіабатта з шинкою і в'яленими томатами.

Кількість їжі в грамах або кілограмах їжі не розраховуються, оскільки це не банкет. І концепція бранча складається в безлімітному доступі до їжі і напоїв.

Some time ago while in the area running errands I stumbled upon Standard Bar & Grill. As a college football enthusiast, it instantly became a bookmark once I saw that the bar was a supporter of the LSU Tigers. At the beginning of the college football season I loved the idea of visiting the college football supportive bars because the environment is the second best thing to being at an actual sporting event. Furthermore, I visited it on New Years Day to watch the LSU Tigers vs UCF Knights.

I always visualized the inside of the bar as something on the lines of a Buffalo Wild Wings, but once I entered it, it looked like your average sports bar with many televisions inside. And in this case, it was filled with die-hard LSU fans, which I expected upon visiting.

The menu consisted of foods, such as burgers, pizza, salad, wraps, tacos, wings, chicken tenders, sandwiches and tortilla chips. There were vegan choices too! With that, the meatless sloppy joe dip was one of the items that caught my interest, which consisted of vegan meat crumbles, melted Chihuahua cheese served with garlic bread. I ended up ordering a pepperoni pizza due to it being the only thing that my appetite could handle at the time.

Considering that the bar was crowded, I did not have any expectations on receiving my food fast, but it was received in a timely manner that was not disappointing. Even though I had just a water and my food, the bartender was very attentive to not just me, but the others that sat at the bar, as well, which is something that I always admire about bartenders and servers. I cannot say much about the pepperoni pizza I ordered, but it did do its job.

Options for parking include metered parking near the bar, or either neighborhood parking which could put you further out from the bar. I ended up finding a spot near the bar paying only $4 at the meter for just 2-hours. With that, I recommend arriving to the bar early or either taking the train if you live outer neighborhood.

Overall, I had a great time at Standard Bar & Grill, and definitely would return, but that would be strictly for sporting events only. With that, I will surely be on the lookout for future LSU Tigers games, even though the bar supports all of our other Chicago sporting teams. I tend to get much rowdier watching college football versus the professional teams.

Take note of their everyday specials, which involve food, beer, cocktails, shots and wine. With all being mentioned, I hope this review assists you in any way.

The place has cleaned up (it actually has lights now!), they turned it into a full sit-down restaurant by adding a lot more tables and expanding the place. Although I laughed because that same ancient ATM that I bet hardly anyone uses is still there collecting dust along the back wall.

She took my order down and rang my up for one burrito...which I corrected her for (would I have gotten a 2 for 1 deal if I hadn't? Dangit!). They took my credit card quick and easy.

They're still huge and the restaurant threw in a ton of green pepper salsa. I dove right into these things once I got home. They were both cooked and prepared well, all the ingredients packed tightly together, nothing was sloppy. The lengua blended perfectly with the cheese, onions, lettuce, tomatoes, sour cream, guacamole, etc. Definitely will have this again on my next trip. The lomo while still good, I think they didn't make it a super burrito as it was filled with rice or its an entirely different recipe.

Whatever the case this place is going to be in my stable of restaurants. Right now it's the best burrito in my area and completely lived up to the taste I had on my mind all these years.

First, I will talk about their drinks. They have a very extensive wine list, but if you're a fan of the dirty martini like I am, that's the move for this restaurant. The blue cheese olives are hand stuffed, and they keep the vermouth pour to a minimum.

You can't go wrong with escargot, but they do it the best. Of course, their charcuterie never disappoints, either. Over time, I've gotten the steak frites (au poivre and maitre d), the salmon, and the steak tartare, and I've always been extremely satisfied. As for the dessert, I recommend the creme brulee.

The service at Le Bouchon is very helpful and quick, which is a great plus. One thing to note is that the restaurant is quite small, so you'll need to book a reservation. Also, they do try to fit a lot of people in there, so it is very cramped (like need to move your table so you can get out and go to the bathroom type of cramped).

If you're a fan of French food and you're in Chicago, you'll need to check Le Bouchon out.

I'm sorry. I really wanted to love this place, but we had an awful takeout experience. We had the NYE takeout meal for two, and with wine and tip ran just north of $300. It comprised seven very underwhelming dishes. Frankly, we would have been much happier with fast food.
Gougeres were good. I would not order again but for one of many courses, it worked
Oysters: absolutely delicious - the truffle butter was great
Foie Gras: portion was too much, and they didn't provide the brioche to offset the overwhelming flavor
Lobster pot pie: good flavor but overly soupy. Probably should've baked longer than 25 mins? The directions weren't very detailed.
Duck confit: good but besides the potatoes was very small portion for two. Also excessive amount of duck sauce and then barely any salad. We literally had two bites each of both the duck and the salad. Portions were just completely off here which was very disappointing.
Panna Cotta: before this dish, I was going to leave a 3/5 star review. But this was inedible. Literally tasted like spoiled cream cheese even though we refrigerated it for the entire three hours it was in our possession. I almost spat it back out. My girlfriend refused to eat it as well after simply licking the back of her spoon. I questioned if this was even the panna cotta because I doubted that this could possibly be the course, but no, I was correct and it was one of the worst things I've ever put in my mouth.
Opera cake: very good. Had to eat in intervals given how strong the flavors were, but enjoyed very much.
Red wine: great pick, very light. We both enjoyed.
I'd really like to give this place a better review, but the portions and taste just absolutely disappointed,  especially given the cost. We could've had takeout nearly anywhere in the city for a comparable or lower price. We'll laugh this one off as an appropriate end to 2020, but at least some of the dishes were good.
Only uploading a picture of the salad to emphasize there were about 8 pieces of lettuce to be split between two people. Either create a garnish or do nothing. Really made an effort to support a local small business and have rarely been more disappointed.
french food, very satisfying. Staff treated us so kindly. The bill was fair I would say.

Other than that, I had no problems finding a tasty beer to wash down my burger and I do believe I would recommend The Grafton for your burger needs when Kuma's just isn't an option.

In those restaurants (or even in a not so wonderful one), a manager would have been over immediately if a guest had been served a bug in the drink or an inedible dessert. We never saw the manager. The biggest reason they lose a point in decor is that, as my girlfriend aptly noted, they had Pandora playing in the background (complete with commercial breaks) on a Katy Perry station or something. Kind of ruined the vibe they had going...

The food was good; I was actually most impressed with their pasta-esque bread. For the price, the rest of the food was average at best. That's not to say that it wasn't good, but simply that you're paying a lot for the meal and I've definitely had better at that price point. Overall, I'm not quite sure I would give this my stamp of approval; I personally wouldn't spend that much money on a dinner here again, but it was a nice dining experience.
The ambiance and great service adds to the amazing food that sets this cozy place over the top. Not to mention the candle lit table that makes this spot a must for romantic dates.

There are at 20+ Italian restaurants I would recommend over this one in Chicago!

Last Sunday was my first visit to Merlo on Maple and will certainly not be my last.  A deeply satisfying dining experience.  The food was true Northern Italy fare prepared impeccably. I can't tolerate the cacophony so common in restaurants today and there is none of that here, you can carry on conversation at a normal volume.  Most rewarding, 5 stars are not enough

My girlfriend and I visited Merlo this past weekend, and we were both very impressed. The restaurant is housed in an impressive brownstone. We were greeted by a pleasant hostess as soon as we arrived and were taken to our table. Great ambiance including fresh flowers on candlelit tables. We started off with a couple of delicious appetizers that our server had suggested, then we shared two handmade fresh pastas that were made a la minute ( incredible ). For main course my girlfriend had a fillet of Halibut that was quite possibly the freshest piece of fish we have had in Chicago, and I had the Osso Bucco that was out of this world good. Service was knowledgeable, friendly, and fun. We will definitely be going back soon with more friends.

My husband and I went here last night for date night.  We try to make a point when white truffles are in season to have a really tasty meal.  So when planning our evening we sought out a restaurant with white truffles on the menu.  Merlo on Maple was a great choice.  Many places we have been have 1 or 2 dishes with white truffles; however, Merlo on Maple offered an entire white truffle menu with 5-6 dishes.

Upon arrival we were greeted by the hostess and immediately taken to our table.  We had the pleasure of having Harmony as our waitress.  She was such a pleasure and eager to please.  We were also on a time constraint because we had to be at a show by 8 p.m.  The atmosphere was pretty standard for a nice restaurant downtown.  Dim lighting and candle light at the table.

Harmony started us off by recommending the best bottle of wine I have had in a long time.  A Barolo from Italy that was simply amazing.  First course we ordered the Burrata Cheese which was one of the best Burrata i've had in a long time.  I got the Beef Capriccio and my husband got the Tuna Tartar both were equally mouth watering.  Then the main course my husband got the white truffle risotto and I got the 50 egg yolks pasta.  The chef did not disappoint.  The fragrance of the white truffles alone was mouth watering.  We both have a fair amount of truffles as well.  All in all this was a great meal.  Harmony did amazing with timing and made sure we were out of there by 7:30 sharp.  I would highly recommend this place for a romantic evening for 2.

Merlo Maple is a charming restaurant fit for any occasion. I dined at Merlo with my boyfriend and we loved our experience. I would definitely dine at Merlo again because of their delicious food, service, and you can't beat the ambiance. I signed up to be on their email list to hear about all their specials because their specials are always changing and my boyfriend and I love truffles. Definitely a must try restaurant.

When we arrived, they placed us at a table that was not romantic at all.   It was quiet and uncomfortable.  I asked for a table in the front room where you have a view of outside and they said everyone had assigned seating and they are fully booked.  I found this interesting considering I booked over a month out and probably way earlier than half of the people dining there.

We ordered appetizers, a salad, and main dishes.  The proportions were extremely small and for a beautiful little Italian restaurant - I had very high expectations for the food.  Nothing was really the right temperature or tasted good - if we had to compare the food to something we decided banquet hall food - which is never a great experience.

My boyfriend also ordered a old fashion drink because he loves whiskey.   They mentioned they have a full bar and make great drinks - he said it was probably the worst drink he ever had which is not good considering how many of these he has had in his lifetime.

Lastly, when we were walking out and leaving after skipping dessert and just wanted to leave - we figured at least one of the hostess' would say thank you for coming in.  She chased us out the front door not to say thank you - but for some reason ask what our name was under our reservation in open table to she could record it.

Overall, it was an extremely disappointing experience that I had scheduled for over a month in advance.   I would not recommend or return to this restaurant.

In a posh Chicago neighborhood, chockablock with haute couture, sits this modest pancake house that looks to have last been remodeled 35 years ago.  The line for a Sunday breakfast spills out the door, and we are told that the wait will be about 15 minutes, which I find hard to believe.  Incredibly, we're led to our table exactly 15 minutes later, seated by the window.  The tables are worn, homey butcher block, where you can see the imprint of every glass of water ever placed on it.  There are stained glass panels, and vintage sheet music hung on the walls.  The joint is buzzing with a hundred conversations, and I feel at home as an out-of-towner, soon to be headed to the airport to reluctantly leave Chicago.  I order a simple meal of over easy eggs, and Canadian bacon (Weight Watchers friendly), and my meal arrives promptly, complete with three 4" pancakes (oh, the temptation!).  It was a short and joyous sendoff from The Windy City.

While I was in Chicago visiting a friend we were trying to decide what to do for lunch. Subway came up as an option and I mentioned maybe we try something unique to Chicago since I can get Subway back home anytime. She suggested Panes and I was good with that, so we drove over there and parked on the street.
I decided I wanted a Turkey Club and ordered and just as I was getting out my credit card, the woman working said they don't take credit, it was cash or check only. Being that I didn't have any cash on me, my friend picked up my tab.
I ordered the turkey club, with no cheese and a water. I asked for a pickle, because I'm pregnant and really, what pregnant woman doesn't love pickles? LOL I mean, come on! But they didn't have pickles, so, better luck next time. The sandwich comes with a side of potato chips (which to me, tasted like Lays). I asked for water and she pointed me to this little side bar, that had a set up for old fashioned plastic glasses and a little freezer bucket for ice and a special little spout, just for water. It was quite cute. After my friend finished ordering and paying, they gave her a number to put on a stand when we chose a table.
I went and got water and sat down. The cafe itself is cute and small. It has very tall ceilings and an open feel. It has about 12 tables inside, maybe 15 at most and a seating area outside as well. After I sat down, I noticed an ATM, in case you don't have cash.
They brought our food out within 5 minutes of sitting down and everything looked great. Once I took one bite of my sandwich I realized I had been there before. I asked my friend if her brother lived near there and she said he did, about a block away (at one time, he's since moved) and I asked if she had brought me there before and she remembered a time when we had been there. How funny! Something as simple as a turkey sandwich, but I remembered it from my past, and about 13 years ago too I might add. So if that says anything about the flavor. It definitely stands out.
We spent some time reminiscing from that visit so many years ago and I noticed she didn't order a sandwich, but she had what appeared to be eggs. I asked what it was and she told me Chilaquiles Verdes. Which I had never heard of before. However, my well traveled friend, who recently spent close to a year in Mexico, knew exactly what they were and explained the ingredients to me. Crispy tortilla strips, simmered in fresh green tomatillo sauce, shredded chicken breast, scrambled eggs and potatoes. She offered a bite to me and I gave it a try. It was pretty good, with a little spicy kick to it.
After we were done eating we bussed our own table and put our stuff in the designated area. It was good, so good, I remembered it from so many years ago. What a nice blast from my past. I'd recommend giving it a try if you're in the area, it's a quaint little cafe.

They brew Intelligentsia here, so it's a great treat to ease the wait, which can exceed an hour or more on the weekends. Once you're seated, you're given a bite of their coffee cake, which is a moist delicious cinnamon striped cake that goes perfectly with the coffee (and they make sure you're always with a full cup). All of the service here is top notch, the bus boys are quick and efficient, and the waiters are always bubbly, friendly, and helpful. I've had an assortment of their offerings, from omelettes to their signature dishes, and nothing has fallen short. Everything is freshly made and in season, and the portion sizes are more than generous. Nearly every entree comes with a fresh fruit cup and a side of toast and/or hash browns. I always want to branch out to other brunch places, but Tweet manages to do everything perfectly!

So my friend and I decide to have brunch.  She suggests Tweet, she said she had heard good things. We get there and there's a wait, but figure it's a Sunday in Chicago and that's to be expected.  They take our names to their list and send us over to a busy bar section to wait.

We drink bloody marys and wait for about an hour and a half.  They finally call our names and we were seated. As soon as we're in our seats our waiter is there to take our order.  The rest of the meal was rushed.  The food came lightning fast and then as soon as we even looked like we were going to put our forks down,  he was there to almost remove our plates at last bite.  That was the only other time we saw him.  He never inquired about our meal once. He wrote the check out at the table and left it in the middle of the table.  He told us to check out up front when WE WE'RE READY.

We both still had coffee to finish, so we continue our conversation when the hostess comes to our table to tell us she "can make change for us" whenever were ready...odd considering we were just told to pay at the front and we never asked for change. She comes back after 5 mins and this time says she'll "be happy to settle our bill" WHEN WE'RE READY.  We both nod and give a confusing smile.

As soon as she leaves a bust boy comes over, he removes a napkin,  a glass and asked if we needed anything else.  My friend asks for a coffee refill and he awkwardly nods and I watch as he walks over to the guy that was calling names who is now looking right at me and shaking his head no that we can not have more coffee.  (Supposedly,  they have bottomless coffee,  though we were never asked if we wanted more coffee).  He walks up to our table and says to us "if you girls want to drink coffee and talk,  you can do that all day at the bar, but not here". I couldn't believe it. It was so rude, even the people next to us noticed and commented.  When I  commented on his rudeness he got huffy and walked away.  We had only actually been seated for about 20 mins after waiting an hour and a half.

Needless to say,  weekend brunch is busy, but that is no excuse to treat customers like they're doing something wrong by wanted to have a nice meal, conversation,  and finish their coffee!
